Caecilian.Name: Sumatran Striped Caecilian
Caecilian.Description: These legless amphibians can be easily mistakened for worms or snakes with their elongated bodies and smooth skin. They have small eyes covered by a layer of skin. This species has a yellow stripe running down both sides of its body.
Caecilian.Habitat: Burrows in the ground and is elusive. Rarely encountered except after a heavy rainfall or in areas of recently disturbed soil

Frog.Name: Crab-eating Frog
Frog.Description: As its name suggests, this species is known to prey on crabs  found swampland and mangroves. Its skin is grey or brown with irregular black markings, and short low ridges. This species is also found in fields and disturbed forests. It is the only known amphibian that can tolerate salt water for short periods.
Frog.Habitat: occurs in a range of habitats including coastal scrub, marshes, disturbed forests and mangroves

Frog.Name: Field Frog
Frog.Description: This common frog has mottled green and brown skin with irregular black markings, and faint yellowish oblique strip on its side. It has short raised skin ridges along its back.
Frog.Habitat: Nocturnal and dwells in rice paddies, forest clearings, parks and gardens

Frog.Name: Golden-eared Rough-sided Frog
Frog.Description: One obvious characteristic of this species is its large  tympanum (eardrum) which has a yellowish spot in the middle.
Frog.Habitat: Found close to forest streams and swamPS.jpg in lowland primary and disturbed secondary forests.

Frog.Name: Common Greenback
Frog.Description: With its bright green back and distinct white stripes on either side of its back, as well as its white upper lip, this species is easily recognisable.
Frog.Habitat: Often seen clinging to shrubs, or in puddles of water or by small streams.

Frog.Name: Copper-cheeked Frog
Frog.Description: This rather slender bright green to brownish or yellowish-green frog gets its name from its copper-coloured tympanum (eardrum), and can be found in forest streams.
Frog.Habitat: Occurs in shallow streams in lowland primary forest, adjacent secondary forest and freshwater swamp forest. Adults tend to perch low on streamside branches or fallen forest debris.

Frog.Name: Masked Rough-sided Frog
Frog.Description: This leaf-litter dwelling frog has a dark tympanum (eardrum), a brown back with blackish markings and a pale underside.
Frog.Habitat: Occurs in freshwater swamp forests in Singapore.

Frog.Name: Banded Bull Frog
Frog.Description: This frog can be easily recognised by its round and stocky body, small head, and broad orange bands on both sides of its back. Common in disturbed habitats.
Frog.Habitat: A highly adaptable species able to survive in disturbed habitat including flooded grassland, roadside puddles and urban storm drains. Hides in holes in the ground, under leaf litter or in cracks of walls

Frog.Name: Black-eyed Litter Frog
Frog.Description: So named for their large black eyes, this small frog has a grey to brown mottled pattern on its back. It's limbs are short and slender, and its call is a loud rapid rattle..
Frog.Habitat: Dwells amongst the leaf litter of primary and mature secondary rainforests. Breeds in shallow water streams.

Frog.Name: Malayan Giant Frog
Frog.Description: This large frog which grows up to 26 cm is mainly found in forests  and forest edges. Its grey, brown or greenish skin is warty when young, but becomes smooth as an adult. Its body is robust and hind legs muscular.
Frog.Habitat: Mainly found in the forest, but at night, it can be found in puddles or wet grass in forest clearings.

Frog.Name: Malesian Frog
Frog.Description: This nocturnal frog can be recognised by the dark patch on its tympanum (eardrum) and skin folds on its back. It can be distinguished from similar species by the 'W'-shaped fold of skin behind its head.
Frog.Habitat: A nocturnal species mainly found in the forest, but may venture into clearings.

Frog.Name: Masked Swamp Frog
Frog.Description: A freshwater swamp forest specialist, the Masked Swamp Frog has uniformly brown skin on its back, and a characterstic dark stripe running from its snout through its eye.
Frog.Habitat: An elusive species that lives in acidic freshwater swamp forests

Frog.Name: Rhinoceros Frog
Frog.Description: A small species that has a distinct stocky body and large head. It has several low ridges on its back. The male has a bony protrusion at the top of its head.
Frog.Habitat: Dwells in shallow, forest streams. It inhabits primary and secondary forests up to 1200 m elevation.

Frog.Name: American Bullfrog
Frog.Description: First introduced into and bred in Singapore for food, many have be released into the wild as part of religious merit-making offerings. This frog is greenish brown with a green head, and has a large tympanium.
Frog.Habitat: Found in ponds and reservoirs , where it is released for religious reasons.

Frog.Name: Malayan Horned Frog
Frog.Description: A rare species found in the forest, this mottled brown frog has distinct horn-like protrusions above its eyes and a wide mouth. It is often mistaken for leaf litter on the forest floor. Its call is a distinct metallic honk.
Frog.Habitat: This mimic of tree litter can be found on the forest floor.

Frog.Name: Painted Chorus Frog
Frog.Description: The tiny Painted Chorus Frog is a small species that has a characteristic hourglass pattern on its back.
Frog.Habitat: Inhabits leaf litter and grassy areas in secondary forest, rural areas, parks and gardens. Can sometimes be found clinging to walls, tree trunks or low vegetation.

Frog.Name: Dark-sided Chorus Frog
Frog.Description: This tiny species has a flat brown back that helPS.jpg keep it out of sight in leaf-litter. As its name suggests, this frog has a thick black stripe along each side of its head and body.
Frog.Habitat: Lives close to small puddles and ponds in rural areas and secondary forest, where it hides in the grass and under leaf litter.

Frog.Name: Manthey's Chorus Frog
Frog.Description: This small frog has a triangular body shape with a small pointed head, brown mottled skin on its back which gets paler on its side, and black spots on its liPS.jpg.
Frog.Habitat: Lives on the forest floor of damp, lowland rainforest. Tends to hide itself under leaf litter but occasionally visible on low vegetation.

Frog.Name: Spotted Tree Frog
Frog.Description: A small but striking frog with orange or brown skin and small white spots on its back, and pale undersides.
Frog.Habitat: Occurs mainly in primary forest, in low vegetation. Its eggs can be found in tree cavities.

Frog.Name: Yellow-bellied Puddle Frog
Frog.Description: So named for its yellow belly, this forest species thrives in our forest streams, and is often well camouflaged by its grey-brown mottled skin. Often seen in shallow streams with its relatively small head protruding above the water surface.
Frog.Habitat: Occurs mainly in small streams and gullies in lowland primary and secondary forests. Can be spotted sitting in shallow water with its head emerged.

Frog.Name: Four-lined Tree Frog
Frog.Description: This slender species has a brown to yellow-brown back, often with four distinct lines from which it derives its common name. In some individuals, these stripes are absent. Common in disturbed habitats.
Frog.Habitat: Inhabits disturbed forests, scrubland, parks and gardens. May be spotted a few feet from the ground clinging on to small stems, or in puddles on wet ground.

Frog.Name: Blue-legged Tree Frog
Frog.Description: A small brown or beige frog with a slender body and legs. It also has large eyes with a white patches underneath.
Frog.Habitat: An elusive species that dwells in moist lowland rainforest and freshwater swamp forest where it lives alongside streamside vegetation. Stays hidden amongst leaf clumPS.jpg or tree crevices in the day, but emerges to the upperside of large leaves at night.

Frog.Name: Thorny Tree Frog
Frog.Description: A very rare species in Singapore that can be very well camouflaged by its green-brown and bumpy skin.
Frog.Habitat: Occurs in lowland rainforest. Eggs may be found above water-filled cavities in trees.

Frog.Name: Günther’s Frog
Frog.Description: This large frog is known from East Asia, and can be identified by its pale brown back, darker brown bands along the sides of its body, and a pale outline around its tympanum (eardrum).
Frog.Habitat: Typically found in open swampy habitats and agricultural areas. Have been found in ponds in Singapore.

Frog.Name: Lim's Black-spotted Sticky Frog
Frog.Description: This nocturnal frog has a distinct flat and triangular body with a brown/orange back skin separated from its sides by a thin white stripe. It camouflages itself well in the forest leaf-litter.
Frog.Habitat: Solitary and nocturnal, this species is primarily found in leaf litter on the forest floor.

Toad.Name: Asian Toad
Toad.Description: This common species can often be heard calling after a rainy day. It has warty grey-green skin and has a blackish raised ridge behind each eye (paratoid glands).
Toad.Habitat: found on grass lawns at night, on patHS.jpg and roads and concretised drains

Toad.Name: Four-ridged Toad
Toad.Description: Commonly found in swampy forests, this toad species can be recognised by its uniform orange-brown distinctly warty skin, four low ridges on top of  its head and dual-syllabic call.
Toad.Habitat: Occupies leaf litter of primary and secondary lowland forest. However it can be found in heavily modified habitats such as plantations.

Toad.Name: Saint Andrew's Cross Toadlet
Toad.Description: This rare species inhabits primary forests. Adults of this tiny species measures just 25mm, and are named for the cross-shaped pattern of bands on their backs. Their backs are mottled brown, with several orange or yellow spots.
Toad.Habitat: Largely confined to lowland primary forest. Eggs are laid in small accumulations of water in the crooks of trees.

Apidae.Name: Black Dwarf Honey Bee
Apidae.Description: Small, brown to black bee with pale abdominal bands. Hind legs broad and flattened.

Apidae.Name: Red Dwarf Honey Bee
Apidae.Description: Small bee with a grey thorax, orange and black abdomen, and pale abdominal bands. Hind legs broad and flattened.

Apidae.Name: Asian Honey Bee
Apidae.Description:
Medium-sized orange bee with a brown thorax and dark brown abdominal bands. Hind legs broad and flattened. 

Males (known as drones) are entirely black and have large eyes that converge on top.

Apidae.Name: Giant Honey Bee
Apidae.Description: Large bee with a black head and thorax and dark wings. Its abdomen is orange and black with pale abdominal bands. Hind legs broad and flattened.

Apidae.Name: Valdez's Stingless Bee
Apidae.Description: Tiny bee with a grey to black thorax and chestnut brown abdomen. Hind legs broad and flattened. Often hovers in flight.
Apidae.Nesting: Nests within small hollows in trees and other structures using plant resin and beeswax.

Apidae.Name: Gold-margined Stingless Bee
Apidae.Description: Tiny bee with yellow hairs lining a grey thorax. Hind legs broad and flattened. Has a hovering flight pattern.
Apidae.Nesting: Nests within small hollows in trees and other structures using plant resin and beeswax.

Apidae.Name: White-cheeked Carpenter Bee
Apidae.Description:
Large bee with a yellow thorax and black abdomen. Its wings have purple iridescence. Unlike the similar Yellow-and-black Carpenter Bee (X. flavonigrescens), the sides of its face have white hairs and the first segment of its abdomen does not have yellow hairs. 

Males are entirely covered with yellow hair.

Apidae.Name: Cerulean Carpenter Bee
Apidae.Description: A large bee with a bright blue thorax and black abdomen. Its wings have a bluish iridescence.

Apidae.Name: Sunda Blue-Banded Digger Bee
Apidae.Description: Large bee with a bright blue thorax and black abdomen. Its wings have a bluish iridescence.

Apidae.Name: Himalayan Cloak-and-Dagger Bee
Apidae.Description: Medium-sized bee with a pale blue body with distinct black markings. This bee has a cuckoo lifestyle.
Apidae.Nesting: Lays in eggs in the nest of digger bees.

Apidae.Name: Notch-toothed Stingless Bee
Apidae.Description: Small black bee with dark. Hind legs broad and flattened. Has a hovering flight pattern.
Apidae.Nesting: Nests within small hollows in trees and other structures using plant resin and beeswax.

Apidae.Name: Milky-tipped Stingless Bee
Apidae.Description: Small brown bee with white-tipped wings. Hind legs broad and flattened. Has a hovering flight pattern.
Apidae.Nesting: Nests within small hollows in trees and other structures using plant resin and beeswax.

Apidae.Name: Companion Small Carpenter Bee
Apidae.Description: A small black and yellow bee. Antennal scapes are entirely black. Marking on the first abdominal segment is a yellow band with two black spots.

Apidae.Name: Emerald Small Carpenter Bee
Apidae.Description: A small, cylindrical bee with a bright metallic green appearance. Its integument is heavily pitted.

Apidae.Name: Puang Reed Bee
Apidae.Description: A tiny, slender black bee. Its face has a pale patch, the shape of a slender inverted triangle. It carries pollen using white hairs on its hind legs.

Apidae.Name: Yellow-and-black Carpenter Bee
Apidae.Description: Large bee with a yellow thorax and black abdomen. Its wings have blueish green iridescence. Unlike the similar White-cheeked Carpenter Bee (X. aestuans), the sides of its face lacks white hairs and the first segment of its abdomen has sparse yellow hairs.

Apidae.Name: Island Forest-Digger Bee
Apidae.Description: Medium-sized bee covered with orange hairs. Its face is yellow with brown markings. It is larger than the Sunda Blue-Banded Digger Bee (Amegilla andrewsi).

Apidae.Name: Lieftinck’s Small Carpenter Bee
Apidae.Description: Small black and yellow bee. Antennal scapes are partially yellow. Marking on the first abdominal segment is a yellow band with two black spots.

Apidae.Name: Broad-handed Carpenter Bee
Apidae.Description:
A very large, black bee. Its wings have bright purple and green iridescence. Females tend to visit large open flowers. 

Males possess white feather-like front legs, and tend to perch on structures.

Apidae.Name: Black-sided Small Carpenter Bee
Apidae.Description: A small black and yellow bee. Antennal scapes are entirely black. Marking on the first abdominal segment is a yellow band with two black spots.

Apidae.Name: One-spotted Small Carpenter Bee
Apidae.Description: A small, cylindrical bee with a metallic purple appearance. Its integument is heavily pitted.

Colletidae.Name: Penang Masked Bee
Colletidae.Description: A tiny black bee with yellow legs and facial markings.

Halictidae.Name: Striped Nomia
Halictidae.Description: A medium-sized bee with a black thorax and iridescent abdominal bands. Hairs on the head and body are mostly yellow.

Halictidae.Name: Wandering Combed-Sweat Bee
Halictidae.Description: Tiny bee with grey body and white abdominal banding.

Halictidae.Name: Palm Plume-vented Bee
Halictidae.Description: Small metallic green bee with pollen-collecting hairs on its legs an underneath the abdomen. Often found visiting the inflorescences of palms.

Halictidae.Name: Red-waisted Grass-Nomia
Halictidae.Description: A tiny bee. Females are orange with yellow abdominal bands. Males are slender and have a red first abdominal segment.  Females collect pollen strictly from grasses.

Halictidae.Name: Singapore Plume-vented Bee
Halictidae.Description: Tiny bee with dark, metallic green integument. Possesses pollen-collecting hairs on legs and underneath the abdomen. Often found visiting the inflorescences of palms. Smaller than the Palm Plume-vented Bee (L. adonidiae)

Halictidae.Name: White Combed-Sweat Bee
Halictidae.Description: A small bee with black body and white abdominal banding. Larger than the Wandering Combed-Sweat Bee.

Halictidae.Name: Black-waisted Pronged-Nomia
Halictidae.Description: Medium-sized bee with a grey thorax and iridescent bands on all abdominal segments except the first. Hairs on the head and body are mostly white or grey.

Megachilidae.Name: Broad-headed Leafcutter Bee
Megachilidae.Description: Medium-sized bee covered with orange to reddish hairs and black abdominal banding. Possesses yellow pollen-collecting hairs underneath the abdomen.
Megachilidae.Nesting: Nests in pre-existing cavities using cut pieces of leaves.

Megachilidae.Name: Disjunct Resin Bee
Megachilidae.Description: Medium-sized, slender bee with a black body except for patches of white hairs behind its thorax. Possesses black pollen-collecting hairs underneath the abdomen.
Megachilidae.Nesting: Nests in pre-existing cavities using plant resin.

Megachilidae.Name: Shadow-winged Resin Bee
Megachilidae.Description: A small to medium-sized, slender bee with a thorax covered with orange hairs. Its wings are dark purple. Possesses yellow pollen-collecting hairs underneath the abdomen.
Megachilidae.Nesting: Nests in pre-existing cavities using plant resin.

Megachilidae.Name: Dimorphic Leafcutter Bee
Megachilidae.Description: Medium-sized bee with a black body except for patches of white hairs behind its thorax. Easily distinguished from the Disjunct Resin Bee (M. disjuncta) in having red pollen-collecting hairs underneath the abdomen.
Megachilidae.Nesting: Nests in pre-existing cavities using cut pieces of leaves.

Megachilidae.Name: Orange-bellied Leafcutter Bee
Megachilidae.Description: A small bee. Females are dark grey with pale abdominal bands. Possesses pollen-collecting hairs underneath the abdomen that are partially orange and white. Males are covered with yellow to brown hairs.
Megachilidae.Nesting: Nests in the soil using cut pieces of leaves.

Megachilidae.Name: Orange-winged Resin Bee
Megachilidae.Description: A medium-sized to large, slender bee with a black body and orange wings.
Megachilidae.Nesting: Nests in pre-existing cavities using plant resin.

Megachilidae.Name: Confusing Sharp-tailed Bee
Megachilidae.Description: A small cuckoo bee with a grey body and white abdominal bands. Females have an abdomen that constricts to a sharp point. Males have spines at the tip of the abdomen.
Megachilidae.Nesting: Lays eggs in the nests of leafcutter bees.

Megachilidae.Name: Sunda Chilli-tail Bee
Megachilidae.Description: A small to medium-sized, stocky bee with a grey head and thorax, and bright red abdomen. It has a cuckoo lifestyle.
Megachilidae.Nesting: Lays eggs in the nests of resin bees.

Asian Barbets.Name: Lineated Barbet
Asian Barbets.Description: The head, nape and breast of this bird are white with brown streaks, and has green wings, back and tail, and a pink bill. It has also has a distinct yellow eye-ring.

Asian Barbets.Name: Red-crowned Barbet
Asian Barbets.Description: This striking bird has a distinctly colourful head - with a red crown and a blue eyebrow and throat.

Asian Barbets.Name: Coppersmith Barbet
Asian Barbets.Description: This small species has a red forehead and a black and yellow mask. It also has a distinct red and yellow patch on its throat.

Australasian Warblers.Name: Golden-bellied Gerygone
Australasian Warblers.Description: This tiny songbird has a brown head and upperparts and yellow underparts.

Babblers.Name: Moustached Babbler
Babblers.Description: This babbler is moustached, from which its common name is derived. It can also be recognised by its red eyes. Tail is strongly rufous.

Babblers.Name: Chestnut-winged Babbler
Babblers.Description: An easily identifiable babbler with chestnut upperparts, a grey head and breast, blue eye-ring and pale belly.

Babblers.Name: Pin-striped Tit-Babbler
Babblers.Description: This babbler has characteristic fine black streaks on its throat and breast, yellowish underparts and brown upperparts.

Barn Owls.Name: Eastern Barn Owl
Barn Owls.Description: Distinctive owl identified by its pale white and brown plumage and heart-shaped face.

Bee-eaters.Name: Blue-throated Bee-Eater
Bee-eaters.Description: While similar to the blue-tailed bee eater, this species can be distinguished by its brown head and bright blue throat.

Bee-eaters.Name: Blue-tailed Bee-Eater
Bee-eaters.Description: While similar to the blue-throated bee eater, this species can be distinguished by its olive head and yellow-brown throat.

Boobies.Name: Red-footed Booby
Boobies.Description: This large seabird has red legs, a blue bill, pinkish facial skin and a mostly white plumage and tail. Juveniles have pale brown plumage.

Boobies.Name: Brown Booby
Boobies.Description: This booby has a chocolate-brown head, upperparts and upper breast, while its belly is white. It has bluish facial skin and pale green bill and feet.

Bulbuls.Name: Straw-headed Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: With its distinct call, this shy songbird is heard more often than it is seen. It has a brown streaked body, olive green wings, straw-coloured crown, black eyebrow and moustache.

Bulbuls.Name: Black-and-white Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: This bulbul is completely black aside from a white wing patch.

Bulbuls.Name: Black-headed Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: This bulbul is easily recognisable with its yellow plumage, black head and blue eyes.

Bulbuls.Name: Red-whiskered Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: This bird has a striking black crest, red eye-patch and vent. Has white cheeks and underparts and partial blackish-brown necklace.

Bulbuls.Name: Sooty-headed Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: Similar plumage to the Yellow-vented Bulbul but has a prominent black head and either a red or orange vent.

Bulbuls.Name: Yellow-vented Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: A common bird with brown upperparts, pale underparts, a black lore and a bright yellow vent.

Bulbuls.Name: Olive-winged Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: This is a drab olive brown bird with red eyes and greenish-yellow tinged wings.

Bulbuls.Name: Cream-vented Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: A generally brown bird with paler undersides that can be recognised by its white eye.

Bulbuls.Name: Asian Red-eyed Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: Similar to the Cream-vented Bulbul but has red eyes. Head and upperparts are uniformly brown.

Bulbuls.Name: Buff-vented Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: Can be identified by its small crest and dark eyestripe.

Bulbuls.Name: Streaked Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: This species has dull olive-green upperparts with grey throat and breast that is streaked white. Has a white belly.

Bulbuls.Name: Black-crested Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: Similar plumage to the Black-headed Bulbul but has a prominent black crest.

Bulbuls.Name: Cinereous Bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: This bulbul has ashy brown upperparts, white underparts and a small crest .Has a prominent white throat that is often puffed out.

Buttonquails.Name: Barred Buttonquail
Buttonquails.Description: As its name suggests, the barred buttonquail has distinct barring on most of its upperparts. Females have a black throat, while males do not.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Black-naped Monarch
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Males have mostly blue plummage with diagnostic black necklace and nape. Females mostly grey-brown on upperparts and underparts with blue restricted to the head.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: White-throated Rock Thrush
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Males of this species have a blue crown and orangey-red underparts. Females are brown above and white below and heavily scaled throughout. White throat patch visible in both sexes

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Grey-streaked Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: This small flycatcher has grey-brown upperparts and white underparts which are heavily streaked throughout.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Dark-sided Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Simiar to Asian Brown Flycatcher, but has more prominent streaked underparts, smaller bill and lacks broad white lores.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Brown-streaked Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Similar to Asian Brown, but with richer brown upperparts and faint brown streaks on underparts.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Ferruginous Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: As its common name suggests, the Ferruginous Flycatcher has a rusty-orange pluamge with a grey head.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Yellow-rumped Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Males have black upperparts with a white eyestripe and yellow underparts, while females have brown upperparts and brownish underparts with a yellowish tinge.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Mugimaki Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Males have black upperparts, white patch behind the eye, orange breast and throat and white belly. Females have brown upperparts instead.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Blue-and-white Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Males are easily recognised by blue upperparts, black face and throat. It is white from belly downwards. Females have brownish upperparts with distinct contrast between brownish breast and white belly.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Chinese Blue Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Males have a distinctive fieldmark where there a narrow orange wedge which extends from breast to the throat.  Females have a white throat and belly separated by a brown breast band.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Oriental Magpie-Robin
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: This songbird has black and white plumage with a long tail that is often held high.  Females are grey on upperparts and breast.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: White-rumped Shama
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: The white-rumped shama has black upperparts, orange breast and belly, white rump and long tail. Females are duller with shorter tail.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Indian Paradise Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Breeding males have an exceptionally long tail and come in either rufous or white colour morphs. Females and non-breeding males have much shorter tail and either white or chestnut upperparts with varying amount of grey or black on head, throat and upper breast.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Japanese Paradise Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Breeding males have an exceptionally long tail, dark purple plumage and white belly. Females and non-breeding males are generally darker than Asian Paradise Flycatchers with rusty-brown upperparts and black on the head, throat and upper breast.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Blue Rock Thrush
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: This species has blue upperparts and breast and a rusty-brown belly. Females are generally grey-brown, sometimes with faint bluish tinge, and heavily scaled throughout.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Brown-chested Jungle Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: This drab flycatcher may be confused with the other brown flycatchers like the Asian Brown and Brown-streaked. It can be identified by its completely yellow lower mandible, flesh coloured legs and also brown breast band which other flycatchers lack.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Asian Brown Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: The Asian Brown flycatcher has grey-brown throat and breast with white belly, prominent white lores and a fleshy base to its lower mandible.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Green-backed Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: With greenish brown upperparts and yellow underparts, females of this species look similar to the female Yellow-rumped Flycatcher. However, females of this species lack the yellow rump that the latter species has.  Males are distinctive – yellow eyebrow, greenish upperparts and bright yellow underparts with big white wing patch.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Mangrove Blue Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Similar to the Chinese Blue Flycatcher, but has a dark blue chin as opposed to an orange one. Females have white lores (area between eyes and bill base) and throat.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Siberian Blue Robin
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Male Siberian Blue Robins has blue upperparts and white underparts, while females are brown with pale underparts. Females have dull blue rump and tail.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Stejneger's Stonechat
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Males have a black head, dark brown upperparts, white collar and rufous underparts. Females are brown with a thin white collar, pale underparts and a beige/ light pink rump.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Zappey's Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Only males in breeding plumage can be distinguished from very similar Blue-and-white Flycatcher. Males of this species have bluish face and throat, not black as per the latter species.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Daurian Redstart
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Males have greyish crown, black face and throat, and orange underparts with distinct white wing patch. Females are generally brownish with pale eyering and white wing patch.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Amur Paradise Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Brown upperparts and tail, black head with grey underparts with white vent. Adult males can have tails longer than 27cm. White morphs exists but are rare. Compared with Blyth's Paradise Flycatcher, the blackish head contrasts noticeably with the greyish breast

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Blyth's Paradise Flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Brown upperparts and tail, grey head and underparts with white vent. Adult males can have tails longer than 27cm. White morphs occur rarely. Compared with Amur Paradise Flycatcher, there is minimal contrast between the grey head and breast

Cisticolas and Allies.Name: Zitting Cisticola
Cisticolas and Allies.Description: A small bird with brown and black upperparts, white underparts, brown rump and flanks and pale face.

Cisticolas and Allies.Name: Yellow-bellied Prinia
Cisticolas and Allies.Description: A tiny bird with a high-pitched trilling song, long tail, and yellow belly and vent.

Cisticolas and Allies.Name: Common Tailorbird
Cisticolas and Allies.Description: Similar to the Dark-necked Tailorbird, but has a less extensive red cap and white vent. Males have a longer tail than females.

Cisticolas and Allies.Name: Dark-necked Tailorbird
Cisticolas and Allies.Description: Similar to the Common Tailorbird but has a more extensive red cap and a yellow vent. Males have black breast patch which is absent in females.

Cisticolas and Allies.Name: Rufous-tailed Tailorbird
Cisticolas and Allies.Description: This species possesses a red tail and crown, grey mantle and white underparts.

Cisticolas and Allies.Name: Ashy Tailorbird
Cisticolas and Allies.Description: This tailorbird has a rufous head and grey upperparts with brownish wings, with pale ashy underparts.

Cockatoos.Name: Yellow-crested Cockatoo
Cockatoos.Description: This white bird is easily identifiable by its yellow crest, and the local population is thought to be a result of escapees or released pet birds.

Cockatoos.Name: Tanimbar Corella
Cockatoos.Description: A non-native bird is generally white and the pink lores.

Crows.Name: House Crow
Crows.Description: This urban bird can be differentiated from the Large-billed Crow by its grey collar.

Crows.Name: Large-billed Crow
Crows.Description: Similar to the House Crow except that it is entirely black and has a distinctly larger bill.

Cuckoos.Name: Chestnut-winged Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: This cuckoo has a distinctive black crest and long black tail.

Cuckoos.Name: Large Hawk-Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: Largest hawk-cuckoo species in Singapore, has contrasting streaks and barring on its underparts. Juveniles have streaked underparts.

Cuckoos.Name: Malaysian Hawk-Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: Adults have greyish upperparts and underparts with thin, dark brown streaks, juveniles with weaker streaking and more spotting; distinct white nape patch and broad tail subterminal band.

Cuckoos.Name: Hodgson's Hawk-Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: Adults have dark streaking with extensive rufous wash, juveniles have strong dark streaking with slight rufous-tinge; narrow tail subterminal band.

Cuckoos.Name: Indian Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: This species has greyish-brown upperparts contrasting and white underparts with numerous black bands. Distinct black band on upperside of tail.

Cuckoos.Name: Banded Bay Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: This species has barred throughout with rufous upperparts and white underparts, and can be distinguished from the other cuckoos by its whitish eyebrow.

Cuckoos.Name: Plaintive Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: This species has rufous underparts and a grey head, throat and breast. Can be differentiaed from the rusty-breasted cuckoo by its rufous plumage which only extendsto its belly. Juveniles have more prominent black barring.

Cuckoos.Name: Rusty-breasted Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: Similar to the Plaintive Cuckoo, except that it has a yellow eye ring, and the rufous plumage extends to its throat.

Cuckoos.Name: Little Bronze Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: Underparts of this cuckoo are white with black barring, not black and white barring. Only males have a red eye-ring.

Cuckoos.Name: Horsfield's Bronze Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: This species looks similar to the Little Bronze Cuckoo but can be distinguished by its dark eyestripe and incomplete bars on its belly.

Cuckoos.Name: Asian Emerald Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: This species gets its name from its bright metallic green upperparts.

Cuckoos.Name: Violet Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: Males of this species have a violet sheen to its head, back and wings. Females are a lot more drab, with mostly rusty brown and green upperparts .

Cuckoos.Name: Chestnut-bellied Malkoha
Cuckoos.Description: This large bird has a grey head and breast, dark metallic green upperparts and a long tail. It can be easily identified by its red eye-patch.

Cuckoos.Name: Greater Coucal
Cuckoos.Description: The Greater Coucal has a distinct dark plumage with chestnut brown wings.

Cuckoos.Name: Lesser Coucal
Cuckoos.Description: Similar to the Greater Coucal but is smaller and paler, and has pale streaks on its head and underparts.

Cuckoos.Name: Himalayan Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: Like Indian Cuckoo but mantle and upper back grey, also lacks the broad dark subterminal band on the upperside of the tail.

Cuckoos.Name: Square-tailed Drongo-Cuckoo
Cuckoos.Description: Can be distinguished from a drongo by its thinner bill and slight white barring on its tail. Juveniles have white spots on their plumage.

Cuckoos.Name: Asian Koel
Cuckoos.Description: This large bird has a distinct loud call from which it derives its common name. They can be distinguished from crows with their long tails and red eyes.

Cuckooshrikes and Minivets.Name: Lesser Cuckooshrike
Cuckooshrikes and Minivets.Description: Males of this species are grey with darker wings, while females are grey with heavily barred underparts.

Cuckooshrikes and Minivets.Name: Pied Triller
Cuckooshrikes and Minivets.Description: Males have a distinct black and white pied plumage, while females are greyish-brown above with fine barring on the underparts.

Cuckooshrikes and Minivets.Name: Ashy Minivet
Cuckooshrikes and Minivets.Description: The Ashy Minivet has grey upperparts and white underparts and a distinct black loral line. Males have a black cap, females have a grey cap.

Cuckooshrikes and Minivets.Name: Scarlet Minivet
Cuckooshrikes and Minivets.Description: Males have red underparts, rump and wing patches on otherwise black wings. In females, areas of red replaced by yellow which also extends to throat and forecrown.

Darters.Name: Oriental Darter
Darters.Description: A large bird with a long snake-like neck and pointed bill. Glossy black plumage with a brown head and neck, and distinct white stripes along the neck.

Drongo.Name: Black Drongo
Drongo.Description: Completely black with a deeply forked tail.

Drongo.Name: Ashy Drongo
Drongo.Description: The Ashy Drongo can be differentiated from the Black Drongo by its paler grey plumage and shallower forked tail.

Drongo.Name: Crow-billed Drongo
Drongo.Description: The Crow-billed Drongo can be differentiated from the Black Drongo by its larger bill and upturned forked tail. Immatures have white spots on the underparts.

Drongo.Name: Greater Racket-tailed Drongo
Drongo.Description: This unmistakable bird has two extended tail feathers and a distinct song with a metallic trill at the end. Also has distinct tuft of feathers at base of the bill.

Ducks.Name: Wandering Whistling Duck
Ducks.Description: So called because of their high-pitched whistles, the wandering whistling duck may be confused with the similar lesser whistling duck. It can be differentiated by its white flank plumes.

Ducks.Name: Lesser Whistling Duck
Ducks.Description: This species is also sometimes called the lesser tree duck as they occasionally nest in tree holes. Can be confused with the wandering whistling duck.

Ducks.Name: Cotton Pygmy Goose
Ducks.Description: Males of this species have a black cap and collar, while females lack this collar and have a dark eye-stripe.

Ducks.Name: Eurasian Wigeon
Ducks.Description: Females of this species are almost entirely brown, while males have a  chestnut head and neck and finely barred whitish underparts.

Ducks.Name: Gadwall
Ducks.Description: Males are generally gray-brown with a white belly and black rump, while females uniformly mottled brown and have a black and orange bill.

Ducks.Name: Eurasian Teal
Ducks.Description: Male Eurasian teals have a distinct green eye-patch. Females are more drab, with a mottled brown plumage and lacking the green eye-patch that males possess.

Ducks.Name: Northern Pintail
Ducks.Description: Males of this sepcies have characteristic long tail-feathers, and a distinct slim and long neck. Females are generally brown.

Ducks.Name: Northern Shoveler
Ducks.Description: So called for its large shovel-shaped bill, the Nothern Shoveler is an easy bird to identify. Males have a green head and white breast, while females are uniformly brown with an orange bill.

Ducks.Name: Tufted Duck
Ducks.Description: Males have a characteristic drooping crest and black and white plumage. Females are uniformly brown and have a short crest.

Fairy-bluebirds.Name: Asian Fairy-bluebird
Fairy-bluebirds.Description: An easily identifiable bird, males have a characteristic blue and black plumage while females are uniformly dull-blue. Both sexes have reddish eyes.

Falcons.Name: Black-thighed Falconet
Falcons.Description: This is a small falcon with a rufous belly, white breast and mostly black upperparts.

Falcons.Name: Common Kestrel
Falcons.Description: Males can be distinguished from the Lesser Kestrel by streaked grey heads and boldly marked chestnut upperparts. Females have more prominent streaks on their heads and underparts and more prominent face mask and upperpart markings.

Falcons.Name: Amur Falcon
Falcons.Description: Males of this species has dark grey upperparts and a pale grey breast and chesnut vent. Females have grey upperparts and grey and white streaked underparts. Both sexes have distinctive orange-red eyering, bill base and legs.

Falcons.Name: Peregrine Falcon
Falcons.Description: Larger than all the other falcons, the Peregrine Falcon has with heavily barred underparts, greyish upperparts with white underparts, whitish cheeks and a broad facial “streak”.

Fantails.Name: Malaysian Pied Fantail
Fantails.Description: This passerine species has a distinct pied plumage with a white throat and underparts and black breast band. Often fans its tail out during displays.

Finfoot.Name: Masked Finfoot
Finfoot.Description: This endangered shorebird is a visitor can be recognised by its dark face and throat with a white border and thick yellow bill. Females have a whitish throat and upper foreneck.

Flowerpeckers.Name: Thick-billed Flowerpecker
Flowerpeckers.Description: With its thick bill, this flowerpecker looks distinctly different from the other flowerpeckers. It has olive-brown upperparts and pale streaked underparts. Also has a unique habit of wagging its tail to one side when perched.

Flowerpeckers.Name: Yellow-vented Flowerpecker
Flowerpeckers.Description: This rare small bird can be easily identified by is olive-green upperparts, white underparts with bold black streaks, yellow vent and red eyes.

Flowerpeckers.Name: Orange-bellied Flowerpecker
Flowerpeckers.Description: Males have a beautiful blue and orange-yellow plumage, while females are duller green and yellow.

Flowerpeckers.Name: Scarlet-backed Flowerpecker
Flowerpeckers.Description: This common garden bird has a red crown and back, black upperparts and white underparts. Females are generally grey with a red rump.

Flycatcher-shrikes.Name: Black-winged Flycatcher-Shrike
Flycatcher-shrikes.Description: This rare species has black upperparts and white underparts.

Frigatebirds.Name: Lesser Frigatebird
Frigatebirds.Description: Males appear all black from below with small white underwing  "armpits" (spurs). Females have white belly patch, but less extensive than in Christmas Frigatebird females. In flight, it has a deeply forked tail and long pointed wings.

Frigatebirds.Name: Christmas Frigatebird
Frigatebirds.Description: Males have a diagnostic white belly patch contrasting with black underwing. Females have are extensively white on the underparts with prominent white underwing spurs and black patches on the side of the upper breast.

Frigatebirds.Name: Short-tailed Shearwater
Frigatebirds.Description: This seabird has a  sooty-brown plumage, a relatively short slender bill and fan-shaped tail.

Grass warblers.Name: Lanceolated Warbler
Grass warblers.Description: This small warbler is brown with pale undersides and prominent dark streaking on its breast, sides and vent.

Grass warblers.Name: Pallas's Grasshopper Warbler
Grass warblers.Description: Similar to the Lanceolated Warbler but with unstreaked rufous rump and lack of underpart streaks.

Greater Painted-snipe.Name: Greater Painted Snipe
Greater Painted-snipe.Description: Females more colourful than males with chestnut head and breast and white eye patch. Males have a yellowish eye patch and are grey-brown on the head and breast.

Grebes.Name: Little Grebe
Grebes.Description: This waterbird has a rusty brown neck and cheeks, yellow eyes and black cap. Non-breeding birds have their rusty-brown areas fade to a duller brown.

Ground babblers.Name: White-chested Babbler
Ground babblers.Description: A small plain bird with brown upperparts and white underparts

Ground babblers.Name: Abbott's Babbler
Ground babblers.Description: Similar to the Short-tailed babbler with brown upperparts, white breast and rusty belly. Can be distinguished by lack of black moustache of latter and longer tail. Grey on head less extensive than Short-tailed.

Ground babblers.Name: Short-tailed Babbler
Ground babblers.Description: The Short-tailed babbler has  brown upperparts, a pale eyebrow, whitish breast and rufous belly and vent. Has more intensely coloured grey head than Abbott's Babbler and black moustache. Tail is very short.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Roseate Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: This tern has a distinctly long white tail and bright red legs in breeding birds. In the winter, they have a black cap, bill and legs. Distinguished from Common Tern by white underwing which lacks any black trailing edge.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Black-naped Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: This tern is easily identified with its black nape on a generally whitish plumage.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Common Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: Similar to the Roseate Tern in non-breeding plumage but its underwing is greyish with black trailing edge.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Whiskered Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: This small tern may be confused with the White-winged tern in non-breeding plumage, but has a grey rump, black-streaked white crown and facial markings which do not extend below the eye.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Lesser Black-backed Gull
Gulls and Terns.Description: This species has a white head and underparts and grey upperparts. Juveniles are a mottled grey.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Brown-headed Gull
Gulls and Terns.Description: Has a brown head and looks similar to the Black-headed gull but has a thicker bill and neck and diagnostic black wing tips in flight.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Black-headed Gull
Gulls and Terns.Description: Breeding adults have a dark-brown hood and reddish bill. Birds in winter plumage have a black ear spot and a reddish bill with a black tip.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Gull-billed Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: So called for possessing a gull-like bill. Breeding adults have a black cap from forehead to nape, while non-breeding adults have a black patch on their ear coverts.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Caspian Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: This tern has a black cap and red bill. Non-breeding indivduals have a streaked cap.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Lesser Crested Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: This species has a black cap extending to the bill, which is reduced to the area around the nape in non-breeders. Has white underparts and a bright orange bill.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Greater Crested Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: Distinguished from Lesser Crested Tern by larger size and dull yellow bill.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Little Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: This is the smallest tern in Singapore and therefore easily recognised. In breeding plumage, it has a white forehead on a black cap, which becomes more extensively white in winter. Breeding birds have yellow bill with black tip.

Gulls and Terns.Name: Aleutian Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: In breeding plumage, the Aleutian tern has  a black crown and nape and eye-stripe, which becomes paler in winter. It can be recognised by its black trailing edge on underwing secondaries (i.e. the tip of the rear flight feathers closest to the bird’s body).

Gulls and Terns.Name: Bridled Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: Dark brownish-grey upperparts with white underparts, flight feathers are dark and form a dark trailing edge in flight/

Gulls and Terns.Name: White-winged Tern
Gulls and Terns.Description: This small tern may be confused with the Whiskered tern in non-breeding plumage, but has a white rump and distinct facial markings reminiscent of headphones which extend below the eye.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Little Egret
Herons and Bitterns.Description: This all-white egret can be differentiated from the others by its black bill and black legs with yellow feet.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Chinese Egret
Herons and Bitterns.Description: In non-breeding plumage, this egret can be differentiated from other similar egrets by a combination of features, greenish facial skin, thick dagger-like bill, greenish-yellow legs and feet, two-tone bill (black towards tip and yellow towards base). Moves very actively when feeding, which is a characteristic behaviour for this egret.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Pacific Reef Heron
Herons and Bitterns.Description: This species has both a dark morph, which is unmistakably slate-grey, and a light morph, which is white. Light morph has thick greenish legs and feet, yellowish bill and appears shorter-legged than other white egrets.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Grey Heron
Herons and Bitterns.Description: This tall bird has a light grey plumage with a black stripe above its eyes and black stripes on its neck.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Great-billed Heron
Herons and Bitterns.Description: This heron gets its name from its large bill and is the tallest bird in Singapore at  115cm. It has dark grey plumage with pale streaks on its wings and neck.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Purple Heron
Herons and Bitterns.Description: This heron can be easily identified by its rusty red neck and purplish grey plumage.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Chinese Pond Heron
Herons and Bitterns.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a brown head and breast, black back and white belly and wings. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Javan Pond Heron
Herons and Bitterns.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a pale rufous head, brown breast, black back. and white belly. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Black-crowned Night Heron
Herons and Bitterns.Description: This distinctive heron has a black crown and back, red eyes and white underparts.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Malayan Night Heron
Herons and Bitterns.Description: This heron has a black crown and reddish-brown plumage with streaked underparts. Juveniles have mottled brown upperparts with numerous white spots and black barring on  their underparts.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Yellow Bittern
Herons and Bitterns.Description: A shy bird that is often found in pondside vegetation, the Yellow Bittern can be identified by the contrast between its yellowish brown wing coverts and black flight feathers in flight.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Von Schrenck's Bittern
Herons and Bitterns.Description: The male of this species has chesnut upperparts and pale underparts, while the females have numerous white spots on brown upperparts and are boldly streaked on their underparts.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Cinnamon Bittern
Herons and Bitterns.Description: This species has cinnamon upperparts with streaked underparts, and appears uniformly reddish-brown in flight.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Black Bittern
Herons and Bitterns.Description: The black bittern is so called for its dark upperparts and underparts which are streaked with white.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Great Egret
Herons and Bitterns.Description: This all-white egret has a yellow bill and black legs, and can be differentiated from other similar egrets by its large size and prominent kink in its long S-shaped neck.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Intermediate Egret
Herons and Bitterns.Description: This all-white egret has a yellow bill with a black tip and black legs and feet. Its S-shaped neck is roughly equal to its body length.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Eastern Cattle Egret
Herons and Bitterns.Description: Easter cattle egrets are white with a rufous head and breast. In non-breeding plumage, it is completely white and can be differentiated by its small size.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Striated Heron
Herons and Bitterns.Description: A small heron with dark crown, grey mantle and underparts and yellowish legs. It can be confused with the Black-crowned Night Heron.

Herons and Bitterns.Name: Indian Pond Heron
Herons and Bitterns.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a pale brown head, neck and breast, white throat and belly, and dark maroon-brown back. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Hornbills.Name: Oriental Pied Hornbill
Hornbills.Description: This large striking bird was once rare in Singapore, but local populations have increased after a successful re-introduction programme. They can be found outside forests as well.

Ibises.Name: Glossy Ibis
Ibises.Description: This tall bird is unmistakable with its characteristic long down-curved bill. It has a rusty brown head and underparts and glossy black upperparts.

Ioras.Name: Common Iora
Ioras.Description: Males have black upperparts and yellow underparts, while females have olive-green upperparts and yellow underparts. Two white wing bars distinctive in both sexes

Jacanas.Name: Pheasant-tailed Jacana
Jacanas.Description: In breeding plumage, this bird has a long prominent tail from which it gets its name from. In non-breeding plumage, it has white underparts, a black breast band, yellow hindneck, black neck-line and brown upperparts.

Jaegers.Name: Pomarine Jaeger
Jaegers.Description: The Pomarine Jaeger is more bulky than the Parasitic  Jawger with generally broader wings It has has diagnostic spoon-shaped tail feathers that are sometimes visible in immatures as well.

Jaegers.Name: Parasitic Jaeger
Jaegers.Description: Adults have pointed tail streamers while juveniles have pointed central tail feathers. Generally more compact that Pomarine Jaeger with a more streamlined flight profile.

Jaegers.Name: Long-tailed Jaeger
Jaegers.Description: This species of jaeger is smallest and greyest of the three and has a distinctly long tail. Adults of this species lack the white flashes on the wings compared to the other two jaeger species.

Kingfishers.Name: Common Kingfisher
Kingfishers.Description: Common Kingfishers can usually be seen perching just above the water's edge. They migrate south to countries like Singapore where they spend the winter months.

Kingfishers.Name: Blue-eared Kingfisher
Kingfishers.Description: This species is similar to the Common Kingfisher but has a deeper blue blue plumage. It is a resident species.

Kingfishers.Name: Stork-billed Kingfisher
Kingfishers.Description: This large kingfisher gets its name from its strong large bill which calls to mind a stork's bill.

Kingfishers.Name: Ruddy Kingfisher
Kingfishers.Description: This species is easy to recognise as it has a pinkish-brown plumage and red bill.

Kingfishers.Name: White-throated Kingfisher
Kingfishers.Description: A common species in Singapore, this bird can be recognised by the white-breast and throat on its otherwise brown underparts.

Kingfishers.Name: Black-capped Kingfisher
Kingfishers.Description: This species has a characteristic black cap, as well as a red bill and legs.

Kingfishers.Name: Oriental Dwarf Kingfisher
Kingfishers.Description: Also known as the Black-backed Kingfisher, this small kingfisher has blue-black wings along with a distinct purplish-pink crown and rump. Underparts are orange.

Kingfishers.Name: Collared Kingfisher
Kingfishers.Description: This common species has a turquoise cap, wings back and tail, and a white collar and underparts.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Jerdon's Baza
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This species has a white-tipped black crest, brown upperparts and rufous bands on its underparts. When viewed from below, it shows shows distinct black bars on flight feathers (i.e. wing tips).

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Black Baza
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: As with the Jerdon's Baza, this species has a black crest as well, but has black upperparts, white underparts with brown bands and a black breast band. In flight, grey patches visible on underwing.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Bat Hawk
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Generally black with a white throat and vent and pale legs, and has bright yellow eyes with white “spectacles” aroud it.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Black-winged Kite
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This kite has grey upperparts and white underparts and head, a black shoulder patch, as well as red eyes. When viewed from below, the outer half of the wings are dark

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Black Kite
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Looks similar to juvenile brahminy kites, can be recognised by its prominent forked tail.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Brahminy Kite
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Easily recognished by its white head and chest and chestnut brown belly. One of the most common raptors in Singapore.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: White-bellied Sea Eagle
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This large raptor can be identified by its white underparts and mostly black wings.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Himalayan Vulture
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This species is much larger than any other raptors seen in Singapore, and has much broader wings compared to the other raptors. They are heavily streaked on the underparts.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Short-toed Snake Eagle
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This snake-eating eagle has a distinct brown head, and white underparts with black speckles and barring when viewed from below. Its wings are barred and black-tipped.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Crested Serpent Eagle
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This bird is mostly brown and has a yellow patch between its eyes and beak. In flight, it can be recognised by a broad white band across the length of the wing bordered by black.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Western Marsh Harrier
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Similar to the Eastern marsh harrier but female is less streaked and males have strong brown upperparts and underparts.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Eastern Marsh Harrier
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Males streaked black on head, mantle and upper breast, lacks white wing patch, while in females, rufous thighs and vent distinctive.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Pied Harrier
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Males have black heads, mantle and upper breast, a large white wing patch and white underparts. Females have white underparts, and grey and white streaked upperparts.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Crested Goshawk
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This species has streaked breast contrasting sharply with dark bands on belly, and bold vertical throat stripe. In flight, comparatively long tail shows four dark tail bands.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Chinese Sparrowhawk
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This is an easily identifiable species with its grey upperparts, mostly white underparts and rufous breast. In flight, wing tips are black and 4 "fingers" are visible.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Japanese Sparrowhawk
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Might be confused with the Chinese Sparrowhawk, but lacks black wing tips and underparts are visibly barred. Has 5 "fingers" visible in flight.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Besra
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Similar to the Japanese Sparrowhawk but with bold mesial stripe in all plumages and bands in underwing are thicker.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Grey-faced Buzzard
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This species has brown upperparts and breast, barred underparts, grey head-sides  and banded tail.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Common Buzzard
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Plumage of this raptor can be variable but is generally brown above with buffy underparts and a brown belly patch. In flight, it has black tips to flight feathers and black trailing edges along the length of its wings.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Steppe Eagle
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: May be confused with the Greater Spotted Eagle but is generally larger, paler and longer wings. When viewed from below, its wings are two-toned.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Booted Eagle
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: In flight, this species has pale or chestnut underparts with dark flight feathers. There is also a light morph which has diagnostic contrast between white underparts and underwing coverts and black primary and secondaries. Both morphs have white shoulder patches that look like headlights when viewed head-on.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Crested Honey Buzzard
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Plumagen of this raptor can be highly variable but its flight shape is distinctive, featuring proportionally small, pigeon-like head, comparatively long tail and wings with 6 "fingers" in flight.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Grey-headed Fish Eagle
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This species has a distinct white tail with black terminal band visible in flight. It also has a sharp demarcation between its brown breast and white belly.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Hen Harrier
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Males are grey with white underparts and vent, while females can be distinguished from other harriers by streaked thighs and vent.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Greater Spotted Eagle
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: Has uniformly dark plumage with broad wings and a short tail. Juveniles have numerous large white spots on their wings.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Eastern Imperial Eagle
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: A very large eagle, with a straw-coloured crown and hindneck distinctive in adults, while juveniles have diagnostic broad white band across the underwing

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Rufous-bellied Eagle
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: As its name suggests, it has a rusty-red belly, with a white breast and throat and dark brown upperparts. Juveniles are generally brown above and white below with distinctive white eye-brow and black face mask.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Changeable Hawk-Eagle
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This species has a light and dark morph. Compared to Crested Honey Buzzard, has a bulging trailing edge and 7 "fingers" in flight, shorter tail and feathered legs.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Blyth's Hawk-Eagle
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: This striking raptor has a characteristic black and white plumage and back crest. Its belly is banded and wings has barring. Can be distinguished from all other hawk-eagles by broad white band on otherwise dark tail.

Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Name: Shikra
Kites, Hawks and Eagles.Description: A small raptor with brown plumage and barrings on its breast and belly, and a greyish head and back.

Laughing Thrushes.Name: White-crested Laughingthrush
Laughing Thrushes.Description: An unmistakable bird with its white crest and breast, black mask and rich brown upperparts.

Laughing Thrushes.Name: Chinese Hwamei
Laughing Thrushes.Description: With its distinctive white spectacles and eye-stripe, this bird is a popular cagebird due to its fantastic singing ability. Escapees have established themselves in several areas throughout Singapore.

Leaf Warblers.Name: Dusky Warbler
Leaf Warblers.Description: A ashy brown warbler with pale underparts that can be identified by its bold white eyebrow.

Leaf Warblers.Name: Yellow-browed Warbler
Leaf Warblers.Description: This rare warbler has olive-brown upperparts and yellowish eyebrow. It has two distinct whitish bars and lack of a crown stripe.

Leaf Warblers.Name: Arctic Warbler
Leaf Warblers.Description: Arctic Warbler differs from Eastern Crowned Warbler by having a white, not yellow, vent and lacks a crown stripe.

Leaf Warblers.Name: Eastern Crowned Warbler
Leaf Warblers.Description: This warbler species can be discerned from the other warblers by its dinstinctive pale crown stripe and yellow vent.

Leaf Warblers.Name: Sakhalin Leaf Warbler
Leaf Warblers.Description: Greyish crown contrasts with olive-brown upperparts with long, thin white supercilium that contrasts sharply with dark eyestripe; underparts whitish with flesh-coloured legs.

Leafbirds.Name: Greater Green Leafbird
Leafbirds.Description: This bird has an all-green plumage, with a black face and throat for males, and yellow eye-ring and throat for females.

Leafbirds.Name: Blue-winged Leafbird
Leafbirds.Description: The most easily identified leafbird due to blue patches on the wings and tail in both sexes. Both sexes also have a yellow cap.

Leafbirds.Name: Lesser Green Leafbird
Leafbirds.Description: Similar to the Greater Green Leafbird but is smaller in size with a slimmer bill. Males have a smaller black mask and females lack yellow eyering and throat.

Munias.Name: Red Avadavat
Munias.Description: A tiny stout bird with a thick  bill. Males are bright red with white spots on its flank, while females are brown with a red rump.

Munias.Name: White-rumped Munia
Munias.Description: Has dark brown plumage with a white belly and rump. Upperparts streaked white.

Munias.Name: Javan Munia
Munias.Description: Similar to the White-rumped munia except that it lacks the white-rump. Upperparts unstreaked.

Munias.Name: Scaly-breasted Munia
Munias.Description: This bird gets its common name from the scaling on its breast. Has a dark brown head and upperparts.

Munias.Name: White-headed Munia
Munias.Description: Has a white head and throat, which distinguishes it from the similar White-capped munia.

Munias.Name: Chestnut Munia
Munias.Description: Easily recognised by its entirely black head and chesnut brown body.

Nightjars.Name: Large-tailed Nightjar
Nightjars.Description: This species has bold dark streaks on its upperparts and has a long tail.

Nightjars.Name: Savanna Nightjar
Nightjars.Description: Can be distinguished from the Large-tailed Nightjar by its slimmer body and lack of black streaks on its upperparts

Nightjars.Name: Malaysian Eared Nightjar
Nightjars.Description: Distinguished from other nightjars by long-tailed appearance in flight recalling a small raptor. At rest appears uniformly brown and ear tufts are sometimes visible.

Nightjars.Name: Grey Nightjar
Nightjars.Description: Has a darker and greyer plumage than the other nightjars. They are frequently encountered roosting in trees.

Old World Sparrows.Name: House Sparrow
Old World Sparrows.Description: While similar to the common Eurasian Tree Sparrow, this rare introduced species can be distinguished by its gray crown and lack of black cheek spot.

Old World Sparrows.Name: Eurasian Tree Sparrow
Old World Sparrows.Description: This common species has a brown cap and prominent black patches on its cheeks and chin.

Orioles.Name: Black-naped Oriole
Orioles.Description: This common garden bird is unmistakable with its bright yellow plumage, black nape and wings, and pink bill.

Osprey.Name: Western Osprey
Osprey.Description: This fish-eating raptor has brown upperparts and grey-white underparts and head. It also has a black eye stripe and brown breast band.

Owls.Name: Oriental Scops Owl
Owls.Description: May be confused with the Sunda Scops Owl but it is smaller, underparts generally contain more white and has bright yellow eyes.

Owls.Name: Buffy Fish Owl
Owls.Description: This large owl has prominent ear tufts, a sharp grey beak and large yellow eyes. It is often found near water as it mainly preys on fish.

Owls.Name: Spotted Wood Owl
Owls.Description: The spotted wood owl can be identified by its rusty-brown face with large dark eyes and dark beak. Might be confused with the Brown Wood Owl which has a dark outline around its face.

Owls.Name: Brown Wood Owl
Owls.Description: This large owl can be recognised by its paler facial disc which contrasts against its dark head, and has also dark “spectacles” around its eyes.

Owls.Name: Brown Hawk-Owl
Owls.Description: This owl has white underparts with distinct heart-shaped spots and a brown head.

Owls.Name: Short-eared Owl
Owls.Description: A distinctive owl with straw-brown upperparts and underparts which are boldly streaked. Unlike most owls, it is active in the daytime as well.

Owls.Name: Sunda Scops Owl
Owls.Description: May be confused with the Oriental Scops Owl but it is larger, underparts are generally brownish and eyes are dark brown/orange.

Owls.Name: Barred Eagle-Owl
Owls.Description: This striking bird has large ear tufts and yellow beak. As its name suggests, it has prominent barring on most of its body.

Owls.Name: Northern Boobook
Owls.Description: Similar to Brown Hawk-owl but has large yellow eyes and vertical, not heart-shaped streaks, on its underparts

Parrots.Name: Blue-rumped Parrot
Parrots.Description: Males of this species have a blue head while females have a brown head.

Parrots.Name: Blue-crowned Hanging Parrot
Parrots.Description: Males of this species have a generally green with a red breast patch and blue spot on its crown. Females lack the red breast patch.

Parrots.Name: Rose-ringed Parakeet
Parrots.Description: Male Rose-ringed Parakeets have a thin red and black ring around their necks which females lack.

Parrots.Name: Red-breasted Parakeet
Parrots.Description: Males of this species have a red/pink beak, while females have a black beak.

Parrots.Name: Long-tailed Parakeet
Parrots.Description: This species has an exceptionally long tail, and can be idneitifed by its red/pink head and green cap.

Parrots.Name: Coconut Lorikeet
Parrots.Description: This colourful bird can be easily identified from its bright red beak, green plumage and yellow nape.

Passerines.Name: Black-and-red Broadbill
Passerines.Description: This bird has black-and-red plumage, white wing stripe and a large broad bill. The upper mandible is bright blue, while the lower mandible is yellow.

Pheasants.Name: Red Junglefowl
Pheasants.Description: This nationally-threatened species is one of the main ancestral species of the domestic chicken. It is able to interbreed with domestic chickens.

Pheasants.Name: King Quail
Pheasants.Description: Males have a black and white face with bluish sides and chestnut belly. Females are uniformly brown.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Red Turtle Dove
Pigeons and Doves.Description: This dove has a black line on its nape and a grey head. Males appear more rusty-brown, while females are  grey-brown.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Common Emerald Dove
Pigeons and Doves.Description: This dove can be easily identified by its emerald-green wings.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Zebra Dove
Pigeons and Doves.Description: This dove may be confused with the Spotted Dove but has a striped neck and has a slimmer build.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Cinnamon-headed Green Pigeon
Pigeons and Doves.Description: As its name suggests, the males of the Cinnamon-headed Green Pigeon has a cinnamon coloured head. Females have a green head instead.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Little Green Pigeon
Pigeons and Doves.Description: This colourful bird has an orange breast , grey head, maroon wings and green belly. Females are mostly green. It is considerably smaller than the Pink-necked Green Pigeon.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Pink-necked Green Pigeon
Pigeons and Doves.Description: Similar colouration to the Little Green Pigeon but males have a pink neck and green wings, and are much larger. Females are mostly green.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Thick-billed Green Pigeon
Pigeons and Doves.Description: This pigeon has a thicker bill compared to the other pigeon species, and also has a distinct green eye-ring. Males have maroon wings, while females are a duller green.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Jambu Fruit Dove
Pigeons and Doves.Description: Males are easily identifiable by their white underparts and distinct pink breast patch. Females are dark green with a pale belly.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Green Imperial Pigeon
Pigeons and Doves.Description: This large pigeon has a distinct chestnut-coloured vent, and has a grey head and underparts and dark green wings and upperparts.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Mountain Imperial Pigeon
Pigeons and Doves.Description: Similar to the Green Imperial Pigeon but has creamy vent and grey tail bands.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Pied Imperial Pigeon
Pigeons and Doves.Description: An unmistakable large pigeon which has a striking black and white plumage.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Rock Dove
Pigeons and Doves.Description: This urban bird typically appears grey, but can include brown, black and white morphs.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Spotted Dove
Pigeons and Doves.Description: This dove may be confused with the Zebra Dove but has a spotted neck and is larger.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Oriental Turtle-Dove
Pigeons and Doves.Description: Dark brown plumage, with distinct black and white markings on neck. Rufous scaling on its wings gave rise to its common name.

Pittas.Name: Hooded Pitta
Pittas.Description: This striking bird has a black head with brown cap, green body and red vent.

Pittas.Name: Mangrove Pitta
Pittas.Description: Similar to the Blue-Winged Pitta, but has a more robust bill and brown supercilium is much thinner.

Pittas.Name: Blue-winged Pitta
Pittas.Description: This colourful pitta has a black head with pale crown and collar, rufous underparts, red vent, green upperparts and blue wings.

Plovers.Name: Pacific Golden Plover
Plovers.Description: In breeding plumage, this bird has a black face and undersides bordered by a white line, and upperparts  are black and gold. In non-breeding plumage, the  bird is mottled golden-brown, and white plumage is restricted to belly, though not particularly distinct.

Plovers.Name: Grey Plover
Plovers.Description: As the name suggests, this plover has a grey plumage. In breeding season, it has a black face and underparts, which become pale in winter. Its key diagnostic feature is its  black “armpits” on underside of wings which is visible in flight.

Plovers.Name: Little Ringed Plover
Plovers.Description: This small plover has brown upperparts, white underparts, a black breast band and distinct yellow eyering. It can be confused with the Common Ringed Plover, but has a yellow eye ring.

Plovers.Name: Kentish Plover
Plovers.Description: This plover has white underparts and brown upperparts, and black legs and bill. Unlike both Lesser and Greater Sand Plovers, it has a complete white neck collar.

Plovers.Name: Malaysian Plover
Plovers.Description: Males have a black “collar” which in females is rufous. This distinguishes them from non-breeding Kentish Plover.

Plovers.Name: Lesser Sand Plover
Plovers.Description: In breeding plumage, this plover has a rusty breast and black band over its eyes. In non-breeding plumage, the plover has brown upperparts and white underparts.

Plovers.Name: Greater Sand Plover
Plovers.Description: Similar to the Lesser Sand Plover but is larger, has longer, greenish-yellow legs and a more robust bill.

Plovers.Name: Oriental Plover
Plovers.Description: In breeding plumage, this species has a chestnut breast band with black border and white face and belly. In winter, it has brown upperparts and pale underparts.

Plovers.Name: Grey-headed Lapwing
Plovers.Description: This large lapwing has a grey head, neck and upper breast, black breastband and brown upperparts and white belly.

Plovers.Name: Red-wattled Lapwing
Plovers.Description: The Red-Wattled Lapwing has a striking black head and breast, white belly, brown upperparts and red beak. It also has a distinct white ear patch.

Pranticoles.Name: Oriental Pratincole
Pranticoles.Description: Resembling an oversized swallow, this bird has a black mark under its eyes that borders the throat.

Pranticoles.Name: Small Pratincole
Pranticoles.Description: The Small Prantincole has a white eye-ring and a generally grey plumage with whitish underparts. It has distinctive white wing bars on upperwing and underwing area visible in flight which the Oriental Pratincole lacks.

Rails and Crakes.Name: Red-legged Crake
Rails and Crakes.Description: This small waterbird gets its name from its bright red legs. Adults also have a distinctive chestnut head and breast and black and white barring on their underparts.

Rails and Crakes.Name: Slaty-legged Crake
Rails and Crakes.Description: Similar to the Red-legged Crake except for grey legs and lacks the whitish spots on its wings.

Rails and Crakes.Name: Slaty-breasted Rail
Rails and Crakes.Description: This rail has grey underparts and dark mottled upperparts. Crown and nape are chestnut, while bill is red.

Rails and Crakes.Name: White-breasted Waterhen
Rails and Crakes.Description: This common waterbird has a white face and breast, and blackish upperparts and brown vent.

Rails and Crakes.Name: Ruddy-breasted Crake
Rails and Crakes.Description: This crake has a rusty-red breast, head and belly, and a black and white barred vent.

Rails and Crakes.Name: White-browed Crake
Rails and Crakes.Description: The White-browed crake is easily recognised by the two white stripes above and below its eyes.

Rails and Crakes.Name: Watercock
Rails and Crakes.Description: When in breeding plumage, this water bird is black with a bright red facial shield.  Females and males in non-breeding plumage is a duller mottled brown.

Rails and Crakes.Name: Common Moorhen
Rails and Crakes.Description: The Common Moorhen is largely black with a prominent red bill with yellow tip. Adults  have a red frontal shield.

Rails and Crakes.Name: Eurasian Coot
Rails and Crakes.Description: Similar to the Common Moorhen except that its shield and beak are white.

Rails and Crakes.Name: Baillons Crake
Rails and Crakes.Description: This crake has a white, brown and black mottled plumage, with a greenish bill and legs.

Rails and Crakes.Name: Black-backed Swamphen
Rails and Crakes.Description: This bird can be easily identified by its brilliant purple-blue plumage and red bill, facial shield and legs.

Rails and Crakes.Name: Band-bellied Crake
Rails and Crakes.Description: Dull brown upperparts, rufous breast and black belly with white bars.

Reed warblers.Name: Black-browed Reed Warbler
Reed warblers.Description: Named after its distinct black eyebrow, the Black-browed reed warbler has brown upperparts and pale underparts.

Reed warblers.Name: Oriental Reed Warbler
Reed warblers.Description: This large warbler may be confused with the smaller Black-browed reed warbler, but can generally be distinguished by the lack of a dark eyebrow.

Reed warblers.Name: Booted Warbler
Reed warblers.Description: Pale brown head and upperparts, and pale underparts. Note also long, white supercilium that fades behind the eye.

Rollers.Name: Oriental Dollarbird
Rollers.Description: This bird has two white circular patches under its wings, which are visible when in flight.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Eurasian Woodcock
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: This species has a reddish-brown upperparts and cream underparts that help it camouflage in woodlands.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Pin-tailed Snipe
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: Only reliable way to differentiate between the two is by the shape of the outer tail feathers. In Pin-tailed Snipes, the outer eight pairs of tail feathers (sometimes six to nine pairs) are very thin (all less than 2mm wide) while in Swinhoe’s the outermost pair is narrowest (between 2 to 4mm), and subsequent tail feathers becoming increasingly broader towards the center. However, this feature is exceptionally difficult to observe in the field.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Swinhoe's Snipe
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: Only reliable way to differentiate between the two is by the shape of the outer tail feathers. In Pin-tailed Snipes, the outer eight pairs of tail feathers (sometimes six to nine pairs) are very thin (all less than 2mm wide) while in Swinhoe’s the outermost pair is narrowest (between 2 to 4mm), and subsequent tail feathers becoming increasingly broader towards the center. However, this feature is exceptionally difficult to observe in the field.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Common Snipe
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: In flight, white trailing edge to secondaries distinctive and unique among all local snipes; underwing coverts (i.e. armpits) generally white and unbarred. At rest, from “Swintail” snipes by white only on outer edge of scapular feathers.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Black-tailed Godwit
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: Similar to the Bar-tailed Godwit, except that its bill is straight, and has white wing bars (mainly visible in flight) and black tail bands. In breeding plumage, this bird has a rufous coloured head and breast.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Bar-tailed Godwit
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: Similar to the Black-tailed Godwit, except that its bill is slightly upturned, and lacks white wing bars and black tail bands.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Little Curlew
