Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: The Little Curlew has a black stripe across its head, a slightly down-curved beak, brown upperparts and pale underparts. Its bill is comparatively fine relative to that of the Whimbrel.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Whimbrel
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: Similar to the Little Curlew but has a larger and with a longer bill.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Eurasian Curlew
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: The Eurasian Curlew has a long down-curved bil and can be distinguished from the Far Eastern Curlew by its white rump and underwing coverts (i.e. armpits; mainly seen in flight).

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Far Eastern Curlew
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: Similar to the Eurasian Curlew but has a longer bill and heavier streaking on its underparts.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Spotted Redshank
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: The Spotted Redshank has a longer and finer bill than Common Redshank, and lacks white wing patch in flight. In breeding plumage,it is all black with numerous white spots on upperparts.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Common Redshank
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: The Common Redshank has shorter legs and bill compared to the Spotted redshank, and as has prominent white wing patches (in flight).

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Marsh Sandpiper
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: This waterbird has greyish upperparts and white underparts, greenish-yellow legs and a thin black bill.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Common Greenshank
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: So called for its greenish long legs, the Common Greenshank can be differentiated from the Marsh Sandpiper by its larger size and slightly upturned bill.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Nordmann's Greenshank
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: The Nordmann's Greenshank may be confused with the Common Greenshank, but has shorter, yellow legs and a characteristic two-tone bill which is paler at the base and darker towards the tip.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Green Sandpiper
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: Has less spotting on upperparts and dark underwing compared to Wood Sandpiper; can also be distinguished from Common Sandpiper by larger size and white rump.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Wood Sandpiper
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: Looks similar to the Green Sandpiper but distinguished by the whitish patches on its underwing and distinctly more white spotting on its upperparts.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Grey-tailed Tattler
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: This species has a prominent white eyebrow and yellow legs. Breast is greyish while belly is white.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Ruddy Turnstone
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: In breeding plumage, this bird has rusty-brown upperparts, which becomes a dull grey-brown in winter. Legs are a distinct orange.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Asian Dowitcher
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: In breeding plumage, the Asian Dowitcher has reddish brown upperparts, which becomes a dull grey in winter. Unlike the Godwits, its bill is uniformly black.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Great Knot
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: The Great Knot has brown streaky upperparts and white underparts. It has distinctive black spots on its breast.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Sanderling
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: In breeding plumage, the Sanderling has brown upperparts and white underparts. In non-breeding plumage, upperparts are greyish. It has a short black bill and legs.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Red-necked Stint
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: This species gets its name from its reddish neck when it is in breeding plumage. In winter, its neck is pale.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Temminck's Stint
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: Temminck's stint have brown upperparts and white underparts, a black beak and yellow legs.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Long-toed Stint
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: This stint has a long neck with short black bill and yellow legs. In non-breeding plumage, upperparts are greyish brown, and underparts white.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Sharp-tailed Sandpiper
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: May be confused with the Pectoral Sandpiper but has a strong contrast between rufous crown and white eyebrow, and has streaks on flanks.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Curlew Sandpiper
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: The Curlew Sandpiper has a relatively long, decurved bill and rusty-red underparts during the breeding season, which become pale in winter.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Broad-billed Sandpiper
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: This sandpiper has a broad bill that droops at the tip and a prominent split eyebrow (supercilium).

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Ruff
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: Males of this species are larger than the females, and in breeding plumage have  brightly coloured head tufts. In winter, both males and females are grey-brown upperparts and white underparts.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Red-necked Phalarope
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: In breeding plumage, this species has a rusty red neck, which becomes white in winter. Upperparts grey-brown and underparts white, and possesses a black eye-stripe. It is generally observed floating on a water body like a tiny duck.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Terek Sandpiper
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: This sandpiper has a dark upcurved bill and short orangey-yellow legs.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Common Sandpiper
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: The Common Sandpiper feeds with a distinct tail-bobbing movement.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Spoon-billed Sandpiper
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: This sandpiper has an unmistakeable spoon-shaped bill that sweeps from side to side on the mud to feed.

Sandpipers and Snipes.Name: Beach Stone-curlew
Sandpipers and Snipes.Description: This coastal bird has a characteristic stout black beak and robust yellow legs..

Shrikes.Name: Tiger Shrike
Shrikes.Description: Adults have a grey head, black face mask, barred chestnut upperparts and white underparts. The more commonly encountered immatures are chestnut above and white below with heavy barring on both upperparts and underparts.

Shrikes.Name: Brown Shrike
Shrikes.Description: Not similar to the Tiger Shrike. Adults have brown cap, white eye-brow above black face mask, unbarred brown upperparts and whitish underparts with a brownish wash.

Shrikes.Name: Long-tailed Shrike
Shrikes.Description: This large shrike has a long black tail which the other two species do not possess. Also differentiated from the other local shrikes by black wings and a white wing patch that is mainly visible in flight.

Sparrows.Name: Java Sparrow
Sparrows.Description: A striking bird with a large red beak and feet, black head with white cheek patch and grey body with pale belly.

Starlings.Name: Asian Glossy Starling
Starlings.Description: This bird is glossy dark green with red eyes is often seen in flocks. Juveniles are grey above and white below and covered in bold streaks.

Starlings.Name: Common Myna
Starlings.Description: Despite its name, it is less common than the White-vented myna. Distinguishable by its brown body and yellow eye-patch.

Starlings.Name: Javan Myna
Starlings.Description: The most common bird in Singapore, this species can be found in most urban areas.It has a black plumage, white vent and yellow beak.

Starlings.Name: Crested Myna
Starlings.Description: This is a rare myna that looks similar to the White-vented Myna that can be identified by its crest, red eyes and white barrings on vent.

Starlings.Name: Common Hill Myna
Starlings.Description: This large myna is black with a prominent orange bill and bare yellow patches of skin on head.

Starlings.Name: Daurian Starling
Starlings.Description: This bird is a creamy white with metallic green wings with a white wingbar.

Starlings.Name: White-shouldered Starling
Starlings.Description: This starling is mostly grey with a large white shoulder patch. It has white eyes.

Starlings.Name: Rosy Starling
Starlings.Description: This distinct bird has a rosy pink and black plumage. Juveniles are brown without the two toned plumage.

Stilts.Name: Black-winged Stilt
Stilts.Description: This bird has a needle-like bill and striking red legs, and black and white plumage.

Storks.Name: Asian Openbill
Storks.Description: This stork gets its common name from the gap in its large bill when closed. Uses bill to feed on favoured diet of snails.

Storks.Name: Lesser Adjutant
Storks.Description: This large stork has a distinct unfeathered neck and head, and has white underparts and dark grey upperparts.

Storm Petrels.Name: Swinhoe's Storm Petrel
Storm Petrels.Description: This seabird is entirely dark brown with a short forked tail.

Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Name: Plain Sunbird
Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Description: This rather dull looking sunbird has olive upperparts, greyish underparts and a short bill. Males have a dark blue patch at the base of their beak.

Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Name: Brown-throated Sunbird
Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Description: Males of this species have a beautiful metallic blue crown and back, brown throat and yellow underparts. Females are duller with olive upperparts and yellow underparts. Both sexes have red eyes, female also has distinct split yellow eye-ring.

Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Name: Crimson Sunbird
Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Description: With its bright red plumage (in males), this tiny bird is Singapore's unofficial national bird.

Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Name: Thick-billed Spiderhunter
Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Description: Similarly coloured to the Little Spiderhunter, but without a white throat. Has a split yellow eye-ring.

Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Name: Yellow-eared Spiderhunter
Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Description: This spiderhunter has a bright yellow eyering, ear coverts and underparts. The yellow on the eye-ring and ears is much brighter than that on the underparts.

Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Name: Van Hasselt's Sunbird
Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Description: Males have a metallic purple throat, green crown and deep red underparts. Females are duller olive and have white tips to tail feathers compared to female Crimson Sunbirds.

Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Name: Copper-throated Sunbird
Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Description: Males have a metallic green cap and wings, copper throat and purple-blue belly. Females have grey head and white throat, olive upper parts, yellow underparts and split white, not yellow, eye ring.

Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Name: Olive-backed Sunbird
Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Description: A commonly seen bird that has olive green upperparts and yellow underparts, with male birds possessing a metallic blue bib.

Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Name: Little Spiderhunter
Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Description: This small bird has a long downcurved bill, olive-brown upperparts, whitish throat and yellow underparts.

Swallows and Martins.Name: Sand Martin
Swallows and Martins.Description: This swallow has brown upperparts with white underparts, a brown band across its breast and a forked tail.

Swallows and Martins.Name: Barn Swallow
Swallows and Martins.Description: Similar to the Pacific Swallow but has a breast band. Other differences include clean white underparts and deeper tail fork.

Swallows and Martins.Name: Pacific Swallow
Swallows and Martins.Description: Similar to the Barn Swallow but has lacks a breast band. This species has glossy blue upperparts with orange forehead and throat and a forked tail. Underparts whitish with brownish flanks.

Swallows and Martins.Name: Asian House Martin
Swallows and Martins.Description: This species might look similar to the Sand Martin, but has a white rump and no breast  band. Also has glossy blue, not brown, upperparts.

Swallows and Martins.Name: Red-rumped Swallow
Swallows and Martins.Description: This swallow has a orangey-red rump and nape, and streaked underparts. Rump colour in the migrants that winter here is beige / light pink.

Swifts.Name: White-throated Needletail
Swifts.Description: This species has a distinct white throat and vent when seen from below.

Swifts.Name: Brown-backed Needletail
Swifts.Description: This species has a brown saddle which is less contrasting than that of the silver-backed or white-throated. It also lacks the pale throat patch seen in the other two species.

Swifts.Name: Asian Palm Swift
Swifts.Description: This swift can be recognised by its obvious forked tail and lack of markings on its dark plumage.

Swifts.Name: House Swift
Swifts.Description: This species has a squarish tail, white rump and throat.

Swifts.Name: Plume-toed Swiftlet
Swifts.Description: This species has glossy black upperparts and a whitish underparts with grey scalloping.

Swifts.Name: Black-nest Swiftlet
Swifts.Description: This species is named after its black nests, which are built with saliva and feathers. The similar Germain's swiftlet builds white nests.

Swifts.Name: Germain's Swiftlet
Swifts.Description: This species is easily confused with the Black-nest swiftlet and is practically impossible to differentiate in flight. Germain’s swiftlets build their nests from saliva which are commonly harvested for the Asian delicacy of bird's nest soup.

Swifts.Name: Pacific Swift
Swifts.Description: This species has a white rump and can be distinguished from the House Swift by its deeply forked tail and longer wings.

Thrushes.Name: Eyebrowed Thrush
Thrushes.Description: This thrush species has brown upperparts, a prominent white eyebrow, orange breast and flanks, and white belly. Males have grey head and throat; females have brownish heads.

Thrushes.Name: Orange-headed Thrush
Thrushes.Description: Males of this species have a orange head and underparts, and grey upperparts. Females generally have brownish wash on grey upperparts

Thrushes.Name: Siberian Thrush
Thrushes.Description: This species has a distinct white eyebrow. Males are black while females are brown with white and show numerous scales in the underparts.

Treeswift.Name: Grey-rumped Treeswift
Treeswift.Description: This species has a greyish-green upperparts, and greyish underparts. Males have a rusty-brown patch below their eyes.

Treeswift.Name: Whiskered Treeswift
Treeswift.Description: This species has two distinct white stripes above and below its eyes. Males have a rusty-brown patch below their eyes.

Wagtails and Pipits.Name: Forest Wagtail
Wagtails and Pipits.Description: This wagtail can be easily identified by the bold black and white bars on its wings and breast.

Wagtails and Pipits.Name: White Wagtail
Wagtails and Pipits.Description: Black-and-white pied plumage unique among Singapore’s wagtails. Generally black on crown, upperparts and breast, rest of plumage white. As it is a migrant, all birds in Singapore are in non-breeding plummage.

Wagtails and Pipits.Name: Citrine Wagtail
Wagtails and Pipits.Description: Breeding males have a bright yellow head and underparts, and grey-black upperparts. Non-breeding males and females may be confused with Yellow Wagtail but has yellow on the forehead and ear coverts.

Wagtails and Pipits.Name: Grey Wagtail
Wagtails and Pipits.Description: Has grey and black upperparts and yellow and white underparts. Breeding males of this species have a black throat which is white in females. Non breeding males also have whitish throat. Distinguished from all other wagtails by bright yellow rump and vent.

Wagtails and Pipits.Name: Paddyfield Pipit
Wagtails and Pipits.Description: A rather drab bird with heavily streaked brown upperparts and breast, and lighter brown underparts. Has a dark eyestripe and pale eyebrow.

Wagtails and Pipits.Name: Olive-backed Pipit
Wagtails and Pipits.Description: Has brown upperparts, pale underparts and heavy dark brown streaking on breast. Also has a distinctive ear patch which is white above and black below at the end of white eye-brow.

Wagtails and Pipits.Name: Red-throated Pipit
Wagtails and Pipits.Description: In breeding plumage, this bird has a pink head. In winter, it may look similar to the Olive-backed pipit but has heavy streaking on both under and uppersides. In non breeding plumage, it is unique among local pipits in having a heavily streaked rump.

Wagtails and Pipits.Name: Eastern Yellow Wagtail
Wagtails and Pipits.Description: Breeding males have yellow underparts and blackish wings with variable crown colour. Non-breeding males and females generally have whitish underparts, brownish upperparts and a white eyebrow.

Weavers.Name: Streaked Weaver
Weavers.Description: Breeding males have a yellow cap and a black face and breast is streaked. Females and non-breeding males have yellowish neck patch and eye-brow, and throat and breast is streaked.

Weavers.Name: Baya Weaver
Weavers.Description: Breeding males have yellow cap and dark face, females and non-breeding birds generally brown overall with streaked upperparts. All plumages distinguished from Streaked Weaver by clean underparts.

Whistlers.Name: Mangrove Whistler
Whistlers.Description: This mangrove passerine has dull brown upperparts and whitish underparts. Also has an entire black hooked bill.

White-eyes.Name: Swinhoe's White-Eye
White-eyes.Description: A common garden bird with greenish-yellow head and upperparts, grey underparts, yellow vent and a prominent white eye-ring.

Woodpeckers.Name: Sunda Pygmy Woodpecker
Woodpeckers.Description: This is the smallest woodpecker species in Singapore and is well camouflaged on trees with its brown and white mottled plumage.

Woodpeckers.Name: White-bellied Woodpecker
Woodpeckers.Description: This large woodpecker is black with a white belly and red crest. Males have a red cap, while females have a black cap.

Woodpeckers.Name: Laced Woodpecker
Woodpeckers.Description: This woodpecker is characteristically green. Males have a red cap, while females have a black cap.

Woodpeckers.Name: Buff-rumped Woodpecker
Woodpeckers.Description: So called for the cream patch on its rump. This woodpecker is otherwise identifiable by its finely-barred head and crest, and black and white mottled plumage.

Woodpeckers.Name: Rufous Woodpecker
Woodpeckers.Description: This woodpecker has a rusty-red plumage with black barring on its upperparts.

Woodpeckers.Name: Banded Woodpecker
Woodpeckers.Description: This species has a distinct yellow crest, bright red upperparts and black and white barring on its underparts.

Woodpeckers.Name: Common Flameback
Woodpeckers.Description: Named after its distinctive golden-yellow plumage on its upperparts. Males have a red cap while females have a black cap.

Woodpeckers.Name: Great Slaty Woodpecker
Woodpeckers.Description: Large woodpecker with grey plumage, and a buffy throat. Males have a red cheek stripe.

Apaturinae.Name: Purple Duke
Apaturinae.Description: Underside pale silvery, with two faint eyespots. Males have a black upperside with a white bar while females are primarily brown.

Apaturinae.Name: Courtesan (M)
Apaturinae.Description: Males are black with white streaks and spots on upperside, but chocolate brown on underside. Females take two forms, one resembling the Magpie Crow.

Apaturinae.Name: Courtesan (F)
Apaturinae.Description: This form of the Courtesan mimicks the Magpie Crow, but differ in wing shape and eye colour.

Apaturinae.Name: Purple Duke
Apaturinae.Description: Underside pale silvery, with two faint eyespots. Males have a black upperside with a white bar while females are primarily brown.

Apaturinae.Name: Courtesan (M)
Apaturinae.Description: Males are black with white streaks and spots on upperside, but chocolate brown on underside. Females take two forms, one resembling the Magpie Crow.

Apaturinae.Name: Courtesan (F)
Apaturinae.Description: This form of the Courtesan mimicks the Magpie Crow, but differ in wing shape and eye colour.

Charaxinae.Name: Black Rajah
Charaxinae.Description: Upperside dark brown, and underside grey with reddish brown patches, and two pointed tails typical of Rajahs and Nawabs.

Charaxinae.Name: Plain Nawab
Charaxinae.Description: Similar to the Malayan Nawab, but upperwing forewing margin decreases markedly towards the tornus.

Charaxinae.Name: Blue Nawab
Charaxinae.Description: Upperside bluish black, with a white band across both wings. Underside silvery and marked with brown and purple patterns, setting it apart from other Nawabs.

Charaxinae.Name: Malayan Nawab
Charaxinae.Description: Similar to the Plain Nawab, but upperwing forewing margin does not decrease greatly towards the tornus.

Charaxinae.Name: Black Rajah
Charaxinae.Description: Upperside dark brown, and underside grey with reddish brown patches, and two pointed tails typical of Rajahs and Nawabs.

Charaxinae.Name: Plain Nawab
Charaxinae.Description: Similar to the Malayan Nawab, but upperwing forewing margin decreases markedly towards the tornus.

Charaxinae.Name: Blue Nawab
Charaxinae.Description: Upperside bluish black, with a white band across both wings. Underside silvery and marked with brown and purple patterns, setting it apart from other Nawabs.

Charaxinae.Name: Malayan Nawab
Charaxinae.Description: Similar to the Plain Nawab, but upperwing forewing margin does not decrease greatly towards the tornus.

Coeliadinae.Name: Great Orange Awlet
Coeliadinae.Description: Similar in appearance to the Orange Awlet but larger. Underside orange-brown with pale streaks on both wings. Upperside of males dark brown, while females deep blue.

Coeliadinae.Name: Orange Awlet
Coeliadinae.Description: Similar in appearance to the Great Orange Awlet but much smaller. Underside purplish-brown, streaked with orange. Upperside of males coppery-brown with darkened veins, while females steely blue.

Coeliadinae.Name: Orange-Tail Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: Underside dark brown with a broad white discal band on both wings. Hindwing tornal region diagnostically deep orange.

Coeliadinae.Name: Common Banded Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: Hindwing underside pale brown with a narrow post-discal band, washed with bluish purple.

Coeliadinae.Name: White Banded Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: Hindwing underside fades from bluish-green at the base to purple near the termen. Post-discal band narrow.

Coeliadinae.Name: Yellow Banded Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: Easily distinguished from the other awls by its broad yellow discal band on the underside.

Coeliadinae.Name: Common Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: Underside brown, with a light purplish glaze and a small white spot in the hindwing cell.

Coeliadinae.Name: Plain Banded Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: This awl can be identified from similar species by its broad hindwing post-discal band and a small forewing sub-apical spot.

Coeliadinae.Name: Brown Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: The bold black bands on the abdomen help distinguish it from other awls. Underside pale greyish-brown. Upperside brown with long white translucent streaks in the cell.

Coeliadinae.Name: Great Orange Awlet
Coeliadinae.Description: Similar in appearance to the Orange Awlet but larger. Underside orange-brown with pale streaks on both wings. Upperside of males dark brown, while females deep blue.

Coeliadinae.Name: Orange Awlet
Coeliadinae.Description: Similar in appearance to the Great Orange Awlet but much smaller. Underside purplish-brown, streaked with orange. Upperside of males coppery-brown with darkened veins, while females steely blue.

Coeliadinae.Name: Orange-Tail Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: Underside dark brown with a broad white discal band on both wings. Hindwing tornal region diagnostically deep orange.

Coeliadinae.Name: Common Banded Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: Hindwing underside pale brown with a narrow post-discal band, washed with bluish purple.

Coeliadinae.Name: White Banded Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: Hindwing underside fades from bluish-green at the base to purple near the termen. Post-discal band narrow.

Coeliadinae.Name: Yellow Banded Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: Easily distinguished from the other awls by its broad yellow discal band on the underside.

Coeliadinae.Name: Common Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: Underside brown, with a light purplish glaze and a small white spot in the hindwing cell.

Coeliadinae.Name: Plain Banded Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: This awl can be identified from similar species by its broad hindwing post-discal band and a small forewing sub-apical spot.

Coeliadinae.Name: Brown Awl
Coeliadinae.Description: The bold black bands on the abdomen help distinguish it from other awls. Underside pale greyish-brown. Upperside brown with long white translucent streaks in the cell.

Coliadinae.Name: Mottled Emigrant
Coliadinae.Description: Underside greenish white with faint brown streaks, giving a mottled appearance. Upperside greenish white.

Coliadinae.Name: Lemon Emigrant
Coliadinae.Description: Represented by several forms; varied patterns present on wings. Distinguished from other emigrants by pale yellow or white upperside.

Coliadinae.Name: Orange Emigrant
Coliadinae.Description: Underside pale yellow. Upperside forewing white while hindwing deep orange.

Coliadinae.Name: No Brand Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has no cell spots on underside forewing and many tiny freckles throughout underside.

Coliadinae.Name: Common Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has two cell spots on underside forewing. Forewing underside lacks the large brown apical spot found in the Forest Grass Yellow.

Coliadinae.Name: Forest Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has two cell spots on underside forewing. Forewing underside has a large partially divided, brown apical spot.

Coliadinae.Name: Three Spot Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has three cell spots on underside forewing.

Coliadinae.Name: Anderson’s Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has a single cell spot on underside of forewing.  Unlike the Chocolate Grass Yellow, its forewing apex is not completely darkened on the underside.

Coliadinae.Name: Chocolate Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has a single cell spot on its forewing underside.  Unlike the Anderson's Grass Yellow, its forewing apex is completely darkened on the underside.

Coliadinae.Name: Tree Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has a pale yellow colour on both sides of its wings. Entirely unmarked except for black borders on upperside.

Coliadinae.Name: Grass Yellows
Coliadinae.Description: Small yellow butterflies with irregular black borders on the upperside and small dark spots on the underside.

Coliadinae.Name: Emigrants
Coliadinae.Description: Moderately large

Coliadinae.Name: Mottled Emigrant
Coliadinae.Description: Underside greenish white with faint brown streaks, giving a mottled appearance. Upperside greenish white.

Coliadinae.Name: Lemon Emigrant
Coliadinae.Description: Represented by several forms; varied patterns present on wings. Distinguished from other emigrants by pale yellow or white upperside.

Coliadinae.Name: Orange Emigrant
Coliadinae.Description: Underside pale yellow. Upperside forewing white while hindwing deep orange.

Coliadinae.Name: No Brand Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has no cell spots on underside forewing and many tiny freckles throughout underside.

Coliadinae.Name: Common Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has two cell spots on underside forewing. Forewing underside lacks the large brown apical spot found in the Forest Grass Yellow.

Coliadinae.Name: Forest Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has two cell spots on underside forewing. Forewing underside has a large partially divided, brown apical spot.

Coliadinae.Name: Three Spot Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has three cell spots on underside forewing.

Coliadinae.Name: Anderson’s Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has a single cell spot on underside of forewing.  Unlike the Chocolate Grass Yellow, its forewing apex is not completely darkened on the underside.

Coliadinae.Name: Chocolate Grass Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has a single cell spot on its forewing underside.  Unlike the Anderson's Grass Yellow, its forewing apex is completely darkened on the underside.

Coliadinae.Name: Tree Yellow
Coliadinae.Description: Has a pale yellow colour on both sides of its wings. Entirely unmarked except for black borders on upperside.

Coliadinae.Name: Grass Yellows
Coliadinae.Description: Small yellow butterflies with irregular black borders on the upperside and small dark spots on the underside.

Coliadinae.Name: Emigrants
Coliadinae.Description: Moderately large

Curetinae.Name: Malayan Sunbeam
Curetinae.Description: Underside silvery-white, peppered with small black spots on both wings. Both its upperside and the bands on its legs copper red.

Curetinae.Name: Sumatran Sunbeam
Curetinae.Description: Underside silvery-white, with a line of crescent-shaped markings on both wings. Both its upperside and the bands of its legs orange. The extent and shade of orange colouration differ between sexes.

Curetinae.Name: Malayan Sunbeam
Curetinae.Description: Underside silvery-white, peppered with small black spots on both wings. Both its upperside and the bands on its legs copper red.

Curetinae.Name: Sumatran Sunbeam
Curetinae.Description: Underside silvery-white, with a line of crescent-shaped markings on both wings. Both its upperside and the bands of its legs orange. The extent and shade of orange colouration differ between sexes.

Cyrestinae.Name: Little Maplet
Cyrestinae.Description: Upperside orange-brown, with reddish-brown bands across both wings. Underside paler but similar in marking to upperside.

Cyrestinae.Name: Little Maplet
Cyrestinae.Description: Upperside orange-brown, with reddish-brown bands across both wings. Underside paler but similar in marking to upperside.

Danainae.Name: Plain Tiger
Danainae.Description: The only tiger butterfly in Singapore without veins on both sides of hindwing. Base colour of hindwing can be orange or white.

Danainae.Name: Common Tiger
Danainae.Description: Has strongly-marked dark veins and exists in two forms. Base colour of hindwing can be orange or white. Submarginal bands narrower than Black Veined Tiger

Danainae.Name: Black Veined Tiger
Danainae.Description: Has strongly-marked dark veins. Unlike the Common Tiger, its hindwing is white without any orange. With a broader sub-marginal border than the Common Tiger.

Danainae.Name: Dark Glassy Tiger
Danainae.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly. Resembles the Blue Glassy Tiger, but differs in direction of black streak within its forewing cell.

Danainae.Name: Yellow Glassy Tiger
Danainae.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly with yellow basal patches on each  wing. Mimicked by the Wanderer, but has more prominent colours on underside.

Danainae.Name: Blue Glassy Tiger
Danainae.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly. Resembles the Dark Glassy Tiger, but has a black bar transversing its forewing cell.

Danainae.Name: Grey Glassy Tiger
Danainae.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly. Distinguishable from the rest of the glassy tigers by its large elongate spot on the forewing upperside usually with a thin central black stripe within the spot.

Danainae.Name: Common Tree Nymph
Danainae.Description: A large, white butterfly with black spots and veins. Distinguished from the Mangrove Tree Nymph by its small disjointed spots and absence of black border on its hindwing.

Danainae.Name: Mangrove Tree Nymph
Danainae.Description: A large, white butterfly with black spots and veins. Distinguished from the Common Tree Nymph by its conjointed black spots and black border on its hindwing.

Danainae.Name: Spotted Black Crow
Danainae.Description: Has a prominent patch at forewing apex on its underside consisting of 5 elongated spots. Similar to the Blue Spotted Crow.

Danainae.Name: Malayan Crow
Danainae.Description: Similar to the King Crow, but has smaller inner series of white spots on its underside, especially near apex of forewing.

Danainae.Name: Striped Black Crow
Danainae.Description: Identified by the series of long streaks and spots along margins of its hindwing.

Danainae.Name: Striped Blue Crow (F)
Danainae.Description: Females have striped hindwings on both sides and an iridescent blue patches on forewing apex of the upperside.

Danainae.Name: Striped Blue Crow (M)
Danainae.Description: Has an iridescent blue patch on its forewing apex like the Dwarf Crow, but has more spots on underside.

Danainae.Name: King Crow
Danainae.Description: Similar to the Malayan Crow, but has larger violet-tinged spots on the forewing apex of the upperside.

Danainae.Name: Blue Spotted Crow
Danainae.Description: Prominent patch at forewing apex of the underside comprising 4 elongated spots. Similar to the Spotted Black Crow.

Danainae.Name: Dwarf Crow
Danainae.Description: Iridescent blue patch on forewing apex like the Striped Blue Crow, but primarily unmarked on underside.

Danainae.Name: Magpie Crow
Danainae.Description: Magpie crows exhibit sexual dimorphism, both sexes have characteristic white patch on underside of each wing. Mimicked by the Courtesan, but told apart by its black eyes and round hindwing.

Danainae.Name: Plain Tiger
Danainae.Description: The only tiger butterfly in Singapore without veins on both sides of hindwing. Base colour of hindwing can be orange or white.

Danainae.Name: Common Tiger
Danainae.Description: Has strongly-marked dark veins and exists in two forms. Base colour of hindwing can be orange or white. Submarginal bands narrower than Black Veined Tiger

Danainae.Name: Black Veined Tiger
Danainae.Description: Has strongly-marked dark veins. Unlike the Common Tiger, its hindwing is white without any orange. With a broader sub-marginal border than the Common Tiger.

Danainae.Name: Dark Glassy Tiger
Danainae.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly. Resembles the Blue Glassy Tiger, but differs in direction of black streak within its forewing cell.

Danainae.Name: Yellow Glassy Tiger
Danainae.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly with yellow basal patches on each  wing. Mimicked by the Wanderer, but has more prominent colours on underside.

Danainae.Name: Blue Glassy Tiger
Danainae.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly. Resembles the Dark Glassy Tiger, but has a black bar transversing its forewing cell.

Danainae.Name: Grey Glassy Tiger
Danainae.Description: A black-veined, white butterfly. Distinguishable from the rest of the glassy tigers by its large elongate spot on the forewing upperside usually with a thin central black stripe within the spot.

Danainae.Name: Common Tree Nymph
Danainae.Description: A large, white butterfly with black spots and veins. Distinguished from the Mangrove Tree Nymph by its small disjointed spots and absence of black border on its hindwing.

Danainae.Name: Mangrove Tree Nymph
Danainae.Description: A large, white butterfly with black spots and veins. Distinguished from the Common Tree Nymph by its conjointed black spots and black border on its hindwing.

Danainae.Name: Spotted Black Crow
Danainae.Description: Has a prominent patch at forewing apex on its underside consisting of 5 elongated spots. Similar to the Blue Spotted Crow.

Danainae.Name: Malayan Crow
Danainae.Description: Similar to the King Crow, but has smaller inner series of white spots on its underside, especially near apex of forewing.

Danainae.Name: Striped Black Crow
Danainae.Description: Identified by the series of long streaks and spots along margins of its hindwing.

Danainae.Name: Striped Blue Crow (F)
Danainae.Description: Females have striped hindwings on both sides and an iridescent blue patches on forewing apex of the upperside.

Danainae.Name: Striped Blue Crow (M)
Danainae.Description: Has an iridescent blue patch on its forewing apex like the Dwarf Crow, but has more spots on underside.

Danainae.Name: King Crow
Danainae.Description: Similar to the Malayan Crow, but has larger violet-tinged spots on the forewing apex of the upperside.

Danainae.Name: Blue Spotted Crow
Danainae.Description: Prominent patch at forewing apex of the underside comprising 4 elongated spots. Similar to the Spotted Black Crow.

Danainae.Name: Dwarf Crow
Danainae.Description: Iridescent blue patch on forewing apex like the Striped Blue Crow, but primarily unmarked on underside.

Danainae.Name: Magpie Crow
Danainae.Description: Magpie crows exhibit sexual dimorphism, both sexes have characteristic white patch on underside of each wing. Mimicked by the Courtesan, but told apart by its black eyes and round hindwing.

Heliconiinae.Name: Tawny Coster
Heliconiinae.Description: Orange upperside with a black border and black spots, but paler in females. Its thorax and hindwing border are black with white spots.

Heliconiinae.Name: Malay Lacewing
Heliconiinae.Description: Upperside orange with black borders and a white band. Distinguishable from other lacewings by absence of submarginal white band.

Heliconiinae.Name: Plain Lacewing
Heliconiinae.Description: Upperside orange with black border and white band. Similar to Malay Lacewing, but with submarginal white band along row of short black stripes.

Heliconiinae.Name: Leopard Lacewing
Heliconiinae.Description: Upperside orange with black borders and a white band. Distinguishable from other lacewings from its large spots in submarginal white band.

Heliconiinae.Name: Leopard
Heliconiinae.Description: Orange-brown on upperside with many black spots. Underside a lighter shade of orange with a purplish sheen in the side light.

Heliconiinae.Name: Rustic
Heliconiinae.Description: Orange-brown with a characteristic yellow patch, adjacent to broad black area around the upperside forewing apex. Similar to Branded Yeoman, but with black spots within the yellow patch.

Heliconiinae.Name: Banded Yeoman
Heliconiinae.Description: Orange-brown with a characteristic yellow patch, adjacent to broad black area around the upperside forewing apex. Similar to the Rustic, but without black spots within yellow patch.

Heliconiinae.Name: Malay Yeoman
Heliconiinae.Description: Upperside deep orange with black borders. Underside pale brown with white band adjacent to a series of black spots on the hindwing.

Heliconiinae.Name: Cruiser (M)
Heliconiinae.Description: Males orange-brown on the upperside with eyespots and a short, pointed tail on the hindwing.

Heliconiinae.Name: Cruiser (F)
Heliconiinae.Description: Females pale greenish-grey on the upperside, with eyespots and a short tail on its hindwing. A white band cuts across both wings.

Heliconiinae.Name: Royal Assyrian
Heliconiinae.Description: Upperside rich purple, with a white area on the hindwing. Underside purple-brown, with pale dull blue lines and orange-tinged spots.

Heliconiinae.Name: Tawny Coster
Heliconiinae.Description: Orange upperside with a black border and black spots, but paler in females. Its thorax and hindwing border are black with white spots.

Heliconiinae.Name: Malay Lacewing
Heliconiinae.Description: Upperside orange with black borders and a white band. Distinguishable from other lacewings by absence of submarginal white band.

Heliconiinae.Name: Plain Lacewing
Heliconiinae.Description: Upperside orange with black border and white band. Similar to Malay Lacewing, but with submarginal white band along row of short black stripes.

Heliconiinae.Name: Leopard Lacewing
Heliconiinae.Description: Upperside orange with black borders and a white band. Distinguishable from other lacewings from its large spots in submarginal white band.

Heliconiinae.Name: Leopard
Heliconiinae.Description: Orange-brown on upperside with many black spots. Underside a lighter shade of orange with a purplish sheen in the side light.

Heliconiinae.Name: Rustic
Heliconiinae.Description: Orange-brown with a characteristic yellow patch, adjacent to broad black area around the upperside forewing apex. Similar to Branded Yeoman, but with black spots within the yellow patch.

Heliconiinae.Name: Banded Yeoman
Heliconiinae.Description: Orange-brown with a characteristic yellow patch, adjacent to broad black area around the upperside forewing apex. Similar to the Rustic, but without black spots within yellow patch.

Heliconiinae.Name: Malay Yeoman
Heliconiinae.Description: Upperside deep orange with black borders. Underside pale brown with white band adjacent to a series of black spots on the hindwing.

Heliconiinae.Name: Cruiser (M)
Heliconiinae.Description: Males orange-brown on the upperside with eyespots and a short, pointed tail on the hindwing.

Heliconiinae.Name: Cruiser (F)
Heliconiinae.Description: Females pale greenish-grey on the upperside, with eyespots and a short tail on its hindwing. A white band cuts across both wings.

Heliconiinae.Name: Royal Assyrian
Heliconiinae.Description: Upperside rich purple, with a white area on the hindwing. Underside purple-brown, with pale dull blue lines and orange-tinged spots.

Hesperiinae.Name: Bush Hopper
Hesperiinae.Description: Upperside brown with yellow markings, but reduced and paler in females. Hindwing yellowish and checkered with a dark-brown pattern.

Hesperiinae.Name: Dark Banded Ace

Hesperiinae.Name: White Palm Bob

Hesperiinae.Name: Quedara monteithi monteithi (F)

Limenitidinae.Name: Knight
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside reddish-brown, with narrow white band across both wings. Hindwing with a pale violet blue sub-marginal area, unlike the other subspecies of the Knight.

Limenitidinae.Name: Knight
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside reddish-brown, with a narrow white band across both wings. Hindwing remains reddish brown, unlike the other subspecies of the Knight.

Limenitidinae.Name: Lance Sergeant
Limenitidinae.Description: Cell streak unbroken like the Colour Sergeant, but with its central white band disjointed.

Limenitidinae.Name: Studded Sergeant

Limenitidinae.Name: Dot-Dash Sergeant
Limenitidinae.Description: Cell streak broken into a band and short spot on each side. Abdomen carries a whitish ring, lacks black-centered spots on the underside and has a relatively curved white-spotted margin on forewing upperside.

Limenitidinae.Name: Malay Staff Sergeant
Limenitidinae.Description: Cell streaks constricted twice to form three parts on each side. Abdomen carries a whitish ring.

Limenitidinae.Name: Colour Sergeant (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Cell streak unbroken like the Lance Sergeant. Central band is continuous and markings are bluish-white.

Limenitidinae.Name: Colour Sergeant (F)
Limenitidinae.Description: Lacks a series of orange spots beside its black and orange border like the Common Lascar, but carries a thinner orange line within border. Some forms are dark brown in colour.

Limenitidinae.Name: Colonel
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside orange with dark brown shadings towards the base. Underside similar in markings as above, but greenish-grey towards the base.

Limenitidinae.Name: Common Sailor
Limenitidinae.Description: Cell streak broken into two parts on each side and lack a whitish ring on abdomen like the Short-Banded Sailor. However, its forewing spot is more triangular and it has a golden-brown underside with black and white stripes.

Limenitidinae.Name: Grey Sailor
Limenitidinae.Description: Cell streak broken into a band and short spot on each side. Abdomen carries a whitish ring, lacks black-centered spots on its underside and has a relatively straight white-spotted margin on the forewing upperside.

Limenitidinae.Name: Chocolate Sailor
Limenitidinae.Description: Dark brown above with narrow white stripes.

Limenitidinae.Name: Short Banded Sailor
Limenitidinae.Description: Cell streak broken into two parts on each side and lack a whitish ring on the abdomen like the Common Sailor. However, its forewing spot is rounder than the Common Sailor's.

Limenitidinae.Name: Burmese Lascar
Limenitidinae.Description: A series of evenly-sized orange spots found adjacent to the black and orange border on its upperside.

Limenitidinae.Name: Malayan Lascar
Limenitidinae.Description: A series of orange spots adjacent to the black and orange border on its upperside. One of the spots in the middle broader than the others.

Limenitidinae.Name: Common Lascar
Limenitidinae.Description: Lacks a series of orange spots beside its black and orange border, like some females of the Colour Sergeant. Carries a thicker orange line within border and has marbled and striated underside.

Limenitidinae.Name: Perak Lascar
Limenitidinae.Description: The only lascar with two fine orange lines within black border of the upperside forewing.

Limenitidinae.Name: Common Jester
Limenitidinae.Description: Similar to the lascars, but with a completely black border on its upperside, a short tail and a marbled underside.

Limenitidinae.Name: Malay Viscount
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside light brown, with variable white markings. Sub-marginal dark brown "V-shaped" markings on hindwing are slightly disjointed.

Limenitidinae.Name: Horsfield's Baron (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside of males black, with broad bright blue marginal borders across both wings.

Limenitidinae.Name: Horsfield's Baron (F)
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside of females light brown, with white markings. Sub-marginal dark brown "V-shaped" markings on hindwing are less distinct that those of the Malay Viscount.

Limenitidinae.Name: Malay Baron (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Males of the gardineri morph are dark brown above, lacking the blue hindwing border of the monina morph.

Limenitidinae.Name: Malay Baron
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside brown, with variable white markings. Sub-marginal dark brown "V-shaped" markings on hindwing are conjoined.

Limenitidinae.Name: White Tipped Baron
Limenitidinae.Description: Bluish tinge on upperside forewing helps distinguish from the Baron and the Malay Baron lack. Females have distinctive post-discal white spots.

Limenitidinae.Name: Baron (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside of males dark brown with broad post-discal bands on both wings. Lacks bluish tinge on forewing like in the White Tipped Baron.

Limenitidinae.Name: Baron (F)
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside of females lighter brown, with prominent post-discal white spots. Lacks bluish tinge like in the White Tipped Baron.

Limenitidinae.Name: Green Baron (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Identified by its lighter green tornal area and distinct apical red spots on the upperside hindwing. Underside marked with red spots on both wings.

Limenitidinae.Name: Green Baron (F)
Limenitidinae.Description: Identified from the upperside by the broad white band across both wings and distinct apical red spots in the hindwing. Underside marked with red spots on both wings.

Limenitidinae.Name: Black Tipped Archduke (M)

Limenitidinae.Name: Black Tipped Archduke (F)
Limenitidinae.Description: Similar to the yellow archduke but with bluish scaling on the hindwing underside. It has black-tipped antennae which distinguishes it from the Archduke.

Limenitidinae.Name: Archduke (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Males black above, with a broad black-spotted border on the hindwing, and a pale green border on the forewing. Its orange-tipped antennae distinguishes it from the Black Tipped Archduke.

Limenitidinae.Name: Archduke (F)

Limenitidinae.Name: Yellow Archduke
