Limenitidinae.Description: Cell streak unbroken like the Lance Sergeant. Central band is continuous and markings are bluish-white.

Limenitidinae.Name: Colour Sergeant (F)
Limenitidinae.Description: Lacks a series of orange spots beside its black and orange border like the Common Lascar, but carries a thinner orange line within border. Some forms are dark brown in colour.

Limenitidinae.Name: Colonel
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside orange with dark brown shadings towards the base. Underside similar in markings as above, but greenish-grey towards the base.

Limenitidinae.Name: Common Sailor
Limenitidinae.Description: Cell streak broken into two parts on each side and lack a whitish ring on abdomen like the Short-Banded Sailor. However, its forewing spot is more triangular and it has a golden-brown underside with black and white stripes.

Limenitidinae.Name: Grey Sailor
Limenitidinae.Description: Cell streak broken into a band and short spot on each side. Abdomen carries a whitish ring, lacks black-centered spots on its underside and has a relatively straight white-spotted margin on the forewing upperside.

Limenitidinae.Name: Chocolate Sailor
Limenitidinae.Description: Dark brown above with narrow white stripes.

Limenitidinae.Name: Short Banded Sailor
Limenitidinae.Description: Cell streak broken into two parts on each side and lack a whitish ring on the abdomen like the Common Sailor. However, its forewing spot is rounder than the Common Sailor's.

Limenitidinae.Name: Burmese Lascar
Limenitidinae.Description: A series of evenly-sized orange spots found adjacent to the black and orange border on its upperside.

Limenitidinae.Name: Malayan Lascar
Limenitidinae.Description: A series of orange spots adjacent to the black and orange border on its upperside. One of the spots in the middle broader than the others.

Limenitidinae.Name: Common Lascar
Limenitidinae.Description: Lacks a series of orange spots beside its black and orange border, like some females of the Colour Sergeant. Carries a thicker orange line within border and has marbled and striated underside.

Limenitidinae.Name: Perak Lascar
Limenitidinae.Description: The only lascar with two fine orange lines within black border of the upperside forewing.

Limenitidinae.Name: Common Jester
Limenitidinae.Description: Similar to the lascars, but with a completely black border on its upperside, a short tail and a marbled underside.

Limenitidinae.Name: Malay Viscount
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside light brown, with variable white markings. Sub-marginal dark brown "V-shaped" markings on hindwing are slightly disjointed.

Limenitidinae.Name: Horsfield's Baron (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside of males black, with broad bright blue marginal borders across both wings.

Limenitidinae.Name: Horsfield's Baron (F)
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside of females light brown, with white markings. Sub-marginal dark brown "V-shaped" markings on hindwing are less distinct that those of the Malay Viscount.

Limenitidinae.Name: Malay Baron (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Males of the gardineri morph are dark brown above, lacking the blue hindwing border of the monina morph.

Limenitidinae.Name: Malay Baron
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside brown, with variable white markings. Sub-marginal dark brown "V-shaped" markings on hindwing are conjoined.

Limenitidinae.Name: White Tipped Baron
Limenitidinae.Description: Bluish tinge on upperside forewing helps distinguish from the Baron and the Malay Baron lack. Females have distinctive post-discal white spots.

Limenitidinae.Name: Baron (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside of males dark brown with broad post-discal bands on both wings. Lacks bluish tinge on forewing like in the White Tipped Baron.

Limenitidinae.Name: Baron (F)
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside of females lighter brown, with prominent post-discal white spots. Lacks bluish tinge like in the White Tipped Baron.

Limenitidinae.Name: Green Baron (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Identified by its lighter green tornal area and distinct apical red spots on the upperside hindwing. Underside marked with red spots on both wings.

Limenitidinae.Name: Green Baron (F)
Limenitidinae.Description: Identified from the upperside by the broad white band across both wings and distinct apical red spots in the hindwing. Underside marked with red spots on both wings.

Limenitidinae.Name: Black Tipped Archduke (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Males black above, with a broad black-spotted border on the hindwing, and a pale green border on the forewing. Its black-tipped antennae distinguishes it from the Archduke.

Limenitidinae.Name: Black Tipped Archduke (F)
Limenitidinae.Description: Similar to the yellow archduke but with bluish scaling on the hindwing underside. It has black-tipped antennae which distinguishes it from the Archduke.

Limenitidinae.Name: Archduke (M)
Limenitidinae.Description: Males black above, with a broad black-spotted border on the hindwing, and a pale green border on the forewing. Its orange-tipped antennae distinguishes it from the Black Tipped Archduke.

Limenitidinae.Name: Archduke (F)
Limenitidinae.Description: Similar to the Yellow Archduke, but with bluish scaling on the underside hindwings. It has orange-tipped antennae which distinguishes it from the Black Tipped Archduke.

Limenitidinae.Name: Yellow Archduke
Limenitidinae.Description: Upperside of both sexes dark brown, with yellow spots on both wings. Differs from the females of the other archdukes in its yellowish scaling on the underside of its hindwing.

Limenitidinae.Name: Sergeants and Sailors
Limenitidinae.Description: Medium-sized butterflies with white bands across a dark ground colour on the upperside.

Limenitidinae.Name: Lascars and Jesters
Limenitidinae.Description: Medium-sized butterflies with orange bands across a dark ground colour on the upperside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Pierrot
Lycaeninae.Description: A black and white butterfly. More small black spots on its underside than the Elbowed Pierrot.

Lycaeninae.Name: Elbowed Pierrot
Lycaeninae.Description: A black and white butterfly. Few black bands and patches on its underside compared to the Common Pierrot.

Lycaeninae.Name: Indian Cupid
Lycaeninae.Description: Has long white-tipped tails and several black spots on the hindwing besides the two orange-crowned, black tornal spots. One of the black spots close to and above the post-discal spots.

Lycaeninae.Name: The Quaker
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside pure white, with light submarginal markings and a distinctive large black circular spot on the hindwing costa. Upperside blackish-brown, with a white patch that may be absent in males.

Lycaeninae.Name: The Malayan
Lycaeninae.Description: Very similar to the Common Hedge Blue, but brown on the upperside, has a small tail, and has its black outer spot clear of the submarginal markings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Hedge Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Very similar to the Malayan, but shining blue on the upperside, lacks a tail, has a small black spot at the base on the underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Lesser Grass Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside purplish-blue in males, while brown in females. The misaligned spot in the hindwing helps distinguish it from other grass blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pygmy Grass Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside of males dull blue, while dark brown in females. The V-shaped marking on the forewing sub-apical region helps distinguish it from other grass blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pale Grass Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside of males light blue, while dark greyish-blue in females. The more pronounced spots on the underside, particularly the sub-marginal spots along both wings help distinguish it from the other grass blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Cycad Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has long white-tipped tails and several black spots on the hindwing besides the two black tornal spots, only one of which is orange-crowned. One of the hindwing black spots close to and above the post-discal spots.

Lycaeninae.Name: Gram Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has long white-tipped tails and several black spots on the hindwing besides the two orange-crowned, black tornal spots. The black spot close to the post-discal spots is further inwards than in the Indian Cupid.

Lycaeninae.Name: Forget-Me-Not
Lycaeninae.Description: Has a black spot on the forewing costa between the cell spot and post-discal band, in addition to the typical black spots in certain blue butterflies.

Lycaeninae.Name: Silver Forget-Me-Not
Lycaeninae.Description: Has a black spot on the forewing costa close to the post-discal band, in addition to the typical black spots in certain blue butterflies.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pea Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside buff brown, with white streaks of varying thickness.

Lycaeninae.Name: Dark Caerulean
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. The smallest of all Caeruleans, with less distinct white markings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Metallic Caerulean
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. Distinguished from other caeruleans by the acute V-shaped white marking in the hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Caerulean
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside aligned to form continuous lines, like in the Malaccan Caerulean. However, white bands in hindwing mostly disjointed.

Lycaeninae.Name: Malaccan Caerulean
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on forewing underside aligned to form continuous lines, like in the Common Caerulean. Distinguishable from the latter by its thick continuous lines in the hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Sky Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. Difficult to distinguish from the Glistening Caerulean.

Lycaeninae.Name: Glistening Caerulean
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. Difficult to distinguish from the Sky Blue.

Lycaeninae.Name: White Fourline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Has a distinctive sub-apical spot in the hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Jewel Fourline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Lacks a subapical spot. Postdiscal bands unicolorous and same as the ground colour. Striae broad, diffuse and yellowish.

Lycaeninae.Name: Large Fourline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Lacks a subapical spot. Postdiscal bands unicolorous and same as the ground colour. Striae narrow and well-defined.

Lycaeninae.Name: Singapore Fourline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Lacks a subapical spot. Postdiscal bands inwardly bound by darker lines.

Lycaeninae.Name: Opaque Sixline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has an additional pair of sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, unlike in the fourline blues. Easily confused with other sixline blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Rounded Sixline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has an additional pair of sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, unlike in the fourline blues. Easily confused with other sixline blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Dark Malayan Sixline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has an additional pair of sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, unlike in the fourline blues. Easily confused with other sixline blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Two Spotted Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailless. Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other Fourline Blues. Unique in having 2 black spots at the tornal region of its hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pointed Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed. Easily confused with several other Lycaenids.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside orange-yellow in males while greyish-beige in females.

Lycaeninae.Name: Tailless Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailless, with a rather large tornal spot on the underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Barred Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed. Easily confused with several other Lycaenids.

Lycaeninae.Name: Banded Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailless, with one black sub-apical black spot and two uncrowned black spots in the tornal region on the hindwing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Ancyra Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: The orange crowns on the tornal region uniquely separated from the rest of the wings by black curved lines.

Lycaeninae.Name: Dingy Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailless, with two uncrowned black spots in the tornal region on the hindwing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Ciliate Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Posseses short fine tails like the Pointed Ciliate Blue. Underside carries prominent black spot on hindwing dorsum.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pointed Ciliate Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Posseses short fine tails like the Ciliate Blue. Underside carries two black spots on the hindwing, near the costa and dorsum respectively.

Lycaeninae.Name: Club Silverline
Lycaeninae.Description: Bands surrounding silver streaks are usually black, but occasionally red. Upperside greyish-blue but variable. Key distinguishing characteristic is the shape of the basal streak on the forewing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Long Banded Silverline
Lycaeninae.Description: Bands surrounding silver streaks are red. Upperside of males deep blue, while females brown. Key distinguishing characteristic is the L-shaped basal streak on the forewing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Centaur Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Can be immediately separated from the other oakblues by the silvery-green edging in the cell markings on the forewing underside. One of the largest oakblues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Malayan Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Identifiable by its white markings on its reddish-brown underside, which shows a purplish wash in the side light.

Lycaeninae.Name: Large Metallic Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Tailed Disc Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from the Common Disc Oakblue in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Disc Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from the Tailed Disc Oakblue in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Arhopala amphimuta amphimuta
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from Arhopala major major in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Arhopala major major
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from Arhopala amphimuta amphimuta in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Small Tailless Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Raffles' Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Can be identified from other oakblues by its alternately arranged spots making up the postdiscal band on the underside forewing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Vinous Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Sylhet Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has a distinctively-shaped spot above the hindwing cell on the underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Green Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Can be identified from other oakblues by the outwardly displaced spot of the postdiscal band on the underside forewing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Arhopala aurea
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Arhopala trogon
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Arhopala ammon ammon
Lycaeninae.Description: This oakblue is characterised by the large white spot in the middle of the hindwing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Aberrant Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: This oakblue is brown on the underside, but with a series of cryptic markings in grey, black and brown giving it a distinctive appearance.

Lycaeninae.Name: Bifid Plushblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed. Distinctive dark, bifid (cleft) costal spot on the hindwing underside. Pale markings contrast strongly against the brown ground colour.

Lycaeninae.Name: Shining Plushblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed. On the hindwing underside, the mid-costal spot continues downwards as a dark band. Violet markings contrast strongly against the brown ground colour.

Lycaeninae.Name: Darky Plushblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailless. Underside mostly dark purple-brown with uncontrasted markings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Plain Plushblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed, with diagnostic dark red patches at the bases of the costa on both wings. Underside dark brown with pale purple markings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Semanga superba deliciosa
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside buff brown, with a narrow reddish-brown post-discal line. Tornal area of hindwing red, black and metallic in colour.

Lycaeninae.Name: Acacia Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside brown, with small obscure dark spots and dark submarginal lines. Upperside of males deep purple-blue, while females are steely blue.

Lycaeninae.Name: Scarce Silverstreak
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside brown, with broad white streaks and spots. Upperside of males shining blue with broad black forewing border, while brown and unmarked in females.

Lycaeninae.Name: Spotted Silverstreak
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside brown, with slighly darkened patches and white markings on both wings. Upperside of males purple, while steely blue in females.

Lycaeninae.Name: Gray Tinsel
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside pale grey, with brown and silver markings broken into several irregular spots. Upperside of males purple, while light blue in females.

Lycaeninae.Name: Yamfly
Lycaeninae.Description: Its hindwing extends to a filamentous tail, giving it a distinctive shape. Upperside bright orange with black apical border, while underside yellowish buff.

Lycaeninae.Name: Branded Imperial
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly orange, with a white tornal area edged by post-discal black lines. Upperside black.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Imperial
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside white, with the apical area of hindwing and most of the forewing orange.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Posy
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside forewing orange and hindwing white with black bands like other posies, but its hindwing lacks both the orange submarginal band of the Pygmy Posy and the white-filled black bands of the Dark Posy.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pygmy Posy
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside forewing orange and hindwing white with black bands like other posies. Identified by its orange submarginal band extending midway up the hindwing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Dark Posy
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside forewing orange and hindwing white with black bands like other posies. Identified by its white-filled black bands on the hindwing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Ambon Onyx
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside brownish yellow, with a white transverse line across both wings. Upperside bright blue with a broad black border and a white discal spot on the forewing.

Lycaeninae.Name: White Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside greyish-white, with a post-discal series of narrow black streaks. Similar to the Peacock Royal, but has black-spotted green eyes.

Lycaeninae.Name: Peacock Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside greyish-white, with a post-discal series of narrow black streaks. Similar to the White Royal, but has black eyes.

Lycaeninae.Name: Felder's Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside greyish-brown, with two orange-crowned black spots like Tajuria dominus dominus, but underside forewing post-discal line closer to termen than to end-cell. Upperside bright blue.

Lycaeninae.Name: Tajuria dominus dominus
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside greyish-brown, with two orange-crowned black spots like Felder's Royal, but underside forewing post-discal line closer to end-cell than to termen. Upperside bright blue.

Lycaeninae.Name: Banded Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside white, with a broad purple-brown border. Upperside of males shining blue, while females brown.

Lycaeninae.Name: Great Imperial
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly orange, with partially white hindwing ending in a sword-like tail. Black spots limited to tornal half of hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Grand Imperial
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly orange, with partially white hindwing. Posesses the longest tail among the imperials. Black markings extend further along the termen than in the Great Imperial.

Lycaeninae.Name: Green Imperial
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly orange, with a partially white hindwing and a relatively short tail. Black markings extend further along the termen than the Great Imperial. Upperside shining bluish-green.

Lycaeninae.Name: Chocolate Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside dark brown, with a dark narrow post-discal line on both wings. Has two black tornal spots and metallic-green scaling on its hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Golden Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Forewing underside golden-yellow and unmarked. Has two black tornal spots and metallic-green scaling on the hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Silver Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside silvery on both wings. Has two black tornal spots adjacent to the orange patch on its hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Dark Tit
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly white, with a black-spotted orange tornal area. A short orange bar on the hindwing helps tell it apart it from the other tits.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Tit
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly white, resembling the Dark Tit and the Narrow Spark. However, it lacks the orange bar in the hindwing of the Dark Tit and has two tails, unlike the Narrow Spark.

Lycaeninae.Name: Fluffy Tit
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside white, with most of forewing and apical area of hindwing orange-brown. Has a prominent black spot on the hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Cornelian
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside greyish brown with broad, white-edged bands. Males deep orange-red above whilst females dark brown and unmarked.

Lycaeninae.Name: Eliot's Cornelian
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside light grey, with rounded post-discal spots outlined in white. Males duller red on the upperside than the Cornelian whilst females have a faint brown marking in the hindwings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pitcher Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed. Can be identified by the series of V-shaped markings making up the submarginal bands.

Lycaeninae.Name: Narrow Spark
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly white like in the Common Tit, but has one tail, unlike in the Common Tit.

Lycaeninae.Name: The Plane (M)
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside of males deep black-brown, with a pale yellow tornal area. Underside yellowish brown, with black and dark brown spots.

Lycaeninae.Name: The Plane (F)
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside of females reddish-brown, with black spots in a whitened tornal area. Underside whitish, with black spots and stripes on the hindwing and orange bands on the forewing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Yellow Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside bright yellow with black markings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Suffused Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside slightly orange-yellow, with an faint outwardly whitened post-discal line. Upperside of males orange-red, with well-defined black forewing apical borders extending to the dorsum, while females brown and unmarked.

Lycaeninae.Name: Copper Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Distinguished from other flashes by the absence of orange crown around its tornal spot. It usually has additional bars on the underside of both wings. Upperside of males reddish-brown, while females blue.

Lycaeninae.Name: Scarlet Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside of males orange-red, with well-defined black forewing apical borders extending to the dorsum, hindwings with black patch. Upperside of females brown and unmarked; difficult to tell apart from some other flashes.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Red Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Distinguished from other flashes on its underside by its outwardly whitened post-discal line. Upperside of males orange-red, with well-defined black apical borders on forewings that do not extend to the dorsum, while females brown and unmarked.

Lycaeninae.Name: Slate Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside blue in both sexes. Similar to Indigo Flash, but with narrower bands and fainter purple wash on its light brown underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Indigo Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside blue in both sexes. Similar to Slate Flash, but with broader bands and stronger purple wash on its dark brown underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Oakblues
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside a shade of brown with pale streaks, while upperside a shade of shining blue or purple.

Lycaeninae.Name: Grass Blues
Lycaeninae.Description: Extremely small butterflies with a black spotted pale grey underside. Upperside blue or brown depending on sex and species.

Lycaeninae.Name: Blues and Caeruleans
Lycaeninae.Description: The group of butterflies with a shining blue or brown upperside and grey undersides marked with streaks and bands.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Pierrot
Lycaeninae.Description: A black and white butterfly. More small black spots on its underside than the Elbowed Pierrot.

Lycaeninae.Name: Elbowed Pierrot
Lycaeninae.Description: A black and white butterfly. Few black bands and patches on its underside compared to the Common Pierrot.

Lycaeninae.Name: Indian Cupid
Lycaeninae.Description: Has long white-tipped tails and several black spots on the hindwing besides the two orange-crowned, black tornal spots. One of the black spots close to and above the post-discal spots.

Lycaeninae.Name: The Quaker
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside pure white, with light submarginal markings and a distinctive large black circular spot on the hindwing costa. Upperside blackish-brown, with a white patch that may be absent in males.

Lycaeninae.Name: The Malayan
Lycaeninae.Description: Very similar to the Common Hedge Blue, but brown on the upperside, has a small tail, and has its black outer spot clear of the submarginal markings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Hedge Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Very similar to the Malayan, but shining blue on the upperside, lacks a tail, has a small black spot at the base on the underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Lesser Grass Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside purplish-blue in males, while brown in females. The misaligned spot in the hindwing helps distinguish it from other grass blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pygmy Grass Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside of males dull blue, while dark brown in females. The V-shaped marking on the forewing sub-apical region helps distinguish it from other grass blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pale Grass Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside of males light blue, while dark greyish-blue in females. The more pronounced spots on the underside, particularly the sub-marginal spots along both wings help distinguish it from the other grass blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Cycad Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has long white-tipped tails and several black spots on the hindwing besides the two black tornal spots, only one of which is orange-crowned. One of the hindwing black spots close to and above the post-discal spots.

Lycaeninae.Name: Gram Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has long white-tipped tails and several black spots on the hindwing besides the two orange-crowned, black tornal spots. The black spot close to the post-discal spots is further inwards than in the Indian Cupid.

Lycaeninae.Name: Forget-Me-Not
Lycaeninae.Description: Has a black spot on the forewing costa between the cell spot and post-discal band, in addition to the typical black spots in certain blue butterflies.

Lycaeninae.Name: Silver Forget-Me-Not
Lycaeninae.Description: Has a black spot on the forewing costa close to the post-discal band, in addition to the typical black spots in certain blue butterflies.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pea Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside buff brown, with white streaks of varying thickness.

Lycaeninae.Name: Dark Caerulean
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. The smallest of all Caeruleans, with less distinct white markings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Metallic Caerulean
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. Distinguished from other caeruleans by the acute V-shaped white marking in the hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Caerulean
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside aligned to form continuous lines, like in the Malaccan Caerulean. However, white bands in hindwing mostly disjointed.

Lycaeninae.Name: Malaccan Caerulean
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on forewing underside aligned to form continuous lines, like in the Common Caerulean. Distinguishable from the latter by its thick continuous lines in the hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Sky Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. Difficult to distinguish from the Glistening Caerulean.

Lycaeninae.Name: Glistening Caerulean
Lycaeninae.Description: The postdiscal bands on the forewing underside curved. Difficult to distinguish from the Sky Blue.

Lycaeninae.Name: White Fourline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Has a distinctive sub-apical spot in the hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Jewel Fourline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Lacks a subapical spot. Postdiscal bands unicolorous and same as the ground colour. Striae broad, diffuse and yellowish.

Lycaeninae.Name: Large Fourline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Lacks a subapical spot. Postdiscal bands unicolorous and same as the ground colour. Striae narrow and well-defined.

Lycaeninae.Name: Singapore Fourline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other fourline blues. Lacks a subapical spot. Postdiscal bands inwardly bound by darker lines.

Lycaeninae.Name: Opaque Sixline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has an additional pair of sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, unlike in the fourline blues. Easily confused with other sixline blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Rounded Sixline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has an additional pair of sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, unlike in the fourline blues. Easily confused with other sixline blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Dark Malayan Sixline Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has an additional pair of sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, unlike in the fourline blues. Easily confused with other sixline blues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Two Spotted Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailless. Without sub-basal lines in the underside forewing cell, like other Fourline Blues. Unique in having 2 black spots at the tornal region of its hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pointed Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed. Easily confused with several other Lycaenids.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside orange-yellow in males while greyish-beige in females.

Lycaeninae.Name: Tailless Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailless, with a rather large tornal spot on the underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Barred Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed. Easily confused with several other Lycaenids.

Lycaeninae.Name: Banded Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailless, with one black sub-apical black spot and two uncrowned black spots in the tornal region on the hindwing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Ancyra Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: The orange crowns on the tornal region uniquely separated from the rest of the wings by black curved lines.

Lycaeninae.Name: Dingy Line Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailless, with two uncrowned black spots in the tornal region on the hindwing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Ciliate Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Posseses short fine tails like the Pointed Ciliate Blue. Underside carries prominent black spot on hindwing dorsum.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pointed Ciliate Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Posseses short fine tails like the Ciliate Blue. Underside carries two black spots on the hindwing, near the costa and dorsum respectively.

Lycaeninae.Name: Club Silverline
Lycaeninae.Description: Bands surrounding silver streaks are usually black, but occasionally red. Upperside greyish-blue but variable. Key distinguishing characteristic is the shape of the basal streak on the forewing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Long Banded Silverline
Lycaeninae.Description: Bands surrounding silver streaks are red. Upperside of males deep blue, while females brown. Key distinguishing characteristic is the L-shaped basal streak on the forewing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Centaur Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Can be immediately separated from the other oakblues by the silvery-green edging in the cell markings on the forewing underside. One of the largest oakblues.

Lycaeninae.Name: Malayan Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Identifiable by its white markings on its reddish-brown underside, which shows a purplish wash in the side light.

Lycaeninae.Name: Large Metallic Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Tailed Disc Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from the Common Disc Oakblue in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Disc Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from the Tailed Disc Oakblue in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Arhopala amphimuta amphimuta
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from Arhopala major major in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Arhopala major major
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from Arhopala amphimuta amphimuta in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Small Tailless Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Raffles' Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Can be identified from other oakblues by its alternately arranged spots making up the postdiscal band on the underside forewing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Vinous Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Sylhet Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Has a distinctively-shaped spot above the hindwing cell on the underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Green Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Can be identified from other oakblues by the outwardly displaced spot of the postdiscal band on the underside forewing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Arhopala aurea
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Arhopala trogon
Lycaeninae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from some of the oakblues in the field.

Lycaeninae.Name: Arhopala ammon ammon
Lycaeninae.Description: This oakblue is characterised by the large white spot in the middle of the hindwing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Aberrant Oakblue
Lycaeninae.Description: This oakblue is brown on the underside, but with a series of cryptic markings in grey, black and brown giving it a distinctive appearance.

Lycaeninae.Name: Bifid Plushblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed. Distinctive dark, bifid (cleft) costal spot on the hindwing underside. Pale markings contrast strongly against the brown ground colour.

Lycaeninae.Name: Shining Plushblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed. On the hindwing underside, the mid-costal spot continues downwards as a dark band. Violet markings contrast strongly against the brown ground colour.

Lycaeninae.Name: Darky Plushblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailless. Underside mostly dark purple-brown with uncontrasted markings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Plain Plushblue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed, with diagnostic dark red patches at the bases of the costa on both wings. Underside dark brown with pale purple markings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Semanga superba deliciosa
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside buff brown, with a narrow reddish-brown post-discal line. Tornal area of hindwing red, black and metallic in colour.

Lycaeninae.Name: Acacia Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside brown, with small obscure dark spots and dark submarginal lines. Upperside of males deep purple-blue, while females are steely blue.

Lycaeninae.Name: Scarce Silverstreak
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside brown, with broad white streaks and spots. Upperside of males shining blue with broad black forewing border, while brown and unmarked in females.

Lycaeninae.Name: Spotted Silverstreak
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside brown, with slighly darkened patches and white markings on both wings. Upperside of males purple, while steely blue in females.

Lycaeninae.Name: Gray Tinsel
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside pale grey, with brown and silver markings broken into several irregular spots. Upperside of males purple, while light blue in females.

Lycaeninae.Name: Yamfly
Lycaeninae.Description: Its hindwing extends to a filamentous tail, giving it a distinctive shape. Upperside bright orange with black apical border, while underside yellowish buff.

Lycaeninae.Name: Branded Imperial
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly orange, with a white tornal area edged by post-discal black lines. Upperside black.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Imperial
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside white, with the apical area of hindwing and most of the forewing orange.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Posy
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside forewing orange and hindwing white with black bands like other posies, but its hindwing lacks both the orange submarginal band of the Pygmy Posy and the white-filled black bands of the Dark Posy.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pygmy Posy
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside forewing orange and hindwing white with black bands like other posies. Identified by its orange submarginal band extending midway up the hindwing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Dark Posy
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside forewing orange and hindwing white with black bands like other posies. Identified by its white-filled black bands on the hindwing underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Ambon Onyx
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside brownish yellow, with a white transverse line across both wings. Upperside bright blue with a broad black border and a white discal spot on the forewing.

Lycaeninae.Name: White Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside greyish-white, with a post-discal series of narrow black streaks. Similar to the Peacock Royal, but has black-spotted green eyes.

Lycaeninae.Name: Peacock Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside greyish-white, with a post-discal series of narrow black streaks. Similar to the White Royal, but has black eyes.

Lycaeninae.Name: Felder's Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside greyish-brown, with two orange-crowned black spots like Tajuria dominus dominus, but underside forewing post-discal line closer to termen than to end-cell. Upperside bright blue.

Lycaeninae.Name: Tajuria dominus dominus
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside greyish-brown, with two orange-crowned black spots like Felder's Royal, but underside forewing post-discal line closer to end-cell than to termen. Upperside bright blue.

Lycaeninae.Name: Banded Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside white, with a broad purple-brown border. Upperside of males shining blue, while females brown.

Lycaeninae.Name: Great Imperial
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly orange, with partially white hindwing ending in a sword-like tail. Black spots limited to tornal half of hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Grand Imperial
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly orange, with partially white hindwing. Posesses the longest tail among the imperials. Black markings extend further along the termen than in the Great Imperial.

Lycaeninae.Name: Green Imperial
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly orange, with a partially white hindwing and a relatively short tail. Black markings extend further along the termen than the Great Imperial. Upperside shining bluish-green.

Lycaeninae.Name: Chocolate Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside dark brown, with a dark narrow post-discal line on both wings. Has two black tornal spots and metallic-green scaling on its hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Golden Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Forewing underside golden-yellow and unmarked. Has two black tornal spots and metallic-green scaling on the hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Silver Royal
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside silvery on both wings. Has two black tornal spots adjacent to the orange patch on its hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Dark Tit
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly white, with a black-spotted orange tornal area. A short orange bar on the hindwing helps tell it apart it from the other tits.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Tit
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly white, resembling the Dark Tit and the Narrow Spark. However, it lacks the orange bar in the hindwing of the Dark Tit and has two tails, unlike the Narrow Spark.

Lycaeninae.Name: Fluffy Tit
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside white, with most of forewing and apical area of hindwing orange-brown. Has a prominent black spot on the hindwing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Cornelian
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside greyish brown with broad, white-edged bands. Males deep orange-red above whilst females dark brown and unmarked.

Lycaeninae.Name: Eliot's Cornelian
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside light grey, with rounded post-discal spots outlined in white. Males duller red on the upperside than the Cornelian whilst females have a faint brown marking in the hindwings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Pitcher Blue
Lycaeninae.Description: Tailed. Can be identified by the series of V-shaped markings making up the submarginal bands.

Lycaeninae.Name: Narrow Spark
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside mostly white like in the Common Tit, but has one tail, unlike in the Common Tit.

Lycaeninae.Name: The Plane (M)
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside of males deep black-brown, with a pale yellow tornal area. Underside yellowish brown, with black and dark brown spots.

Lycaeninae.Name: The Plane (F)
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside of females reddish-brown, with black spots in a whitened tornal area. Underside whitish, with black spots and stripes on the hindwing and orange bands on the forewing.

Lycaeninae.Name: Yellow Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside bright yellow with black markings.

Lycaeninae.Name: Suffused Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside slightly orange-yellow, with an faint outwardly whitened post-discal line. Upperside of males orange-red, with well-defined black forewing apical borders extending to the dorsum, while females brown and unmarked.

Lycaeninae.Name: Copper Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Distinguished from other flashes by the absence of orange crown around its tornal spot. It usually has additional bars on the underside of both wings. Upperside of males reddish-brown, while females blue.

Lycaeninae.Name: Scarlet Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside of males orange-red, with well-defined black forewing apical borders extending to the dorsum, hindwings with black patch. Upperside of females brown and unmarked; difficult to tell apart from some other flashes.

Lycaeninae.Name: Common Red Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Distinguished from other flashes on its underside by its outwardly whitened post-discal line. Upperside of males orange-red, with well-defined black apical borders on forewings that do not extend to the dorsum, while females brown and unmarked.

Lycaeninae.Name: Slate Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside blue in both sexes. Similar to Indigo Flash, but with narrower bands and fainter purple wash on its light brown underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Indigo Flash
Lycaeninae.Description: Upperside blue in both sexes. Similar to Slate Flash, but with broader bands and stronger purple wash on its dark brown underside.

Lycaeninae.Name: Oakblues
Lycaeninae.Description: Underside a shade of brown with pale streaks, while upperside a shade of shining blue or purple.

Lycaeninae.Name: Grass Blues
Lycaeninae.Description: Extremely small butterflies with a black spotted pale grey underside. Upperside blue or brown depending on sex and species.

Lycaeninae.Name: Blues and Caeruleans
Lycaeninae.Description: The group of butterflies with a shining blue or brown upperside and grey undersides marked with streaks and bands.

Miletinae.Name: Moth Butterfly
Miletinae.Description: Has a uniquely deformed appearance. Wings brownish-orange on the upperside with black borders, while purple-brown on the underside.

Miletinae.Name: Miletus gopara gopara
Miletinae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from Bigg's Brownie in the field, has a tail.

Miletinae.Name: Bigg's Brownie
Miletinae.Description: Similar in appearance to the Blue Brownie on its underside. However, its upperside is light brown with an oblique white band.

Miletinae.Name: Blue Brownie
Miletinae.Description: Similar in appearance to the Bigg's Brownie on its underside. However, its forewing upperside is whitish, with a broad dark apical area, while its hindwing is light bluish-grey.

Miletinae.Name: Lesser Darkie
Miletinae.Description: Upperside dark brown and unmarked. Underside primarily greyish-white with striations ranging from dark brown to light greyish-brown.

Miletinae.Name: Pale Mottle
Miletinae.Description: Underside with a distinct, irregularly marked and mottled appearance. Upperside is bluish grey with a black apex.

Miletinae.Name: Apefly
Miletinae.Description: Underside greyish buff with dark striations and a clearly defined brown-edged white spot in the forewing cell. Upperside is dark brown and unmarked, except for a small whitish patch in the middle of the forewing.

Miletinae.Name: Moth Butterfly
Miletinae.Description: Has a uniquely deformed appearance. Wings brownish-orange on the upperside with black borders, while purple-brown on the underside.

Miletinae.Name: Miletus gopara gopara
Miletinae.Description: Difficult to distinguish from Bigg's Brownie in the field, has a tail.

Miletinae.Name: Bigg's Brownie
Miletinae.Description: Similar in appearance to the Blue Brownie on its underside. However, its upperside is light brown with an oblique white band.

Miletinae.Name: Blue Brownie
Miletinae.Description: Similar in appearance to the Bigg's Brownie on its underside. However, its forewing upperside is whitish, with a broad dark apical area, while its hindwing is light bluish-grey.

Miletinae.Name: Lesser Darkie
Miletinae.Description: Upperside dark brown and unmarked. Underside primarily greyish-white with striations ranging from dark brown to light greyish-brown.

Miletinae.Name: Pale Mottle
Miletinae.Description: Underside with a distinct, irregularly marked and mottled appearance. Upperside is bluish grey with a black apex.

Miletinae.Name: Apefly
Miletinae.Description: Underside greyish buff with dark striations and a clearly defined brown-edged white spot in the forewing cell. Upperside is dark brown and unmarked, except for a small whitish patch in the middle of the forewing.

Morphinae.Name: Common Faun
Morphinae.Description: Deep brown underside with a series of small white spots and dark lines across both wings. Upperside is orange-brown.

Morphinae.Name: Palm King
Morphinae.Description: Multiple brown bands across both wings, each separated by thin white streaks. Hindwing also contains two widely separated eyespots.

Morphinae.Name: Saturn
Morphinae.Description: Underside resembles a leaf, with two large hindwing eyespots and a dark central line. Males have iridescent blue patches on uppersides, which are absent in females.

Morphinae.Name: Dark Blue Jungle Glory
Morphinae.Description: Underside dark brown, with several white streaks and two prominent black-filled eyespots. Males have a greater extent of blue patches on the upperside.

Morphinae.Name: Common Duffer
Morphinae.Description: Has a dark central line and two hindwing eyespots on a mottled brown underside. Few bluish spots on upperside of males, while females have a series of pale orange and whitish spots.

Morphinae.Name: Common Faun
Morphinae.Description: Deep brown underside with a series of small white spots and dark lines across both wings. Upperside is orange-brown.

Morphinae.Name: Palm King
Morphinae.Description: Multiple brown bands across both wings, each separated by thin white streaks. Hindwing also contains two widely separated eyespots.

Morphinae.Name: Saturn
Morphinae.Description: Underside resembles a leaf, with two large hindwing eyespots and a dark central line. Males have iridescent blue patches on uppersides, which are absent in females.

Morphinae.Name: Dark Blue Jungle Glory
Morphinae.Description: Underside dark brown, with several white streaks and two prominent black-filled eyespots. Males have a greater extent of blue patches on the upperside.

Morphinae.Name: Common Duffer
Morphinae.Description: Has a dark central line and two hindwing eyespots on a mottled brown underside. Few bluish spots on upperside of males, while females have a series of pale orange and whitish spots.

Nymphalinae.Name: Painted Lady
Nymphalinae.Description: Primarily orange on its upperside with black and white markings. Mottled underside with grey patches and an orange patch on its forewing.

Nymphalinae.Name: Indian Red Admiral
Nymphalinae.Description: Upperside dark grey-brown, with orange, black and white markings on edges. Underside has a blotched appearance with shades and patterns of brown, grey and orange.

Nymphalinae.Name: Malayan Eggfly
Nymphalinae.Description: Upperside reddish brown while underside darker brown. Exists in several forms, but identifiable on underside by lack of costal black spot and presence of two white spots near apex of hindwing.

Nymphalinae.Name: Danaid Eggfly
Nymphalinae.Description: Black with several blue-bordered white patches on its upperside. Its diagnostic feature is the black costal spot on the underside of its hindwing.

Nymphalinae.Name: Great Eggfly
Nymphalinae.Description: Similar to the Jacintha Eggfly. Thicker submarginal borders in females. Lacks the V-shaped appearance in the Jacintha Eggfly.

Nymphalinae.Name: Jacintha Eggfly
Nymphalinae.Description: Similar to the Great Eggfly. The submarginal borders of females are more reduced than in the Jacintha Eggfly, giving a V-shaped appearance.

Nymphalinae.Name: Autumn Leaf
Nymphalinae.Description: Leaf-like appearance. Told apart from other subspecies of Autumn Leaf by the presence of several small white spots on the forewing apex of its underside.

Nymphalinae.Name: Autumn Leaf
Nymphalinae.Description: Leaf-like appearance. Told apart from other subspecies of Autumn Leaf by the absence of several small white spots on the forewing apex of its underside.

Nymphalinae.Name: Chocolate Pansy
Nymphalinae.Description: Upperside reddish brown, while underside dark brown. Both sides are lined with orange eyespots.

Nymphalinae.Name: Grey Pansy
Nymphalinae.Description: Wings  grey on both sides, but slightly paler on the underside. Both sides are lined with grey or orange-and-black eyespots.

Nymphalinae.Name: Peacock Pansy
Nymphalinae.Description: Orange on both sides, but slightly paler on the underside. Both sides contain prominent eyespots.

Nymphalinae.Name: Blue Pansy (M)
Nymphalinae.Description: The male Blue Pansy has a bright blue hindwing on the upperside and a pale brown underside. Eyespots observed on both sides.

Nymphalinae.Name: Blue Pansy (F)
Nymphalinae.Description: The female Blue Pansy has a sombre brown upperside and a pale brown underside. Eyespots can be observed on both sides.

Nymphalinae.Name: Angled Castor
Nymphalinae.Description: A deep brown butterfly with wavy black lines on both sides of its wings. Has a diagnostic white spot near the forewing apex.

Nymphalinae.Name: Vagrant
Nymphalinae.Description: Tailed. Upperside orange-brown with a narrow black border, black markings on the forewing and small black spots on the hindwing. Underside consists of purplish brown, dark and pale orange-brown patches.

Nymphalinae.Name: Painted Lady
Nymphalinae.Description: Primarily orange on its upperside with black and white markings. Mottled underside with grey patches and an orange patch on its forewing.

Nymphalinae.Name: Indian Red Admiral
Nymphalinae.Description: Upperside dark grey-brown, with orange, black and white markings on edges. Underside has a blotched appearance with shades and patterns of brown, grey and orange.

Nymphalinae.Name: Malayan Eggfly
Nymphalinae.Description: Upperside reddish brown while underside darker brown. Exists in several forms, but identifiable on underside by lack of costal black spot and presence of two white spots near apex of hindwing.

Nymphalinae.Name: Danaid Eggfly
Nymphalinae.Description: Black with several blue-bordered white patches on its upperside. Its diagnostic feature is the black costal spot on the underside of its hindwing.

Nymphalinae.Name: Great Eggfly
Nymphalinae.Description: Similar to the Jacintha Eggfly. Thicker submarginal borders in females. Lacks the V-shaped appearance in the Jacintha Eggfly.

Nymphalinae.Name: Jacintha Eggfly
Nymphalinae.Description: Similar to the Great Eggfly. The submarginal borders of females are more reduced than in the Jacintha Eggfly, giving a V-shaped appearance.

Nymphalinae.Name: Autumn Leaf
Nymphalinae.Description: Leaf-like appearance. Told apart from other subspecies of Autumn Leaf by the presence of several small white spots on the forewing apex of its underside.

Nymphalinae.Name: Autumn Leaf
Nymphalinae.Description: Leaf-like appearance. Told apart from other subspecies of Autumn Leaf by the absence of several small white spots on the forewing apex of its underside.

Nymphalinae.Name: Chocolate Pansy
Nymphalinae.Description: Upperside reddish brown, while underside dark brown. Both sides are lined with orange eyespots.

Nymphalinae.Name: Grey Pansy
Nymphalinae.Description: Wings  grey on both sides, but slightly paler on the underside. Both sides are lined with grey or orange-and-black eyespots.

Nymphalinae.Name: Peacock Pansy
Nymphalinae.Description: Orange on both sides, but slightly paler on the underside. Both sides contain prominent eyespots.

Nymphalinae.Name: Blue Pansy (M)
Nymphalinae.Description: The male Blue Pansy has a bright blue hindwing on the upperside and a pale brown underside. Eyespots observed on both sides.

Nymphalinae.Name: Blue Pansy (F)
Nymphalinae.Description: The female Blue Pansy has a sombre brown upperside and a pale brown underside. Eyespots can be observed on both sides.

Nymphalinae.Name: Angled Castor
Nymphalinae.Description: A deep brown butterfly with wavy black lines on both sides of its wings. Has a diagnostic white spot near the forewing apex.

Nymphalinae.Name: Vagrant
Nymphalinae.Description: Tailed. Upperside orange-brown with a narrow black border, black markings on the forewing and small black spots on the hindwing. Underside consists of purplish brown, dark and pale orange-brown patches.

Papilioninae.Name: Common Birdwing
Papilioninae.Description: Similar to Malayan Birdwing, but with primarily dark forewing, sometimes with faint whitish streaks. Females have many black spots on hindwing.

Papilioninae.Name: Malayan Birdwing
Papilioninae.Description: Similar to Common Birdwing, but with stronger whitish streaks on forewing. Females have many black spots on hindwing.

Papilioninae.Name: Common Rose
Papilioninae.Description: Has a diagnostic red body and a full series of red spots along underside margins of hindwing.

Papilioninae.Name: Common Mime
Papilioninae.Description: A moderately large butterfly with black and white stripes.

Papilioninae.Name: Lime Butterfly
Papilioninae.Description: Upperside black with pale yellow spots and band; underside yellow with distinctive orange spots encircled by blue and black edges.

Papilioninae.Name: Banded Swallowtail
Papilioninae.Description: Tailed, with pale green band across both wings.

Papilioninae.Name: Red Helen
Papilioninae.Description: Tailed, marked with red marginal markings along underside of hindwing. Similar to Common Rose and the polytes form of the Common Mormon, but differ in position of white patch.

Papilioninae.Name: Great Helen
Papilioninae.Description: A large tailed butterfly with distinctive blue patches above tornal red spots.

Papilioninae.Name: Common Mormon
Papilioninae.Description: Tailed, with prominent white band across entire underside of hindwing. Females vary in form. The cyrus form resembles the male, but with red tornal bar.

Papilioninae.Name: Common Mormon (F)
Papilioninae.Description: Females of the polytes form mimick the Common Rose, but lacks red body. Central white patch and  series of red spots along margin on underside of hindwings.

Papilioninae.Name: Great Mormon
Papilioninae.Description: A large butterfly with prominent red patches near the base and tornus of its underside. Exist in several forms, mostly tailless.

Papilioninae.Name: Blue Helen
Papilioninae.Description: Tailed, with characteristic blue and orange spots behind white band on underside of hindwing.

Papilioninae.Name: Common Bluebottle
Papilioninae.Description: An arrowhead-shaped butterfly with distinctive blue band spanning both wings. Tailless.

Papilioninae.Name: Blue Jay
Papilioninae.Description: An arrowhead-shaped butterfly with black stripes. Lacks red costal spot on underside. Has small yellowish green patch separated from larger white patch.

Papilioninae.Name: Common Jay
Papilioninae.Description: An arrowhead-shaped, striped butterfly with a distinctive red costal bar on underside, as opposed to the red costal spot in the Great Jay.

Papilioninae.Name: Tailed Jay
Papilioninae.Description: An arrowhead-shaped butterfly with distinctive apple-green spots on predominantly black wings.

Papilioninae.Name: Striped Jay
Papilioninae.Description: An arrowhead-shaped butterfly with black stripes. Continuous dark central line bisects white band in hindwing.

Papilioninae.Name: Great Jay
Papilioninae.Description: An arrowhead-shaped, striped butterfly with a distinctive red costal spot on underside, as opposed to the red costal bar in the Common Jay.

Papilioninae.Name: Five Bar Swordtail
Papilioninae.Description: Has green and black stripes on its forewing. Identified by its characteristic long tail.

Papilioninae.Name: Common Birdwing

Papilioninae.Name: Blue Helen

Papilioninae.Name: Common Bluebottle

Papilioninae.Name: Striped Jay

Papilioninae.Name: Five Bar Swordtail

Satyrinae.Description: Can be identified by its yellow wash around the marginal areas on its underside. Forewing contains five relatively even-sized eyespots.

Satyrinae.Name: Dark Grass Brown
Satyrinae.Description: This butterfly resembles the bush browns, but has a more prominent white stripe on its dark brown underside. Has fewer, relatively larger eyespots.

Satyrinae.Name: Common Four-Ring
Satyrinae.Description: A small grey-brown butterfly with a mottled underside. Distinguishable from other ring butterflies by having four eyespots on the underside of its hindwings.

Satyrinae.Name: Malayan Six-Ring
Satyrinae.Description: Hindwing eyespots are small and lined up almost in a straight line. Has an additional eyespot compared to the five-rings.

Satyrinae.Name: Common Five-Ring
Satyrinae.Description: Lacks an eyespot compared to the Malayan Six-Ring. Second hindwing eyespot is always bigger than the first.

Satyrinae.Name: Malayan Five-Ring
Satyrinae.Description: Lacks an eyespot compared to the Malayan Six-Ring. Middle pair of eyespots on hindwings are smaller and separated.

Satyrinae.Name: Common Three-Ring
Satyrinae.Description: Small grey-brown butterfly with a mottled underside. Distinguishable from other ring butterflies by having three eyespots on the underside of its hindwings.

Satyrinae.Name: Bush Browns
Satyrinae.Description: Small, brown or orange-brown butterflies with a series of eyespots along their margins on the underside.

Damselfly.Name: Malayan Grisette
Damselfly.Description: This damselfy is generally restricted to forested areas of the nature reserves. It is light brownish throughout with pale spots along the abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance, but the female is paler.

Damselfly.Name: Common Flashwing
Damselfly.Description: This common large damselfly has distinct transparent wings with a bluish iridescence. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Damselfly.Name: Charming Flashwing
Damselfly.Description: Similar to the Common Flashwing, the two species can only be distinguished by their male anal appendages. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Damselfly.Name: Fiery Gem
Damselfly.Description: The male of this striking species has a stout red abdomen, and yellow markings on its black thorax. It has a dark apical spot on its forewings. Females have yellowish or greyish-olive markings on its black thorax and abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Clearwing Gem (M)
Damselfly.Description: This rare species has only been recorded at Nee Soon freshwater swamp forest. Mature males have a bluish-purple abdomen. Immature males have a bluish-grey abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Clearwing Gem (F)
Damselfly.Description: Mature females have a dark abdomen with pale markings on the thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Golden Gem (M)
Damselfly.Description: Males of this species can be identified by the bright yellow segments on its abdomen. They also have a dark apical spot on their forewings.

Damselfly.Name: Golden Gem (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females of this species is are light greenish. They also have a dark apical spot on their forewings.

Damselfly.Name: Blue Slim
Damselfly.Description: This is a very rare species in Singapore, and has only beeen occasionally encountered in the Central Catchment and Bukit Timah Nature Reserves, as well as Pulau Tekong.

Damselfly.Name: Variable Wisp (M)
Damselfly.Description: Individuals of this species change colour as they mature. Young males have a greenish thorax, and a black abdomen with an orange tip. They will lose this orange tip as they mature. Mature males have a white thorax and a dark coloured abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Variable Wisp (F)
Damselfly.Description: Immature females are red, and become olive as they mature. Mature females look like young males, but are duller in colour.

Damselfly.Name: Dwarf Wisp (M)
Damselfly.Description: This is the smallest damselfly in Singapore. Males have a blue thorax and abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Dwarf Wisp (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females have a green thorax and blue abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Wandering Wisp
Damselfly.Description: Similar to the Variable Wisp, this species changes colour as it matures. Males lose the orange tip at the end of their abdomen and the thorax takes on a blue-white colouration. Females start off reddish-brown, and become increasingly green.

Damselfly.Name: Will-o-Wisp (M)
Damselfly.Description: This uncommon species can be found near swamp forests. It has a very slender abdomen. Males have a metallic green thorax and almost translucent anal appendages.

Damselfly.Name: Will-o-Wisp (F)
Damselfly.Description: Immature females are red while mature females are olive green.

Damselfly.Name: Blue-nosed Sprite
Damselfly.Description: This species has blue markings on its abdomen and thorax, and is a relatively weak flier. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Damselfly.Name: Rebecca's Sprite
Damselfly.Description: The Rebecca's Sprite is similar to the Violet Sprite, but has lighter blue markings.

Damselfly.Name: Violet Sprite
Damselfly.Description: Violet Sprites have prominent blue markings on their thorax and the end of the abdomens. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Damselfly.Name: Variable Sprite (M)
Damselfly.Description: This species has extremely variable colours, depending on their sex and age. Mature males are dark with bright blue markings on their abdomen and thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Variable Sprite (F)
Damselfly.Description: This species has extremely variable colours, depending on their sex and age. Adult females lack the blue markings at the ends of their abdomens, which males have.

Damselfly.Name: Fiery Coraltail (M)
Damselfly.Description: Males have a bright red abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Fiery Coraltail (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females are a dark olive green.

Damselfly.Name: Ornate Coraltail
Damselfly.Description: This species has a pale blue head and thorax, and a dark abdomen with orange markings on both ends. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Damselfly.Name: Common Bluetail (M)
Damselfly.Description: Males have green markings on their thorax, and blue markings on the last two segments of their abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Common Bluetail (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females have a few morphs: one generally olive green, and the other with a orange thorax. Females can also look similar to males.

Damselfly.Name: Arthur's Midget (M)
Damselfly.Description: Males could either have yellow or blue stripes on their thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Arthur's Midget (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females are dark with blue stripes on their thorax, but are generally paler compared to the males.

Damselfly.Name: Hooked Midget (M)
Damselfly.Description: Looks similar to the Arthur's Midget, although males can be discerned by their down-curved superior appendages.

Damselfly.Name: Hooked Midget (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females have a reddish-brown thorax with blue stripes.

Damselfly.Name: Shorttail (M)
Damselfly.Description: This species has a short abdomen and dense spines on its long legs. Mature males have a purplish-blue thorax. Young males and females have yellowish stripes on their thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Shorttail (F)
Damselfly.Description: Mature females are dark with yellowish-white stripes on the thorax. Young males and females have yellowish stripes on their thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Dryad
Damselfly.Description: The Dryad has a long abdomen and a thorax which is yellow on both sides and black on top. Males have short, dark brown wing tips. Females have white wing tips.

Damselfly.Name: Look-alike Sprite (M)
Damselfly.Description: This species is similar to the Blue Sprite but is larger and less abundant. Males have blue eyes and thorax, and blue markings on their abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Look-alike Sprite (F)
Damselfly.Description: This species is similar to the Blue Sprite but is larger and less abundant. Females are light brownish-yellow.

Damselfly.Name: Blue Sprite (M)
Damselfly.Description: Males have a bright blue thorax, abdomen and eyes.

Damselfly.Name: Blue Sprite (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females are light brown with green markings.

Damselfly.Name: Grey Sprite
Damselfly.Description: Males have a bright blue thorax, abdomen and eyes. Females are light brown with green markings.

Damselfly.Name: Orange-faced Sprite
Damselfly.Description: As the name suggests, males of this species have orange faces. Orange-faced Sprites have only been recorded in Nee Soon Freshwater Swamp Forest and Toa Payoh Town Garden. Females are orange-yellow from head to thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Red-tailed Sprite
Damselfly.Description: The Red-tailed Sprite has a red thorax, and a largely dark abdomen which is red on the last few segments. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Damselfly.Name: Blue-sided Satinwing (M)
Damselfly.Description: Males have a thorax with blue-coloured sides, and a distinct dark patch on their hindwings.

Damselfly.Name: Blue-sided Satinwing (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females have an olive-grey and black thorax, with wings that are narrow and clear.

Damselfly.Name: Crenulated Spreadwing
Damselfly.Description: This species prefers open habitats such as reservoirs and large ponds, and typically rests with its wings held open. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Damselfly.Name: Blue-spotted Flatwing
Damselfly.Description: This species has bright blue markings on their thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Damselfly.Name: White-tailed Sylvan (M)
Damselfly.Description: As its name suggests, the White-tailed Sylvan has a distinct white 'tip' at the end of its abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: White-tailed Sylvan (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females of this species have a dorsally brown abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Telephone Sylvan
Damselfly.Description: This damselfly gets its curious name from the markings on top of its thorax, which resembles two telephone handsets facing each other. The female's telephone-shaped markings are not as clearly seen and at times fragmented.

Damselfly.Name: Yellow Featherlegs
Damselfly.Description: This species gets its name from its yellow legs. It is commonly found near streams and swamps near forest edges. Immatures individuals have white bodies and legs. Males and females are similar in appearance, but females are paler in colour.

Damselfly.Name: Variable Featherlegs
Damselfly.Description: This species has yellow legs, similar to the Yellow Featherlegs, but has irregular green markings on its thorax. It has fewer white markings on its abdomen tip than do the Yellow Featherlegs. Immature individuals are mostly white, and are known as "ghost forms". Males and females are similar in appearance, except females are brownish where the males are black.

Damselfly.Name: Singapore Shadowdamsel
Damselfly.Description: This species was first found in Singapore and was only recently found in Johor. The 8th and 9th segments of the male's abdomen are blue. Females have a very small blue colouration at the tip of its abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Collared Threadtail (M)
Damselfly.Description: This species may be confused with the Crescent Threadtail, but can be identified by its blue anal appendages.

Damselfly.Name: Collared Threadtail (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females are paler and have narrower stripes on the thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Orange-striped Threadtail (M)
Damselfly.Description: The males of this species have orange stripes on its thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Orange-striped Threadtail (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females have pale stripes which are not orange.

Damselfly.Name: Interrupted Threadtail
Damselfly.Description: Males have interrupted (broken) blue bands on the top of their thorax, and blue markings on the end of their abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance, but females are paler in colour.

Damselfly.Name: Crescent Threadtail (M)
Damselfly.Description: This species may be confused with the Collared Threadtail, but can be identified by its black anal appendages.

Damselfly.Name: Crescent Threadtail (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females have narrower blue markings on the thorax.

Dragonfly.Name: Emperor
Dragonfly.Description: This large species has a dark abdomen and a blue-green thorax. Emperor females lay their eggs in plant tissue. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Spoon-tailed Duskhawker
Dragonfly.Description: The distinguishing feature of this rare species is its spoon-shaped anal appendages. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Small Duskhawker
Dragonfly.Description: A rare species in Singapore, this duskhawker has a dark abdomen with a green thorax. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Spear-tail Duskhawker
Dragonfly.Description: This is a rare forest species and has a pair of bright green eyes and thorax. The shape of its abdomen is similar to that of the Dingy Duskhawker. The inferior appendage is largely yellowish-white. Females are duller.

Dragonfly.Name: Dingy Duskhawker
Dragonfly.Description: This species can be found in rainforests, and can be recognised by its distinct, dark T-shaped mark on the upper surface of the frons. Females are paler.

Dragonfly.Name: Nighthawker
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a bright green thorax, while females are generally brownish.

Dragonfly.Name: Lesser Nighthawker
Dragonfly.Description: The Lesser Nighthawker is similar to the Spear-tail Duskhawker, except the former has anal appendages that are flat and broad. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Giant Hawker
Dragonfly.Description: A rarely seen species, this large dragonfly has a reddish-brown body. Males have a brown streak on each long, broad wing. Females are bigger, more commonly seen than males, and have large dark patches near the tips of all its wings.

Dragonfly.Name: Pond Cruiser
Dragonfly.Description: This large species has yellow markings on its dark thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Stream Cruiser (M)
Dragonfly.Description: The Stream Cruiser has large blue-green eyes and a distinct white line across the thorax between its wings.

Dragonfly.Name: Stream Cruiser (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Lesser Stream Cruiser
Dragonfly.Description: This species is similar to the Stream Cruiser, but can be distinguished by a yellow band at the base of its abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance, but females have a larger body.

Dragonfly.Name: Emerald
Dragonfly.Description: This very rare species has a slender abdomen and is generally a dark metallic green. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Shadowdancer
Dragonfly.Description: The Shadowdancer is a small species with brilliant green eyes, an emerald thorax and a dark abdomen. There is a yellow band at the side of its green thorax. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Lesser Splayed Clubtail
Dragonfly.Description: This species has prominent yellow markings on its mostly-black thorax and abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Malayan Grappletail
Dragonfly.Description: This species has blue-green eyes and a green-sided thorax. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Flangetail
Dragonfly.Description: The Common Flangetail is common in open habitats. It has green-yellow bands on its thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Ris' Clubtail
Dragonfly.Description: This species has a slender abdomen that is mostly black, and has two yellow strips on the sides of its thorax.

Dragonfly.Name: Forktail
Dragonfly.Description: The front part of the thorax has two large yellow squarish patches, and the abdomen has several orange rings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Malayan Spineleg
Dragonfly.Description: The Malayan Spineleg has green-yellow stripes on the top and side of its thorax. The superior anal appendages are whitish.

Dragonfly.Name: Tiny Sheartail
Dragonfly.Description: This species has a yellow triangular patch on either side of its thorax. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Banded Hooktail
Dragonfly.Description: This species has a rather stout abdomen with thick yellow stripes. It has unique scimitar-like appendages. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Trumpet Tail (M)
Dragonfly.Description: The Trumpet Tail has a trumpet-shaped abdomen. Males are blue with dark markings.

Dragonfly.Name: Trumpet Tail (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are greenish-yellow with similar markings as males.

Dragonfly.Name: Blue Adjudant
Dragonfly.Description: The Blue Adjudant is a small dragonfly. The thorax and part of the abdomen of both the mature male and female are bright blue. In the male, the last four abdominal segments are dark. In the female, the last five abdominal segments are dark.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Adjudant (M)
Dragonfly.Description: The Scarlet Adjudant is a small red dragonfly. Males have a short bright red abdomen. The "knees" on the hind legs are red in colour.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Adjudant (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are brown-yellow with yellowish "knees" on the hind legs.

Dragonfly.Name: Pond Adjudant (M)
Dragonfly.Description: The Pond Adjudant male is a small powdery blue dragonfly. It can be differentiated from the larger Blue Dasher by how only the last two abdominal segments are dark.

Dragonfly.Name: Pond Adjudant (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are yellowish-brown with black markings.

Dragonfly.Name: Grenadier
Dragonfly.Description: This species has mottled yellow markings on its thorax and the top half of its abdomen is red. Females are similar in appearance to the males, but slightly duller.

Dragonfly.Name: Handsome Grenadier (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have distinct blue, black and red segments on the abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Handsome Grenadier (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are mostly dark with dull yellowish-orange markings.

Dragonfly.Name: Blue Dasher (M)
Dragonfly.Description: This species has a yellow tint at the base of its wings. Males have a powdery blue body with a black tip on its abdomen (on the last three abdominal segments).

Dragonfly.Name: Blue Dasher (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are brownish-yellow with a dark streak along its abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Pixie (M)
Dragonfly.Description: The males of this rare species are mainly orange with a white patch on the abdomen. The last three segments are black.

Dragonfly.Name: Pixie (F)
Dragonfly.Description: The females of this rare species are light brown.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Amberwing (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a reddish-gold tint on their wings and have an orange abdomen. Immature males are similar to females in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Amberwing (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are light brown and have yellowish-orange wing spots.

Dragonfly.Name: Sultan
Dragonfly.Description: Males of this large species have a distinct red patch on one-third of the wings. Females of this large species are brownish-orange.

Dragonfly.Name: Green-eyed Percher
Dragonfly.Description: This species is uniformly dark blue and has a thin abdomen with a slightly swollen base. The female is similar to the male in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Lined Forest-skimmer
Dragonfly.Description: The Lined Forest-skimmer has yellow stripes on its thorax. Only females have dark wing tips.

Dragonfly.Name: Dark-tipped Forest-skimmer (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Both males and females have dark wing tips and a dark blue body, with a broken yellow line along the thorax.

Dragonfly.Name: Dark-tipped Forest-skimmer (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females can be distinguished by the lack of the light blue segments on their abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Scarlet (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are red with a dark line along the abdomen, which distinguishes them from the Common Redbolt.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Scarlet (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females have a light brown body with a similar dark line along its abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Black-tipped Percher (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are blue with dark wing tips. The immature male is similar in appearance to the female.

Dragonfly.Name: Black-tipped Percher (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are yellow with a dark band down their abdomen. The wings are clear. The female is similar in appearance to the immature male.

Dragonfly.Name: Blue Percher (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are mostly dark blue, with the last three abdominal segments black. They have distinct white anal appendages. The immature male is similar in appearance to the female.

Dragonfly.Name: Blue Percher (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females have yellow-green markings on both the thorax and abdomen, as well as distinct white anal appendages. The female is similar in appearance to the immature male.

Dragonfly.Name: Water Monarch
