Dragonfly.Description: This species is brownish and has an irregular dark band on its hindwings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Restless Demon
Dragonfly.Description: This rare species has a blackish thorax and dark-bluish abdomen. Its wings are dark at the tips and base. The female is paler and less commonly observed.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Grenadier
Dragonfly.Description: The Scarlet Grenadier has a yellow-striped thorax and bright red abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Coastal Glider (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are red with a thick dark line down the abdomen. This dark line is shaped like the roman numerical, '1'. Immature males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Coastal Glider (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are orange-yellow with a thick dark line down the abdomen. This dark line is shaped like the roman numerical, '1'.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Pygmy (M)
Dragonfly.Description: This is the smallest dragonfly in Singapore. Males have a bright red abdomen and thorax. The immature male has a brownish-yellow body.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Pygmy (F)
Dragonfly.Description: This is the smallest dragonfly in Singapore. Females are mostly dark with white bands across the abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Striped Grenadier
Dragonfly.Description: Males of this species have a distinct red lower abdomen with black bands, and a thorax with yellow stripes. Females have a dark brown abdomen and similar markings as males do on their thorax. Immature females have a red abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Parasol (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a dark red colouration on their wings and clear wing tips. This is the most common dragonfly in Singapore.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Parasol (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are light brown with dark markings along the sides of its abdomen. Its wings are clear. This is the most common dragonfly in Singapore.

Dragonfly.Name: Riverhawk
Dragonfly.Description: A very rare species with a mostly dark body and yellow markings on its thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Blue Sentinel
Dragonfly.Description: This rare species has only been recorded at Nee Soon freshwater swamp forest. The male looks similar to the blue form of the Variable Sentinel, but it has a thinner, longer abdomen with more white colour.

Dragonfly.Name: Variable Sentinel (M)
Dragonfly.Description: This species has many colour morphs and males can have a red abdomen with or without white markings, or a black abdomen with white markings.

Dragonfly.Name: Variable Sentinel (F)
Dragonfly.Description: This species has many colour morphs and females can either be red or dark-coloured, or be yellow when young.

Dragonfly.Name: Spine-tufted Skimmer (M)
Dragonfly.Description: This species can be easily confused with the Scarlet Skimmer, but can be distinguished by its brown thorax and dark grey eyes.

Dragonfly.Name: Spine-tufted Skimmer (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are reddish-brown.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Blue Skimmer (M)
Dragonfly.Description: While adult males have a generally blue body with a darkened tip, immature males are usually yellow-brown and resemble the females.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Blue Skimmer (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are generally yellow-brown.

Dragonfly.Name: Slender Blue Skimmer (M)
Dragonfly.Description: As the name suggests, males of this species have a slender blue abdomen and also posess light blue eyes. Immature males and females are light brown.

Dragonfly.Name: Slender Blue Skimmer (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are light brown.

Dragonfly.Name: Variegated Green Skimmer
Dragonfly.Description: This common species can be found in many habitats, and has distinct yellowish-green markings on its thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Skimmer (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a bright red thorax and abdomen and a red patch near the base of their wings.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Skimmer (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are yellowish-brown with clear wings.

Dragonfly.Name: Wandering Glider
Dragonfly.Description: This common species can often be seen flying in open areas and is one of the most widespread species in the world. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Mangrove Marshal
Dragonfly.Description: This species is mostly found in mangroves. Mature males have a white pruinescence on their thorax. Females have a thorax with olive colour on its sides.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Chaser (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a striking blue thorax with a yellow and black abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Chaser (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females have black and yellow stripes on their thorax. The abdomen is black with dull orange markings. Notably, it has conspicuous flaps near the tip of the abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Banded Skimmer (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are black with a white patch on the first few segments of their abdomens.

Dragonfly.Name: Banded Skimmer (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females have a yellow abdomen with black markings.

Dragonfly.Name: Mangrove Dwarf (M)
Dragonfly.Description: This species looks similar to the Blue Dasher but is smaller and does not have the amber tint at the base of its wings. Found only in mangrove areas.

Dragonfly.Name: Mangrove Dwarf (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females have yellow markings along the thorax and the abdomen. Found only in mangrove areas.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Redbolt (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are bright red throughout, including the eyes.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Redbolt (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are brown with a bright yellow streak that extends from the thorax to the top of the abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Bronze Flutterer
Dragonfly.Description: The Bronze Flutterer has striking opaque iridescent wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Yellow-barred Flutterer
Dragonfly.Description: This is one of the easiest species to identify with a distinct dark-coloured and yellow pattern on the base of its hindwings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Sapphire Flutterer
Dragonfly.Description: The Sapphire Flutterer can be easily identified by the blue patches on its wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Potbellied Elf
Dragonfly.Description: This rare species is restricted to swampy forests. A distinctive feature is its curved abdomen which is swollen at the first two segments. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Elf
Dragonfly.Description: This species looks similar to the Potbellied Elf, but does not have a curved abdomen. Females are similar in appearance to the male, but has a thicker abdomen and greater amount of yellow markings.

Dragonfly.Name: White-barred Duskhawk (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a distinct light brown and white patch on their hindwings. Immature males lack this wing pattern and are generally pale brown, similar to the female in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: White-barred Duskhawk (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are generally pale brown with clear wings.

Dragonfly.Name: Saddlebag Glider
Dragonfly.Description: The veins on the base of this species' hindwings are red. Two black spots are present at tip of its abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Crimson Dropwing (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a luminous pink abdomen, red wing veins and an amber tint at the wing base.

Dragonfly.Name: Crimson Dropwing (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are light brown with yellow veins on the base of their hindwings, and black markings along the sides of their abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Indigo Dropwing (M)
Dragonfly.Description: This common species can be found near streams and rivers. Males are dark blue, and have a half-blackish abdoment with yellow spots.

Dragonfly.Name: Indigo Dropwing (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are yellowish-brown with dark markings on the thorax and abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Dancing Dropwing
Dragonfly.Description: This species has distinct yellow markings on its thorax and abdomen, and a yellow tint at the base of its wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Treehugger (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are very distinct with their blue bodies and broad metallic blue patch at the base of their hindwings.

Dragonfly.Name: Treehugger (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are light brown and have black markings on their abdomens.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Basker (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have two diamond-shaped spots at the end of the abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Basker (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are yellowish-brown in colour with an amber patch at the base of the hindwings.

Dragonfly.Name: Slender Duskdarter
Dragonfly.Description: Males have green eyes, and a slender abdomen. Females have a slightly thicker abdomen. The species is most active at dusk and dawn.

Damselfly.Name: Variable Wisp (M)
Damselfly.Description: Individuals of this species change colour as they mature. Young males have a greenish thorax, and a black abdomen with an orange tip. They will lose this orange tip as they mature. Mature males have a white thorax and a dark coloured abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Variable Wisp (F)
Damselfly.Description: Immature females are red, and become olive as they mature. Mature females look like young males, but are duller in colour.

Damselfly.Name: Variable Sprite (M)
Damselfly.Description: This species has extremely variable colours, depending on their sex and age. Mature males are dark with bright blue markings on their abdomen and thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Variable Sprite (F)
Damselfly.Description: This species has extremely variable colours, depending on their sex and age. Adult females lack the blue markings at the ends of their abdomen which males have.

Damselfly.Name: Fiery Coraltail (M)
Damselfly.Description: Males have a bright red abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Fiery Coraltail (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females of this species are a dark olive green.

Damselfly.Name: Ornate Coraltail
Damselfly.Description: This species has a pale blue head and thorax, and a dark abdomen with orange markings on both ends. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Damselfly.Name: Common Bluetail (M)
Damselfly.Description: Males have green markings on their thorax, and blue markings on the last two segments of their abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Common Bluetail (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females have a few morphs: one generally olive green, and the other with a orange thorax. Females can also look similar to males.

Damselfly.Name: Arthur's Midget (M)
Damselfly.Description: Males could have either yellow or blue stripes on their thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Arthur's Midget (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females are dark with blue stripes on their thorax, but are generally paler compared to the males.

Damselfly.Name: Shorttail (M)
Damselfly.Description: This species has a short abdomen and dense spines on its long legs. Mature males have a purplish blue thorax. Young males and females have yellowish stripes on their thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Shorttail (F)
Damselfly.Description: This species has a short abdomen and dense spines on its long legs. Mature females are dark with yellowish-white stripes on the thorax. Young males and females have yellowish stripes on their thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Look-alike Sprite (M)
Damselfly.Description: This species is similar to the Blue Sprite but is larger and less abundant. Males have blue eyes and thorax, and blue markings on their abdomen.

Damselfly.Name: Look-alike Sprite (F)
Damselfly.Description: This species is similar to the Blue Sprite but is larger and less abundant. Females are light brownish-yellow.

Damselfly.Name: Blue Sprite (M)
Damselfly.Description: Males have a bright blue thorax, abdomen and eyes.

Damselfly.Name: Blue Sprite (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females are light brown with green markings.

Damselfly.Name: Orange-faced Sprite
Damselfly.Description: As the name suggests, males of this species have orange faces. Orange-faced Sprites have only been recorded in Nee Soon Freshwater Swamp Forest and Toa Payoh Town Garden. Females are orange-yellow from head to thorax.

Damselfly.Name: Crescent Threadtail (M)
Damselfly.Description: This species may be confused with the Collared Threadtail, but can be identified by its black anal appendages.

Damselfly.Name: Crescent Threadtail (F)
Damselfly.Description: Females have narrower blue markings on the thorax.

Dragonfly.Name: Emperor
Dragonfly.Description: This large species has a dark abdomen and a blue-green thorax. Emperor females lay their eggs in plant tissue. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Dingy Duskhawker
Dragonfly.Description: This species can be found in rainforests, and can be recognised by its distinct, dark T-shaped mark on the upper surface of the frons. Females are paler.

Dragonfly.Name: Pond Cruiser
Dragonfly.Description: This large species has yellow markings on its dark thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Flangetail
Dragonfly.Description: The Common Flangetail is common in open habitats. It has green-yellow bands on its thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Trumpet Tail (M)
Dragonfly.Description: The Trumpet Tail has a trumpet-shaped abdomen. Males are blue with dark markings.

Dragonfly.Name: Trumpet Tail (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are greenish-yellow with similar markings as males.

Dragonfly.Name: Blue Adjudant
Dragonfly.Description: The Blue Adjudant is a small dragonfly. The thorax and part of the abdomen of both the mature male and female are bright blue. In the male, the last four abdominal segments are dark. In the female, the last five abdominal segments are dark.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Adjudant (M)
Dragonfly.Description: The Scarlet Adjudant is a small red dragonfly. Males have a short bright red abdomen. The "knees" on the hind legs are red in colour.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Adjudant (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are brown-yellow with yellowish "knees" on the hind legs.

Dragonfly.Name: Pond Adjudant (M)
Dragonfly.Description: The Pond Adjudant male is a small powdery blue dragonfly. It can be differentiated from the larger Blue Dasher by how only the last two abdominal segments are dark.

Dragonfly.Name: Pond Adjudant (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are yellowish-brown with black markings.

Dragonfly.Name: Grenadier
Dragonfly.Description: This species has mottled yellow markings on its thorax and the top half of its abdomen is red. Females are similar to males, but slightly duller.

Dragonfly.Name: Blue Dasher (M)
Dragonfly.Description: This species has a yellow tint at the base of its wings. Males have a powdery blue body with a black tip on its abdomen (on the last three abdominal segments).

Dragonfly.Name: Blue Dasher (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are brownish-yellow with a dark streak along its abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Amberwing (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a reddish-gold tint on their wings and have an orange abdomen. Immature males are similar to females in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Amberwing (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are light brown and have yellowish-orange wing spots.

Dragonfly.Name: Sultan
Dragonfly.Description: Males of this large species have a distinct red patch on one-third of the wings. Females of this large species are brownish-orange.

Dragonfly.Name: Green-eyed Percher
Dragonfly.Description: This species is uniformly dark blue and has a thin abdomen with a slightly swollen base. The female is similar to the male in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Scarlet (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are red with a dark line along the abdomen, which distinguishes them from the Common Redbolt.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Scarlet (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females have a light brown body with a similar dark line along its abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Black-tipped Percher (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are blue with dark wing tips. The immature male is similar in appearance to the female.

Dragonfly.Name: Black-tipped Percher (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are yellow with a dark band down their abdomen. The wings are clear. The female is similar in appearance to the immature male.

Dragonfly.Name: Blue Percher (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are mostly dark blue, with the last three abdominal segments black. They have distinct white anal appendages. The immature male is similar in appearance to the female.

Dragonfly.Name: Blue Percher (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females have yellow-green markings on both the thorax and abdomen, as well as distinct white anal appendages. The female is similar in appearance to the immature male.

Dragonfly.Name: Water Monarch
Dragonfly.Description: This species is brownish and has an irregular dark band on its hindwings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Grenadier
Dragonfly.Description: The Scarlet Grenadier has a yellow-striped thorax and bright red abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Coastal Glider (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are red with a thick dark line down the abdomen. This dark is shaped like the roman numerical, '1'. Immature males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Coastal Glider (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are orange-yellow with a thick dark line down the abdomen. This dark line is shaped like the roman numerical, '1'.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Parasol (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a dark red colouration on their wings and clear wing tips. This is the most common dragonfly in Singapore.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Parasol (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are light brown with dark markings along the sides of its abdomen. Its wings are clear. This is the most common dragonfly in Singapore.

Dragonfly.Name: Spine-tufted Skimmer (M)
Dragonfly.Description: This species can be easily confused with the Scarlet Skimmer, but can be distinguished by its brown thorax and dark grey eyes.

Dragonfly.Name: Spine-tufted Skimmer (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are reddish-brown.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Blue Skimmer (M)
Dragonfly.Description: While adult males have a generally blue body with a darkened tip, immature males are usually yellow-brown and resemble the females.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Blue Skimmer (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are generally yellow-brown.

Dragonfly.Name: Slender Blue Skimmer (M)
Dragonfly.Description: As the name suggests, males of this species have a slender blue abdomen and also posess light blue eyes. Immature males and females are light brown.

Dragonfly.Name: Slender Blue Skimmer (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are light brown.

Dragonfly.Name: Variegated Green Skimmer
Dragonfly.Description: This common species can be found in many habitats, and has distinct yellowish-green markings on its thorax and abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Skimmer (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a bright red thorax and abdomen and a red patch near the base of their wings.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Skimmer (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are yellowish-brown with clear wings.

Dragonfly.Name: Wandering Glider
Dragonfly.Description: This common species can often be seen flying in open areas and is one of the most widespread species in the world. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Chaser (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a striking blue thorax and yellow and black abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Chaser (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females have black and yellow stripes on their thorax. The abdomen is black with dull orange markings. Notably, it has conspicuous flaps near the tip of the abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Banded Skimmer (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are black with a white patch on the first few segments of their abdomens.

Dragonfly.Name: Banded Skimmer (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females have a yellow abdomen with black markings.

Dragonfly.Name: Mangrove Dwarf (M)
Dragonfly.Description: This species looks similar to the Blue Dasher but it is smaller and does not have the amber tint at the base of its wings. Found only in mangrove areas.

Dragonfly.Name: Mangrove Dwarf (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females have yellow markings along the thorax and the abdomen. Found only in mangrove areas.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Redbolt (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males are bright red throughout, including the eyes.

Dragonfly.Name: Common Redbolt (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are brown, with a bright yellow streak that extends from the thorax to the top of the abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Bronze Flutterer
Dragonfly.Description: The Bronze Flutterer has striking opaque iridescent wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Yellow-barred Flutterer
Dragonfly.Description: One of the easiest species to identify with a distinct dark and yellow pattern on the base of their hindwings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Sapphire Flutterer
Dragonfly.Description: The Sapphire Flutterer can be easily identified by the blue patches on its wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: White-barred Duskhawk (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a distinct light brown and white patch on their hindwings. Immature males lack this wing pattern and are generally pale brown, similar to the female.

Dragonfly.Name: White-barred Duskhawk (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are generally pale brown with clear wings.

Dragonfly.Name: Saddlebag Glider
Dragonfly.Description: The veins on the base of this species' hindwings are red. Two black spots are present at tip of abdomen. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Crimson Dropwing (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have a luminous pink abdomen, red wing veins and an amber tint at the wing base.

Dragonfly.Name: Crimson Dropwing (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are light brown with yellow veins on the base of their hindwings, and black markings along the sides of the abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Indigo Dropwing (M)
Dragonfly.Description: This common species can be found near streams and rivers. Males are dark blue, abdomen half blackish with yellow spots.

Dragonfly.Name: Indigo Dropwing (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are yellowish-brown with dark markings on the thorax and abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Dancing Dropwing
Dragonfly.Description: This species has distinct yellow markings on its thorax and abdomen, and a yellow tint at the base of its wings. Males and females are similar in appearance.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Basker (M)
Dragonfly.Description: Males have two diamond-shaped spots at the end of the abdomen.

Dragonfly.Name: Scarlet Basker (F)
Dragonfly.Description: Females are yellowish-brown in colour with an amber patch at the base of the hindwing.

Dragonfly.Name: Slender Duskdarter
Dragonfly.Description: Males have green eyes, and a slender abdomen. Females have a slightly thicker abdomen. The species is most active at dusk and dawn.

Bee-eaters.Name: Blue-throated bee-eater
Bee-eaters.Description: While similar to the blue-tailed bee eater, this species can be distinguished by its brown head and bright blue throat.

Bee-eaters.Name: Blue-tailed bee-eater
Bee-eaters.Description: While similar to the blue-throated bee eater, this species can be distinguished by its olive head and yellow-brown throat.

Bulbuls.Name: Yellow-vented bulbul
Bulbuls.Description: A common bird with brown upperparts, pale underparts, a black lore and a bright yellow vent.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Oriental magpie-robin
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: This songbird has black and white plumage with a long tail that is often held high.  Females are grey on upperparts and breast.

Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Name: Asian paradise flycatcher
Chats and Old World Flycatchers.Description: Breeding males have an exceptionally long tail and come in either rufous or white colour morphs. Females and non-breeding males have much shorter tail and either white or chestnut upperparts with varying amount of grey or black on head, throat and upper breast.

Cisticolas and Allies.Name: Common tailorbird
Cisticolas and Allies.Description: Similar to the Dark-necked Tailorbird, but has a less extensive red cap and white vent. Males have a longer tail than females.

Crows.Name: House crow
Crows.Description: This urban bird can be differentiated from the Large-billed Crow by its grey collar.

Crows.Name: Large-billed crow
Crows.Description: Similar to the House Crow except that it is entirely black and has a distinctly larger bill.

Cuckoos.Name: Asian koel
Cuckoos.Description: This large bird has a distinct loud call from which it derives its common name. They can be distinguished from crows with their long tails and red eyes.

Flowerpeckers.Name: Scarlet-backed flowerpecker
Flowerpeckers.Description: This common garden bird has a red crown and back, black upperparts and white underparts. Females are generally grey with a red rump.

Hornbills.Name: Oriental pied hornbill
Hornbills.Description: This large striking bird was once rare in Singapore, but populations have since recovered due to a successful re-introduction programme.

Ioras.Name: Common iora
Ioras.Description: Males have black upperparts and yellow underparts, while females have olive-green upperparts and yellow underparts. Two white wing bars distinctive in both sexes

Kingfishers.Name: White-throated kingfisher
Kingfishers.Description: A common species in Singapore, this bird can be recognised by the white-breast  and throat on its otherwise brown underparts.

Kingfishers.Name: Collared kingfisher
Kingfishers.Description: This common species has a turquoise cap, wings back and tail, and a white collar and underparts.

Munias.Name: Scaly-breasted munia
Munias.Description: This bird gets its common name from the scaling on its breast. Has a dark brown head and upperparts.

Old World Sparrows.Name: Eurasian tree sparrow
Old World Sparrows.Description: This common species has a brown cap and prominent black patches on its cheeks and chin.

Orioles.Name: Black-naped oriole
Orioles.Description: This common garden bird is unmistakable with its bright yellow plumage, black nape and wings, and pink bill.

Pheasants.Name: Red junglefowl
Pheasants.Description: This nationally-threatened species is thought to be the ancestral species of the domestic chicken. It is commonly encountered on P. Ubin.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Rock pigeon
Pigeons and Doves.Description: This urban bird typically appears grey, but can include brown, black and white morphs.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Spotted dove
Pigeons and Doves.Description: This dove may be confused with the Zebra Dove but has a spotted neck and is larger.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Zebra dove
Pigeons and Doves.Description: This dove may be confused with the Spotted Dove but has a striped neck and has a slimmer build.

Pigeons and Doves.Name: Pink-necked green pigeon
Pigeons and Doves.Description: Similar colouration to the Little Green Pigeon but males have a pink neck and green wings, and are much larger. Females are mostly green.

Rails and Crakes.Name: White-breasted waterhen
Rails and Crakes.Description: This common waterbird has a white face and breast, and blackish upperparts and brown vent.

Shrikes.Name: Tiger shrike
Shrikes.Description: Adults have a grey head, black face mask, barred chestnut upperparts and white underparts. The more commonly encountered immatures are chestnut above and white below with heavy barring on both upperparts and underparts.

Shrikes.Name: Brown shrike
Shrikes.Description: Not similar to the Tiger Shrike. Adults have brown cap, white eye-brow above black face mask, unbarred brown upperparts and whitish underparts with a brownish wash.

Starlings.Name: Asian glossy starling
Starlings.Description: This bird is glossy dark green with red eyes is often seen in flocks. Juveniles are grey above and white below and covered in bold streaks.

Starlings.Name: Common myna
Starlings.Description: Despite its name, it is less common than the White-vented myna. Distinguishable by its brown body and yellow eye-patch.

Starlings.Name: Javan myna
Starlings.Description: The most common bird in Singapore, this species can be found in most urban areas.It has a black plumage, white vent and yellow beak.

Starlings.Name: Daurian starling
Starlings.Description: This bird is a creamy white with metallic green wings with a white wingbar.

Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Name: Brown-throated sunbird
Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Description: Males of this species have a beautiful metallic blue crown and back, brown throat and yellow underparts. Females are duller with olive upperparts and yellow underparts. Both sexes have red eyes, female also has distinct split yellow eye-ring.

Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Name: Olive-backed sunbird
Sunbirds and Spiderhunters.Description: A commonly seen bird that has olive green upperparts and yellow underparts, with male birds possessing a metallic blue bib.

White-eyes.Name: Oriental white-eye
White-eyes.Description: A common garden bird with greenish-yellow head and upperparts, grey underparts, yellow vent and a prominent white eye-ring.

Woodpeckers.Name: Sunda pygmy woodpecker
Woodpeckers.Description: This is the smallest woodpecker species in Singapore and is well camouflaged on trees with its brown and white mottled plumage.

Woodpeckers.Name: Common goldenback
Woodpeckers.Description: So called for its golden-yellow plumage. Males have a red cap, while females have a black cap.

Bittern.Name: Yellow Bittern
Bittern.Description: A shy bird that is often found in pondside vegetation, the Yellow Bittern can be identified by the contrast between its yellowish brown wing coverts and black flight feathers in flight.

Bittern.Name: Cinnamon Bittern
Bittern.Description: This species has cinnamon upperparts with streaked underparts, and appears uniformly reddish-brown in flight.

Bittern.Name: Von Schrenck's Bittern
Bittern.Description: The male of this species has chestnut upperparts and pale underparts, while the females have numerous white spots on brown upperparts and are boldly streaked on their underparts.

Bittern.Name: Black Bittern
Bittern.Description: The black bittern is so called for its dark upperparts and underparts which are streaked with white.

Egret.Name: Little Egret
Egret.Description: This all-white egret can be differentiated from the other by its black bill and black legs with yellow feet.

Egret.Name: Intermediate Egret
Egret.Description: This all-white egret has a yellow bill with black tip and black legs and feet. Its S-shaped neck is roughly equal to its body length.

Egret.Name: Great Egret
Egret.Description: This all-white egret has a yellow bill and black legs, and can be differentiated from the others by the kink in its long S-shaped neck.

Egret.Name: Eastern Cattle Egret
Egret.Description: Eastern cattle egrets are white with a rufous head and breast. In non-breeding plumage, it is completely white and can be differentiated by its shorter neck.

Egret.Name: Chinese Egret
Egret.Description: This all-white egret can be differentiated from the others by its crest (in breeding plumage), greenish facial skin, legs and feet with two-tone bill (black upper half and yellow bottom half). Very similar to the white morph Pacific Reef Heron but the latter has distinctively shorter legs and upper mandible of bill is generally paler.

Egret.Name: Pacific Reef Heron
Egret.Description: This species has both a dark morph, which is unmistakably slate-grey, and a light morph, which is white. Light morph has greenish legs and feet, yellowish bill and appears shorter-legged than other white egrets.

Heron.Name: Grey Heron
Heron.Description: This tall bird has a light grey plumage with a black stripe above its eyes and black stripes on its neck.

Heron.Name: Purple Heron
Heron.Description: This heron can be easily identified by its rusty red neck and purplish grey plumage.

Heron.Name: Great-billed Heron
Heron.Description: This heron get its name from its large bill and is the tallest bird in Singapore at 115 cm. It has dark grey pluamge with pale streaks on its wings and neck.

Heron.Name: Malayan Night Heron
Heron.Description: This heron has a black crown and reddish-brown plumage with streaked underparts. Juveniles have mottled brown upperparts with numerous white spots and black barring on their underparts.

Heron.Name: Striated Heron
Heron.Description: A small heron with dark crown, grey mantle and underparts and yellowish legs. It can be confused with the Black-crowned Night Heron.

Heron.Name: Black-crowned Night Heron
Heron.Description: This distinctive heron has a black crown and back, red eyes and white underparts.

Heron.Name: Javan Pond Heron
Heron.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a pale rufous head, brown breast, black back, and white belly. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Heron.Name: Indian Pond Heron
Heron.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a buffy head, neck and breast, maroon mantle and scapulars and white belly. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Heron.Name: Chinese Pond Heron
Heron.Description: In breeding plumage, this heron has a brown head and breast, black back and white belly and wings. All pond-herons look similar in non-breeding plumage with brownish upperparts and bold streaks on head, neck and breast.

Anemone.Name: Burgundy Anemone
Anemone.Description: Burgundy or dark red in color. Short tentacles that taper off at its ends. Some may have five yellow spots around its mouth.

Anemone.Name: Snaky Anemone
Anemone.Description: Has purplish-grey, green or brown colored tentacles that are tightly curled together. Looks like udon noodles.

Anemone.Name: Striped Sand Anemone
Anemone.Description: Has parallel dark bars down and white stripes across its semi-transparent tentacles. Easily confused with the Striped Bead Anemone, but has shorter tentacles and a light-colored body column.

Anemone.Name: Striped Bead Anemone
Anemone.Description: Has parallel dark lines down its semi-transparent tentacles and white bars across. Easily confused with the Striped Sand Anemone, but has longer tentacles and a tan or green body column.

Anemone.Name: Whelk-hitching Anemone
Anemone.Description: Small body. Brown with white stripes. Attached to the shells of whelks.

Anemone.Name: Swimming Anemone
Anemone.Description: Many tentacles - something striped in red/white, or sometimes plain yellow or brown. Can swim - for about 15 seconds each time, though they do not really swim much at low tide.

Anemone.Name: Common Peachia Anemone
Anemone.Description: Small anemone with 16 fat tentacles having white, pink, beige or brown chevron patterns near its mouth. Cream-colored body column.

Anemone.Name: Giant Carpet Anemone
Anemone.Description: Densely covered with short tentacles, resembling a carpet. Usually brown or purple in color, with tips of the tentacles in a lighter shade. Bright pink bumps sometimes seen on the underside.

Anemone.Name: Haddon's Carpet Anemone
Anemone.Description: Has long-short tentacles with bulbous tips at the circumference of its outer disk. Generally green, blue, grey or purple in color.

Anemone.Name: Mini Carpet Anemone
Anemone.Description: Small carpet anemone about the size of one's palm. Has short tentacles that can be green, brown or grey.

Anemone.Name: Lined Bead Anemone
Anemone.Description: This tiny, grey anemone is seldom seen with its tentacles, making it look like a bead with fine white/orange/red stripes. The Lined Bead Anemone is commonly found all over the world, as it is easily dispersed by ships.

Brittle Star.Name: Very Long-armed Brittle Star
Brittle Star.Description: Long arms - sometimes stretching up to 30 cm long. Small central disk that is about 1-2 cm in diameter. Flat arms have spines laterally extended. Arms may have a faint banded pattern.

Brittle Star.Name: Tiny Colorful Brittle Star
Brittle Star.Description: Comes in a variety of colors and patterns, usually mimicking that of the animal it is on. Arms have small spines along its length. Central disk is colorfully patterned.

Butterflyfish.Name: Copperband Butterflyfish
Butterflyfish.Description: Distinct body pattern of orange/ yellow stripes with black and white edges. Has a flat body and a long snout. Characterised by a black eye spot on its dorsal fin.

Butterflyfish.Name: Kite Butterflyfish
Butterflyfish.Description: Kite-shaped. Distinct body pattern of 4 brown stripes (juvenile ones have 5) and a black eye spot on its dorsal fin. Has a flat body and a short snout.

Butterflyfish.Name: Batavia Batfish
Butterflyfish.Description: Characterised by its flat body and small mouth. Is usually silver with a dark bar vertically down its eye. A lighter-colored bar is seen behind the dark bar.

Butterflyfish.Name: Bengal Sergeant
Butterflyfish.Description: Rounded tail fins. White or yellow body with 6-7 black or grey vertical bars across its body. The bars end right before the tail of the fish.

Button.Name: Clear Sundial Snail
Button.Description: Grey and yellowish brown with alternating bands of dark brown and white. Flat circular shell with whorls. Bottom view resembles a spiral staircase.

Button.Name: Button Snail
Button.Description: Identified by circular glossy shells. Can be found in a variety of colors and patterns.

Cerianthid.Name: Cerianthid Phoronid Worm
Cerianthid.Description: Grey or pinkish-black in color. Possesses a pair of feathery spiraling tentacles. Extremely shy and retreat once they sense danger.

Clam.Name: Fluted Giant Clam
Clam.Description: 5-6 rows of open flutes on its valves. Shell opening faces upwards. Hinged side is firmly attached to the rock surface.

Clam.Name: Pacific Yellow Cockle
Clam.Description: Characterised by thick and spherical shells with vertical ribs. Yellowish shell often seen with dark stains on it.

Clam.Name: Common File Clam
Clam.Description: Fan-shaped thick shell. Usually white and yellow. Rough with coarse scaly ribs and long sticky tentacles.

Clam.Name: Big Brown Mactra Clam
Clam.Description: Smooth and triangular. Usually unmarked and is buried just beneath the surface of the ground with an extended siphon sticking out.

Clam.Name: Lettered Venus Clam
Clam.Description: Shaped like a trapezium. Smooth and thin clam is white with small black dots.

Conch.Name: Black-lipped Conch
Conch.Description: Narrow shell with wavy flared lips. Black edges around its shell opening. Green body with white or beige spots.

Conch.Name: Gong-gong
Conch.Description: White pearly shell with a flared lip. Body is olive green. Has a brown-orange tentacle connected to a large eye. Interestingly, the snail hops instead of creeping along surfaces.

Conch.Name: Spiral Melongena
Conch.Description: Large shell with a black body. Shell is covered by a fine layer of hairs. Hairs only fall off after the snail dies, revealing an orange shell underneath.
Conch.Habitat: Mudflat, Sandy beach, Rocky shore, Seagrass, Mangrove

Conch.Name: Margined Conch
Conch.Description: Thick shell with wavy flared lips. Shell is usually white with brown streaks.

Coral.Name: Zebra Coral
Coral.Description: A type of encrusting hard coral that thrives even in the murkiest waters. Aptly named the Zebra Coral due to its white ring on a black background.

Crab.Name: Red-eyed Reef Crab
Crab.Description: Oval body that is reddish to purplish brown. Bright red eyes. Moves fast.

Crab.Name: Velcro Crab
Crab.Description: Body in the shape of a tear-drop. Often disguised under bits and pieces of sponges, seagrass, coral rubble and shell.

Crab.Name: Spotted Moon Crab
Crab.Description: Circular, pale white/yellow body with little dark spots. Long spikes on its sides. Its paddle-shaped walking legs allow the crab to quickly burrow into the sand.

Crab.Name: Stone/Thunder Crab
Crab.Description: Large pincers with brown-black tips. Bright green eyes, encircled with red. Upperside of its body is dull grey, but the underside is orange.

Crab.Name: Maroon Stone Crab
Crab.Description: Reddish-brown to maroon in color. Black tips on its pincers. Eyes are completely red, unlike the Stone crab which has green eyes.

Crab.Name: Horn-eyed Ghost Crab
Crab.Description: Aptly named the Ghost Crab given its elusive nature. Can run up to 2m/s. Box-shaped body with markings shaped like a ‘H’. Adults have darker colored 'horns' on top of each eyestalk.

Crab.Name: Orange Fiddler Crab
Crab.Description: Males identified by an enlarged pincer, with the lower pincer orange or yellow but the upper pincer white. Females do not have an enlarged pincer. Body color varies from green to grey.

Crab.Name: Spotted-belly Forceps Crab
Crab.Description: Enlarged pincer that has grinding teeth (‘molar’) like humans. Smooth red/purple brown body on the upperside, pale orange with dark spots on the underside.
Crab.Habitat: Rocky shore, Coral reef, Coral rubble, Sea wall

Crab.Name: Painted Porcelain Crab
Crab.Description: Not a true crab! Small and white with purplish polka dots on the pincers and upper body. Often found in pairs.

Crab.Name: Purple-legged Swimming Crab
Crab.Description: Last pair of legs on this crab is padde-shaped, allowing it to swim expertly. Comes in various colors, with walking legs in purple and claws in orange with black tips.

Crab.Name: Flower Crab
Crab.Description: Males have attractive bright colors and white spots on their body. Females are dull green/brown and have a bigger abdomen on the underside to carry eggs.

Crab.Name: Blue Swimming Crab
Crab.Description: Padde-shaped legs on the last pair of legs allows this crab to swim expertly. Distinct rectangular, blue body. 6 rounded lobes between its widely-spaced eyes.

Crab.Name: Blue-spined Swimming Crab
Crab.Description: Bright blue-black tips on its pincers and 5 spines next to its eyes. 6 rounded lobes between its widely-spaced eyes.

Crab.Name: Red Swimming Crab
Crab.Description: Bright orange/red in color, but sometimes brown. Has 5 spines with black tips on the side of its body. Last pair of paddle-shaped walking legs can be blue in color.

Crab.Name: Mangrove Tree-dwelling Crab
Crab.Description: Half-circular body. Green eyes spaced widely far apart on the non-circular side of its body. Yellow body with dark brown patches.

Crab.Name: Smooth Spooner Crab
Crab.Description: Pincers are smooth with spoon-shaped tips. Left pincer is slightly larger than the right. Usually come in a wide variety of colors - brown, beige, and grey.

Crab.Name: Leaf Porter Crab
Crab.Description: Commonly found using leaves, clam shells or wood for camouflage. Has long, thin legs and small pincers which are tucked close to its body.

Crab.Name: Soldier Crab
Crab.Description: Move around in groups at low tide. Has long eyestalks with slender and long pincers which fold downward.

Crab.Name: Common Hairy Crab
Crab.Description: Crab is covered with long, soft 'hair' which helps the crab to camouflage as drifting flotsam. Has distinct red eyes. Fun fact: The Common Hairy Crab is also known as the Teddy Bear Crab!

Creeper.Name: Zoned Cerith
Creeper.Description: Conical-shaped shell with a brown band spiraling down its white or beige-colored shell.
Creeper.Habitat: Sandy beach, Coral rubble, Coral reef

Creeper.Name: Obelisk Creeper Snail
Creeper.Description: Conical-shaped shell. Can take on two types of spiral patterns - fine spirals with small dots or wide spirals with regular bumps. Has a sharp pointed tip.

Creeper.Name: Javan Turrid Snail
Creeper.Description: Identified by the spirals on its shell with regular pointed bumps. Shell is pale brown or beige. Body is pale with brown spots.

Cuttlefish.Name: Glittering Cuttlefish
Cuttlefish.Description: Smooth and oval. Has glittering spots on each side of its body.

Dangerous.Name: Red Egg Crab
Dangerous.Description: Red in color with an egg-shaped body. Has obvious white dots on its body. It is poisonous! Do not eat or touch them.

Dangerous.Name: Mosaic Reef Crab
Dangerous.Description: Orange/red body with striking white mosaic-like patterns. Do not touch or eat, it is poisonous!

Dangerous.Name: Fire Anemone
Dangerous.Description: This anemone has thick and fleshy tentacles and its central oral disk has white stripes with small, dark spots. The colour of this animal can vary from green, yellow, purple, blue and brown. This anemone can give a powerful and painful sting as its name suggests, beware not touch them!

Dangerous.Name: Three-spined Toadfish
Dangerous.Description: Do not touch! There are sharp spines on the side of its head which can be painful. Best identified by its large eyes, wide mouth and big, flat head. Has greyish-brown bars on its sides.
Dangerous.Habitat: Rocky shore, Coral rubble, Sandy beach

Dangerous.Name: Longspined Waspfish
Dangerous.Description: A pair of spines can be spotted next to its mouth. Dorsal fin starts from above the eyes of the animal. Do not touch with bare hands! This fish has prickly dorsal spines that can be painful!

Dangerous.Name: Hollow-cheeked Stonefish
Dangerous.Description: Do not touch! This fish can be fatal to humans! Resembles a stone, and is very well camouflaged. Can be identified by its downturned mouth that resembles a frown.
Dangerous.Habitat: Sea wall, Coral reef, Coral rubble

Dangerous.Name: Black Eeltail Catfish
Dangerous.Description: Do not touch! It has venomous spines on its dorsal and pectoral fins. Best identified by four pairs of 'whiskers' around its mouth and flat eel-like tail.

Dangerous.Name: Cone Snail
Dangerous.Description: This snail is identified by its conical shell that looks similar to an ice cream cone. The shell opens in a narrow slit and the operculum (opening) is a long and horn-like. The snail is about 5-10 cmand slow-moving but uses its radula that shoots out like a harpoon to inject a potent toxin to hunt for prey. Although this animal may look harmless like other types of snails, but it is one of the most dangerous animals on our shores and the effects of their sting can be fatal. Do not handle any snails with a similar conical shell and make sure to be in proper footwear and attire.

Dangerous.Name: Reef Bristleworm
Dangerous.Description: Green, brown or pink body lined with long bristles. Often found hiding under stones. Do not touch! Bristles are filled with toxins and can cause burning pain when touched.

Dangerous.Name: Golden Fireworm
Dangerous.Description: Extremely beautiful with colorful hairy bistles. Do not touch! Sharp bristles are filled with toxins and can easily penetrate bare skin.

Eel.Name: Estuarine Moray Eel
Eel.Description: Long body and flattened at the tail. Resembles a snake in both appearance and movement. Usually blue-grey, brown, or reddish-brown with yellow-white spots all over its body.

Eel.Name: Carpet Eel-blenny
Eel.Description: Contrary to its name and appearance, it is neither an eel nor a snake. Identified as a fish by its fins and scales, but also has a flat eel-like tail. Has a large mouth with thick lips. Green in color.

Feather.Name: Delicate Feathery Green Seaweed
Feather.Description: Each feathery structure is 5 – 7 cm long with long fine branches with pointed tips on a cylindrical central stem. This seawwed is found in clumps and can cover an area of 40 - 50 cm.

Feather.Name: Taxifolia Feathery Green Seaweed
Feather.Description: Each feather structure is around 3 – 15 cm long and has flat branches with pointed tips on a flat central stem. This seaweed can also be found in clumps, covering an area of 40 - 50 cm but does not blanket the shore.

Feather Star.Name: Red Feather Star
Feather Star.Description: Has about 30 distinct bright red, feathery arms, as well as some yellowish parts.

Fish.Name: Tropical Silverside
Fish.Description: Color can range from silvery grey to blue. Streamlined-shaped with large eyes. Often has a long silver line along the length of its side.

Fish.Name: Diamond Tuskfish
Fish.Description: Characterised by its pointed snout and sharp teeth. Is usually silver or green in color and can be found with red, blue and yellow markings that form 4-5 bars across its body.

Fish.Name: Gold-spotted Mudskipper
Fish.Description: Obvious orange spots on its cheeks and the sides of its body. Males have an orange and black dorsal fin with elongated spikes.
Fish.Habitat: Mangrove, Rocky shore, Seagrass, Coral rubble

Fish.Name: Brown Shore Goby
Fish.Description: Chubby-faced with small eyes. Has a body covered with irregular pale spots.

Fish.Name: Head Stripe Lagoon Goby
Fish.Description: Colorful goby with dark spots and stripes on its head. Luminous blue stripes on the side of its body.

Fish.Name: Ornate Lagoon Goby
Fish.Description: Fat round snout with thick lips. Has dashed lines on its sides, red and blue speckles on its body. Can be differentiated from the Black-spotted lagoon goby which has black spots instead.

Fish.Name: Peacock Sole
Fish.Description: Challenging to spot this fish due to its high ability to camouflage. Fish has a flat and 2D-shape body with white circles all over its body.

Fish.Name: Commerson's Sole
Fish.Description: Usually plain brown or beige with no markings, and can camouflage easily in sandy areas. Flat and elongated and tapers off at the tail.

Fish.Name: Seagrass Filefish
Fish.Description: Identified by irregular curved yellow or white line from the front of its body to the middle of its upper body. The line forms a 'smile' on the side of its body.

Fish.Name: Black-spot Tuskfish
Fish.Description: Characterised by the black spot in the middle of its dosal fin.

Hermit Crab.Name: Orange-striped Hermit Crab
Hermit Crab.Description: Orange stripes on its brown walking legs. Black body with white spots. Can be found in any type of shell (as long as they fit).

Hermit Crab.Name: Blue-striped Hermit Crab
Hermit Crab.Description: Blue stripes on its brown walking legs. Can be found in any type of shell (as long as they fit).

Hermit Crab.Name: Banded Hermit Crab
Hermit Crab.Description: Black bands on its pale yellow walking legs, body and antennae. Right pincer is larger than the left.
Hermit Crab.Habitat: Coral rubble, Living coral, Sea fan

Horseshoe Crab.Name: Mangrove Horseshoe Crab
Horseshoe Crab.Description: Identified by a short telson (tail) that is circular in cross-section. Smooth, brown shell with short spines on the side of its body.

Horseshoe Crab.Name: Coastal Horseshoe Crab
Horseshoe Crab.Description: Identified by a long telson (tail) that is triangular in cross-section. Grey-brown shell with long spines on sides of the body.

Limpet.Name: Flat False Limpet
Limpet.Description: Thick and flat shell with 20 or more thick ribs on it. Ribs have the same color as the shell. No hole at the top of its shell.

Limpet.Name: Star Limpet
Limpet.Description: Thick shell with 5 or 6 raised white ribs creating a star-like pattern.

Ribbon.Name: Tape Seagrass
Ribbon.Description: Identified by its inrolled leaf edges. Long ribbon-like leaves with smooth round tips. Found covering large areas on sand and mud banks.

Ribbon.Name: Fern Seagrass
Ribbon.Description: Leaf made up by up to 20 pairs of tiny leaflets on a single stem, creating its fern-like appearance. Found in small patches.
Ribbon.Status: Critically Endangered (2008 Singapore Red Data Book)

Ribbon.Name: Sickle Seagrass
Ribbon.Description: Curved sickle-shaped with smooth and round tips. Has cross hatched veins. Found scattered in patches.
Ribbon.Status: Critically Endangered (2008 Singapore Red Data Book)

Ribbon.Name: Sea Lettuce
Ribbon.Description: Sea lettuce is a thin and translucent seaweed and it can range from sheets, ribbon- or net-like. They often cover a large area of the shore and floats freely.
Ribbon.Size: Approximately 1 - 2 cm (narrow strips) or more than 20 cm (sheets)

Sand Dollar.Name: Cake Sand Dollar
Sand Dollar.Description: Circular with fine hairs around the edges. Usually found in large quantities. Sometimes have a star-shaped pattern in the centre.

Scallop.Name: Singapore Scallop
Scallop.Description: Both long and short tentacles seen when submerged in water. Many tiny eyes.

Sea Cucumber.Name: White-rumped Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: White/grey rear ends on a smooth brown body. Rear end is actually its anus that is surrounded by 5 yellow 'teeth'. Sometimes completely brown; other times seen with white marks on its surface.

Sea Cucumber.Name: Beige Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: White or beige in color with 5 small brown spots along the length of its upperside. Has distinguishable soft, short projections all along its upperside. Underside is flat with translucent tube feet.

Sea Cucumber.Name: Black Long Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: Black and long. Tapered ends on a tube-like body. Has tube feet surrounding the length of its body, without a distinct upper or underside.

Sea Cucumber.Name: Remarkable Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: Looks like long sausage with one end more tapered than the other. Found in many colors such as yellow, brown, orange, or white - but all have irregular dark spots around its body.

Sea Cucumber.Name: Sandfish Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: Shaped like a loaf of garlic bread. Beige with black bars, distinct square-ish ends.

Sea Cucumber.Name: See-through Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: Translucent body that is smooth and slippery. Internal muscles and organs can be seen. Species lacks tube feet.

Sea Cucumber.Name: Sea Apple Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: Upperside is red and purple in color. Underside is usually pale to white in color. Sausage-like appearance, but inflates itself into a round ball when stressed.

Sea Cucumber.Name: Pink Warty Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: Pink and yellow in color. Soft and leathery with irregular bumps. Looks similar to the Thorny Sea Cucumber but has less red on its body.

Sea Cucumber.Name: Thorny Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: Looks similar to the Pink Warty Sea Cucumer but has soft thorns and rarely has yellow on its body Usually red or orange in color with grey lines along its body.

Sea Cucumber.Name: Orange Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: Mostly orange appearance due to the orange stripes on its dark blue body. Soft and leathery.

Sea Cucumber.Name: Plasticky Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: Appears plasticky. Pale blue or grey with dark-colored lines along its U-shaped body. Feet has bright orange tips.

Sea Cucumber.Name: Durian Sea Cucumber
Sea Cucumber.Description: Resembles a durian with its thorny appearance. Grey-colored with spine-shaped structures.
Sea Cucumber.Size: Approximately About 20 cm, up to 50 cm

Sea Fan.Name: Asparagus Sea Fan
Sea Fan.Description: Red/orange/yellow/white stems. Looks like an asparagus when polyps retract.

Sea Fan.Name: Gnarled sea fan
Sea Fan.Description: Red/orange/maroon/pink stems. Looks rough and twisted when polyps retract.

Sea Pen.Name: Spiky Sea Pen
Sea Pen.Description: The spiky sea pen has a thick white stem with feather-like structures supported by spines, resembling a quilted pen. It is about 15 – 20 cm long and may have brown spots or an orange foot that is usually buried. The tiny painted porcelain crab is often found hiding in this sea pen.

Sea Star.Name: Plain Sand Star
Sea Star.Description: Sea star with bright orange spines on the edge of its arms. Upperside is brown with a darker brown centre and line down each of its arms. Underside is plain white.

Sea Star.Name: Painted Sand Star
Sea Star.Description: Sea star with white spines along the edge of its arms. On the upperside, it is lined with an orange or dark blue stripe down its arms. Tip of each arm is black.

Sea Star.Name: Eight-armed Luidia Sea Star
Sea Star.Description: Has 8 arms that are 12 - 20 cm long with irregular black bars. Usually beige in color, star-shaped black mark in the centre. Underside is white.

Sea Star.Name: Common Sea Star
Sea Star.Description: Upperside can be in various colors - beige, grey, or brown with variable patterns. Has long arms.

Sea Star.Name: Cake Sea Star
Sea Star.Description: Underside is pale with a chevron pattern of dark bars. Upperside is covered with small pincer-like appendages.

Sea Star.Name: Biscuit Sea Star
Sea Star.Description: Resembles a baked biscuit with its brown-beige color and smooth, cookie-cutter rounded arm tips. Upperside has blue edges running along the arms towards a dark center.

Sea Star.Name: Spiny Sea Star
Sea Star.Description: Upperside has spiny bumps and large plate-like pincers. Underside is pale without any patterns.

Sea Star.Name: Knobbly Sea Star
Sea Star.Description: Also named 'Chocolate Chip Sea star'. Has dark knobs along the arms and in a circle at the center.

Sea Urchin.Name: White Salmacis Urchin
Sea Urchin.Description: Short sharp white spines with bands in green/purple/brown. Commonly found camouflaging with leaves, seagrass or shells stuck on its spines.

Sea Urchin.Name: Passion Salmacis Urchin
Sea Urchin.Description: Short sharp purple spines with white tips. Spines around the mouth may be banded in white or maroon color.

Sea Urchin.Name: Black Sea Urchin
Sea Urchin.Description: Short, black spines about 1 cm in length radiating from its body. Has translucent tube feet that sometimes extends past its spines, helping it to move away from predators.

Sea Urchin.Name: Long-spined Black Sea Urchin
Sea Urchin.Description: Skinny, long, black spines can prick through clothing, gloves and even shoes. Upperside has a sac with an orange ring, five white spots, and a v-shaped pattern of tiny bright blue spots.
Sea Urchin.Habitat: Sandy beach, Rocky shore, Coral rubble
Sea Urchin.Size: Approximately Spines up to 30 cm long

Seahorse.Name: Estuarine Seahorse
Seahorse.Description: Refrain from touching as this can damage the protective mucus on the seahorse’s skin. Segmented body armour with no obvious spines, an upright posture and a curled tail.

Shrimp.Name: Peacock-tail Anemone Shrimp
Shrimp.Description: Translucent orange body with white spots. Characterized by 5 eyespots on its tail that is orange with a black ring around.

Slug.Name: Extraordinary Sea Hare
Slug.Description: Tentacles on its head resemble the ears of a rabbit. Smooth body and dark body flaps with irregular white blotchy bars and dots.

Slug.Name: Geographic Sea Hare
Slug.Description: Olive and yellow body with tiny white spots. Has large tentacles that looked similar to rabbit ears. Usually only found during low tides or during night time.

Slug.Name: Spotted Sea Hare
Slug.Description: Body is large and smooth. Brown-colored with thin, white bars on the inner edge of its 'wings'.

Slug.Name: Hairy Sea Hare
Slug.Description: Brown body with bright blue dots. Can easily camouflage with seaweeds and seagrasses. Species is covered with many finger-like projections, giving it a hairy appearance.

Slug.Name: Jolly Green Giant Nudibranch
Slug.Description: Large horn-like lobe at the front of its gills. Green body outlined in white with yellow bumps all over its body.

Slug.Name: Polka-dot Nudibranch
Slug.Description: White oval body with black circular markings, looking like polka-dots. Black tipped feathery gills on its back.

Slug.Name: Pimply Phyllid Nudibranch
Slug.Description: Black bodies covered with bright blue, pink, grey, red, or green bumps.

Slug.Name: Starry-mouthed Nudibranch
Slug.Description: Oral tentacles with star-shaped tips. White-colored with a net-like pattern of red or orange lines. Has orange-tipped appendages, which protects its feathery white gills.

Slug.Name: Moon-headed Sidegill Slug
Slug.Description: Resembles a chocolate chip pancake. Beige with irregular brown spots. Has a large flap of skin known as the veil with sensory 'hairs' to help them detect preys.

Slug.Name: Ornate Leaf Slug
Slug.Description: Bears some resemblance to seaweeds. Body color can vary from green, yellow to white. Black margin on the edge of a pair of large 'wings' it possesses. Black or white spots on its body.

Snail.Name: Dubious Nerite Snail
Snail.Description: No two shells of the species look identical. Smooth and glossy shell with a large opening.

Snail.Name: Scaly Nerite Snail
Snail.Description: Scaly shell with uneven spiralling ribs that makes its surface rough. Unlike other similar nerite snails, the spire (where you can find the tip of the shell) is not sticking out.

Snail.Name: Waved Nerite Snail
Snail.Description: Thick shell with irregular dark patches and fine, narrow, and smooth ribs. 3-4 'teeth' at the shell opening and occasionally a large 'tooth' at the outer lip of the opening.

Snail.Name: Lined Nerite Snail
Snail.Description: Distinctively identified by the spiraling black ribs on its shell. Has a smooth and white underside. Has a thick operculum that is covered with small pink and black bumps.

Snail.Name: Flat Slipper Snail
Snail.Description: Usually spotted in the shells of Hermit crabs. Flat and white shell. Commonly found in pairs.

Snail.Name: Conical Slipper Snail
Snail.Description: Usually found on the shell of Hermit crabs. Thin and pointed shell with colors varying from white, pink, to red.

Snail.Name: Grey Bonnet Snail
Snail.Description: Resembles a bonnet. Smooth helmet-shaped shell with a pointed end. Operculum is shaped like a fan and brightly yellow in color.

Snail.Name: Miliaris Cowrie
Snail.Description: Pear-shaped shell that is beige to light-brown in color. White spots on the shell. Base has a white perimeter.

Snail.Name: Ovum Cowrie
Snail.Description: Pear-shaped shell that is pale blue in color with three broad brown bands. Tiny brown speckles on the shell.

Snail.Name: Fig Snail
Snail.Description: Resembles a fig. Shell has a white spiral pattern with irregular dark bands and has a large opening.

Snail.Name: Knobbly Periwinkle Snail
Snail.Description: Conical-shaped shell with knobs arranged in a spiral pattern. Shell is usually black or bleached white.

Snail.Name: Ball Moon Snail
Snail.Description: Spherical shell that is smooth and plain with pearly pastel shades. Looks similar to the Oval moon snail, but can be distinguished by a brown patch and a small depression on its underside.

Snail.Name: Spotted Moon Snail
Snail.Description: Smooth thick shell with a spiral tip. Beige, grey or orange with many irregular dark bands. White body with many dark spots.

Snail.Name: Tiger Moon Snail
Snail.Description: Shell pattern resembles a leopard. Pear-shaped. White or beige shell with dark spots in a spiral pattern.

Snail.Name: Eggwhite Moon Snail
Snail.Description: Smooth glossy shell. White, yellow, orange, or brown in color. Underside has a U-shaped depression. Resembles a hard boiled egg.

Snail.Name: Oval Moon Snail
Snail.Description: Resembles a tear-drop. Smooth white shell with a spiral tip. Usually plain, can have patches of yellow, orange, brown, or black at times. Grey bands can be seen on shell.

Snail.Name: Lined Moon Snail
Snail.Description: White or beige shell with fine brown lines. Body is white or beige with short brown tentacles.
Snail.Habitat: Near seagrass, Sandy beach, Muddy bottoms

Snail.Name: Common Triton Snail
Snail.Description: Beige or brown shell with dark brown spiral patterns of beaded dots and lines.

Snail.Name: Spiral Babylonia Snail
Snail.Description: Distinctive spirals with orange or brown spots on the shell. Shell can vary from brown to white color.

Snail.Name: Waved Mitre Snail
Snail.Description: Bullet-shaped shell with fine ridges arranged in a cross-hatched manner. Shell has a layer of skin which can be peeled off.

Snail.Name: Creno Whelk
Snail.Description: Conical shell with fine pointed bumps and fine brown lines.

Snail.Name: Prickly Whelk
Snail.Description: Pointed fine bumps on its conical shell. Usually white with fine brown lines.

Snail.Name: Mud Whelk
Snail.Description: Conical shell with bumpy ridges on the spire (where the tip is). Found in shades of brown, white and green, usually with a brown band on the shell.

Snail.Name: Common Whelk
Snail.Description: Conical-shaped shell with neat and regular ridges. Alternating bands of white and brown. Can commonly see tiny sea anemones on its shell.

Snail.Name: Olive Whelk
Snail.Description: Brown or olive green shell with smooth spiralling ridges. Has a very long siphon and short tentacles.

Snail.Name: Lined Whelk
Snail.Description: Purple line lining the spirals of the shell. Shell is conical-shaped and yellow in color.

Snail.Name: Olive Weasel Snail
Snail.Description: Resembles a bullet. Fine brown zig-zag lines on beige-colored shell. Opening of shell is violet in color.

Snail.Name: Noble Volute
Snail.Description: Wide brown zig-zag lines on beige, yellow, or orange shell. Body is black with orange or yellow spots.

Snail.Name: Baler Volute
Snail.Description: Thin and fragile shell that is usually beige or orange with brown bands. Body is brown with white stripes.
Snail.Habitat: Muddy bottoms, Near seagrass, Near mangrove

Snail.Name: Turtle Dove Snail
Snail.Description: Pale white/ beige shell with a dark net-like pattern. Occasionally, a second shell can be spotted at its shell opening.

Snail.Name: Dotted Dove Snail
Snail.Description: Thick shell with black and yellow patterns.

Spinefish.Name: False Scorpionfish
Spinefish.Description: Large backward pointing spines above its mouth that can hurt. Hard to spot the fish as it is good at camouflaging and staying motionless.

Sponge.Name: Chocolate Sponge
Sponge.Description: Chocolate brown with a smooth, velvety texture. Tiny brittle stars can be found in the small holes of the sponge.
Sponge.Habitat: Muddy bottoms of lagoons, Near reefs

Sponge.Name: Blue Spatula Sponge
Sponge.Description: Pale blue with a prickly texture. Can be spotted in a wide range of forms, including looking like leaves of a lettuce or spatula-like fingers.

Sponge.Name: Daisy Sponge
Sponge.Description: Wide range of colors - yellow, purple, brown, green, and black. Usually has 1 or 2 hollow cones in the middle and is encircled by upright long structures.

Sponge.Name: Orange Prickly Sponge
Sponge.Description: Orange-colored with prickly projections. Has many tiny holes of about 0.5 cm. Can be found covering rocks and stones or forming branches on their own.

Sponge.Name: Champagne Sponge
Sponge.Description: Pink in color. Rough texture due to the tiny spikes on it. Holes may be found along the length of its branches.

Spoon.Name: Spoon Seagrass
Spoon.Description: Spoon-shaped seagrass with smooth edges. Found in large quantities.

Spoon.Name: Hairy Spoon Seagrass
Spoon.Description: Spoon-shaped with minute hairs on both sides of its leaves. Has thin, smooth and white stems. Leaves appear in pairs from the stems.

Top Shell.Name: Ribbed Turban Snail
Top Shell.Description: Thick shell has many smooth spirals and an operculum that resembles a 'cat's eye'. Operculum is usually a green ring with yellow or white margins and a dark centre.

Top Shell.Name: Toothed Top Shell Snail
Top Shell.Description: Assymmetrical grey shell with spiraling round bumps. A white tooth structure at its shell opening.

Top Shell.Name: Spotted Top Shell Snail
Top Shell.Description: Thick conical shell with spiraling bumps. Has a yellow underside with dark spots in spirals.
Top Shell.Habitat: Rocky shore, Sea wall, Coral reef

Watering Pot.Name: Watering Pot Shell
Watering Pot.Description: Broader end has many small holes like the spout of a watering can. Resembles an upside-down carrot when buried.
Watering Pot.Status: Presumed Nationally Extinct (2008 Singapore Red Data Book)

Worm.Name: Very Long Ribbon Worm
Worm.Description: Very long. White body with 4-5 black stripes along the entire length of its body.

Worm.Name: Olive Flatworm
Worm.Description: Olive-colored on one side, pale on its underside. White outer margin and black inner margin.

Worm.Name: Blue-lined Flatworm
Worm.Description: White body with a blue margin and a central blue stripe (sometimes yellow).

Worm.Name: Straw Tubeworm
Worm.Description: This animal is a complex worm that lives inside a tube that it builds. The tube resembles a straw and it is usually embedded in the substrate and about 2 – 3 cm exposed aboveground. The straw is 0.5 cm in diameter and often found in large numbers covering large distances.

Acrochordidae.Name: Banded File Snake
Acrochordidae.Description: Baggy skin enclosed by tiny uneven scales, head is not apparent. Its tail recede and condenses to a point. Body covered with black and white stripes across.

Agamidae.Name: Earless Agamid
Agamidae.Description: Body very slender with long slender limbs and tail. Relatively large head. Brown, mature males have a blue iris, females have a white one.

Agamidae.Name: Green Crested Lizard
Agamidae.Description: Head slender and tail very long. Spiny crest over middle of neck. Body colour is usually bright green, sometimes with a bluish tinge. However, when threatened, colour may change to dark brown or grey. Blackish eye-ring and ear. Part of the tail is often brown.

Agamidae.Name: Changeable Lizard
Agamidae.Description: Top of the head is pointed along the middle of the neck and the back. Brownish to greenish yellow with blackish streaks radiating from the eyes and brown bands along the back with a whitish stripe on the sides. Males are bigger with swollen cheeks. During breeding season, the males develop an orange head and a black blotch over the cheeks and throat.

Agamidae.Name: Black-Bearded Flying Dragon
Agamidae.Description: Body very slender with small scales and long slender limbs. Topside of body olive or green with greyish brown bars or diamond-shaped blotches. Throat flap of males black and orange.

Agamidae.Name: Sumatran Flying Dragon
Agamidae.Description: Topside of body light brown with dark brown bloches and whitish mottling, patagium (membrane that helps the animal to glide) black with irregular brownish and greenish blotches. The male has a bluish head and a large yellow throat flap.

Cheloniidae.Name: Hawksbill Turtle
Cheloniidae.Description: Husk is oval and brown, overlapping scutes with sporadic yellow and orange speckles. Upper lip bulging ahead of lower lip.

Colubridae.Name: Bigeye Green Whip Snake
Colubridae.Description: Head is apparent from a slim body, nose is sharp. Lime green body, with a white underside with three green stripes.

Colubridae.Name: Oriental Whip Snake
Colubridae.Description: Head is apparent from a slim body, nose is sharp. Adults are bright fluorescent green topside, juveniles yellow to pale brown. Snout twice as long as width of the eye.

Colubridae.Name: Dog-Toothed Cat Snake
Colubridae.Description: Head is apparent from a slim body very slender and flat. Body yellowish or brown with sporadic black cross bars, some are nearly completely black. Head light brown with a black line behind the eye.

Colubridae.Name: Gold-ringed Cat Snake
Colubridae.Description: Body shiny black with a sequence of narrow bright yellow bands, distributed along the body. The local subspecies, has bands which do not meet over the back. Scales on the throat and across the lips bright yellow.

Colubridae.Name: White-spotted Cat Snake
Colubridae.Description: One is mainly green with pale green lines, the other is mainly brown with wide lines of orange and white. Juveniles may exhibit black smudges on top of the head.

Colubridae.Name: Variable Reed Snake
Colubridae.Description: Head is not apparent from the body, tail somewhat short and smooth. Body is dark brown, consistently with white or yellow line along the side. Underside with black and yellowish white bands. Young have a pink head and thin white streaks across the back and belly. Five upper labial scales

Colubridae.Name: Pink-headed Reed Snake
Colubridae.Description: Head is not apparent from body, tail is short and smooth. It has a bright pink head, topside of body and tail is black and white on the underside. Five upper labial scales.

Colubridae.Name: Paradise Gliding Snake
Colubridae.Description: Slim and circular body, head, with five yellow bands, is compressed and is apparent from the body. Body is black above with a green or yellow spot on each dorsal scale. Some have clusters of red spots to form a pattern down the middle of the back. The belly is yellowish-green.

Colubridae.Name: Common Malayan Racer
Colubridae.Description: Head is recognisable from the body, blackish brown with a sequence of black streaks on the sides beside the front of the body. A wide yellowish brown stripe along the middle of the back, enclosed by black streaks darkens as it approached the end. Two black streaks behind and below eye, and along the neck, lips, white streaks.

Colubridae.Name: Striped Bronzeback
Colubridae.Description: Black stripe on light background at the sides of the snake. Topside of body brown with six narrow black stripes from the neck to the tail, belly is greenish yellow with black stripe under the tail.

Colubridae.Name: Elegant Bronzeback
Colubridae.Description: Often confused with Blue Bronzeback. Body long and extremely slender. Topside of the body is bronze brown, a wide black streak across the snout, eye, and partly down the sides. Blue skin runs between the scales, along the sides, belly is yellowish green. Three thin, black lines are present along the tail, which is lacking in Blue Bronzeback.

Colubridae.Name: Kopstein's Bronzeback
Colubridae.Description: Body is bronze brown with the neck region bright orange-red. A black streak runs on the side of the head to the top part of the nape. Downside is yellowish green on the front half, then turns to dull green and brown on the tail.

Colubridae.Name: Painted Bronzeback
Colubridae.Description: Topside of the body is bronze, belly is yellowish or greenish, and a white streak down each side of the body. A black stripe runs from the start of the snake through the sides, above the white streak. When threatened, the scales of its neck and front of the body expands, exposing the blue skin under the scales.

Colubridae.Name: Malayan Bridle Snake
Colubridae.Description: Body is yellow-grey, with thick, regular brown bands on the top which do not continue to the bottom. A second form has alternating brown and yellow stripes. Scales on the belly are kneeled while the scales along the back are smooth.

Colubridae.Name: Keel-bellied Whip Snake
Colubridae.Description: Slender body is flattened sideways. Body is greyish or ruddy-brown, with black spots speckled along its back. Belly is beige with brown specks. Tongue is bright red and a wide brown streak runs behind the eyes.

Colubridae.Name: Red-tailed Racer
Colubridae.Description: Body is broad and flat, top of head is darker green, topside usually is bright green, underside paler. Tail is orange-red. Other less-common colour forms occur.

Colubridae.Name: House Wolf Snake
Colubridae.Description: Topside of head is dark brown, flat and has a thick yellowish band around the neck. The back of the body is purplish brown with various white specks. The belly is white.

Colubridae.Name: Banded Wolf Snake
Colubridae.Description: Topside of body is dark brown or black with white streaks across the front part, and darkens towards the tail.

Colubridae.Name: Striped Kukri Snake
Colubridae.Description: Head is not recognisable from large and smooth body. Topside is greyish brown with a red streak along the middle of the back, which is bounded by three black stripes on each side. Topmost two stripes joined at the top of the head, a black streak runs across the eyes and the belly is pink in colour.

Colubridae.Name: Barred Kukri Snake
Colubridae.Description: Topside of the body is dark-brown with red streaks of different shapes, the streaks will join to form a chevron pattern on the head. Underside is reddish-pink.

Colubridae.Name: Dwarf Reed Snake
Colubridae.Description: Body hardly recognisable from its body, nose is sharp and the tail is short. Topside of the body is in lustrous black and smooth. Some have a pale yellow collar with a pair of pale spots on the neck.

Colubridae.Name: Keeled Rat Snake
Colubridae.Description: Head is recognisable from slim and smooth body. Topside is brown blackish at the front sometimes with yellow streaks. Back of the body is yellowish brown with a specific web pattern, tail is black with yellow speckles. Sides of the head and neck is white.

Colubridae.Name: White-bellied Rat Snake
Colubridae.Description: Head is recognisable from slim and smooth body. Topside of the body is brown with a reddish brown stripe down the back towards the tail. A broad black line along the sides near the tail. Underside usually yellow or white.

Crocodylidae.Name: Estuarine Crocodile
Crocodylidae.Description: Snout long and relatively broad, tail muscular and compressed. Body yellow, olive or grey above with black checker-spots, and white below.

Dactyloidae.Name: Brown Anole
Dactyloidae.Description: Male colour differs from light grey to stark-black and have a dewlap that is orange-red. Females have dark-coloured triangular pattern along a white stripe which runs down the back.

Elapidae.Name: Banded Krait
Elapidae.Description: Head is somewhat recognisable from large and smooth body, body has triangular sub-sections. Topside on body is white or yellow with various black bands which runs until the belly, alternating with the white sections. Both head and tail are rounded.

Elapidae.Name: Blue Malayan Coral Snake
Elapidae.Description: A small head that is somewhat recognisable from a very slim body. Topside of body is dark navy blue with sky blue streak that runs by the sides, underside is red. Head and tail bright coral red.

Elapidae.Name: Banded Malayan Coral Snake
Elapidae.Description: Small head hardly recognisable from slim body. Topside of body is dark brown with a red streak down the middle. Belly is white with black rings, underside of tail is coloured red, with black streaks across.

Emydidae.Name: Red-eared Slider
Emydidae.Description: Husk is greenish brown with yellowish lines, bottom side of husk is yellow with black specks on each scute. Head green streaked with yellow, a wide bright red smudge behind the eye. Limbs and tail green with yellow lines. Adult males have claws at front limbs.

Gekkonidae.Name: Peters’s Bent-toed Gecko
Gekkonidae.Description: Black or brownish body above with narrow, irregular white bands across body and tail. Bands become dark-edged in adults. Symmetrical arrangement of pale or cream reticulations present on head.

Gekkonidae.Name: Singapore Bent-toed Gecko
Gekkonidae.Description: Body pinkish grey with black blotches down the back, tail blackish with pale bands. Pale yellow mottling on head.

Gekkonidae.Name: Frilly Gecko
Gekkonidae.Description: Distinctly mottled with brown and grey above, yellowish below. Colouration may be variable, very well camouflaged. Flattened tail and flaps of skin along the flanks.

Gekkonidae.Name: Peninsular Rock Gecko
Gekkonidae.Description: Snout long, broad and slightly upturned. Yellow above with dark brown and white blotches and streaks. Previously known as Kendall's Rock Gecko.

Gekkonidae.Name: Spotted House Gecko
Gekkonidae.Description: Body covered with warts, pale greyish-brown with seven to nine pairs of blackish blotches along the back, and a series of blackish bars on the tail.

Gekkonidae.Name: Four-clawed Gecko
