Gekkonidae.Description: Translucent pinkish brown with gold and blackish flecks. Tail smooth.

Gekkonidae.Name: Tokay
Gekkonidae.Description: Similar to Large Forest Gecko, discernible by size. Body blue-grey spotted with orange.

Gekkonidae.Name: Spiny-tailed House Gecko
Gekkonidae.Description: Highly variable species. Can be distinguished by the presence of whorls of small spines on original tail. Colour variable, but tends to be uniformed shade of brown or brown with darker markings.

Gekkonidae.Name: Flat-tailed Gecko
Gekkonidae.Description: Tail relatively flat. Colour variable, ranging from pale gret to gret with dark grey mottles and streaks.

Gekkonidae.Name: Lowland Dwarf Gecko
Gekkonidae.Description: Body very slender with short limbs. Body brown above with blackish markings over the back. Tail slender, pale brown or yellow with a yellowish blotch at the base.

Gekkonidae.Name: Mourning Gecko
Gekkonidae.Description: Body slender with ornate greyish-brown marbling. Pattern often presents in the form of chevrons on the back. Broad tail with a series of irregular black-edged yellowish bands on top.

Geoemydidae.Name: Malayan Box Terrapin
Geoemydidae.Description: Husk is rounded and black in coloured, bottom part of the husk is yellowish, with a pivot that allows the turtle to completely hide inside the husk. Topside of the head is black with a yellow streak across the eyes.

Geoemydidae.Name: Asian Leaf Terrapin
Geoemydidae.Description: Husk is oval shaped and coloured brown with five vertebral scutes, sides of the husk is jagged and slighly curved upwards. Head and nape dark brown with orange strokes.  Infants have greyish brown, compressed husk with thick black specks.

Geoemydidae.Name: Spiny Terrapin
Geoemydidae.Description: Rosy brown husk that is leveled at the top with jagged edges and a light brown backbone through the husk, with five vertebral scutes. Head, arms and legs are dark grey with reddsh speck on two sides of the head. Husks for young are leveled and heart-shaped with jagged edges. Young have the bottom side of the husk in intense yellow, streaked with black, and jagged borders.

Geoemydidae.Name: Black Marsh Terrapin
Geoemydidae.Description: Husk has smooth sides, black, while the bottom side of husk is black with brown stripes. Husk is rounded when seen from the side and jagged at the end, with five vertebral scutes. The head is black spotted white.

Homalopsidae.Name: Cantor's Water Snake
Homalopsidae.Description: Very slim body that is yellow with thick black or brown smudges. Some have back end of the body nearly totally black.

Homalopsidae.Name: Sunda Dog-faced Water Snake
Homalopsidae.Description: Wide head, topside of body is grey, brown or green. A dark line crosses the eyes and continues to the neck, eyes and nose are on the top of the head.

Homalopsidae.Name: Rainbow Water Snake
Homalopsidae.Description: Topside of body is brownish, a flat head and neck is greener than the other part of the body, with a pair of paler lines running through which meets at the head. Underside is light coloured with a thin brown line along the middle.

Homalopsidae.Name: Crab-eating Water Snake
Homalopsidae.Description: Head is blunt and not recognisable from the circular body, with a short tail. Topside is plurplish brown dimming to white to the underside.

Homalopsidae.Name: Yellow-lipped Water Snake
Homalopsidae.Description: Blunt head that is somewhat recognisable from the circular body, topside is grey and light brown underside with a black streak down the middle. Upper lips are yellow, which continues along the side of the body.

Homalopsidae.Name: Puff-faced Water Snake
Homalopsidae.Description: Wide head that is recognisable from thick and circular body. Topside is grey rigged with black and dark brown blotches across the body. Nose is black with a black streak cutting across the eyes, belly is white with tiny black smudges. The topside of a young is orange with black blotches.

Homalopsidae.Name: Blackwater Mud Snake
Homalopsidae.Description: Rich brown to greyish black colour patterned with thin, broken bright yellow bands on the side of the body. Bright yellow belly. Thin Yellow band between its eyes with numerous small yellow spots through body and tail.

Natricidae.Name: Spotted Keelback
Natricidae.Description: Head is recognisable from the body and scales are strongly kneeled. Topside is dark brown or grey, squared black smudges on the neck. A wide dark brown streak with black spots runs down the back, alternating with squared yellow speckles. Slightly red at the sides and yellow on the belly, rigged with black edges.

Natricidae.Name: Striped Keelback
Natricidae.Description: Head is recognisable from the body and scales are strongly kneeled. Topside is black with four yellowish brown streaks running through. Belly is white, segmented with wide black rings.

Pareatidae.Name: White-spotted Slug Snake
Pareatidae.Description: Head is recognisable from broad and compressed body. Topside is grey or brown with various white and black specks together, neck is bounded by a ring of reddish collar. Belly is white and spotted with black specks

Pythonidae.Name: Reticulated Python
Pythonidae.Description: Head is recognisable from broad and smooth body. Eyes are orange and topside is greyish brown with a web of sporadic lines, white belly. The sides are spotted white interchanging with black lines, a thin black line runs down the centre of the head, and another from eye towards the neck.

Scincidae.Name: Many-lined Sun Skink
Scincidae.Description: Body bronze-brown with possible arrays of thin black stripes along the back. Sides either blackish with white spots or wrap with orange from the ear to the back legs. Underside of the head yellow on some individuals.

Scincidae.Name: Striped Sun Skink
Scincidae.Description: Body brown or olive-green on top, usually with 5 to 7 yellowish stripes or series of spots, greenish-white below.

Scincidae.Name: Striped Tree Skink
Scincidae.Description: Body slim and draped in shiny smooth, overlapping flakes; symmetrical arrangement of large scales on top of the head with an outstretched snout. Body and head with a broad yellow stripe bounded by black stripes along the back; tail long and orange.

Scincidae.Name: Brown Tree Skink
Scincidae.Description: Strong body that is enclosed with glossy, rigged overlapping scales. Symmetrical scales patterned above the head. Body olive brown above with sporadic, thin black bands and white spots. Young are black and yellowish bands along the back, tail yellow with thin black bands.

Scincidae.Name: Mangrove Skink
Scincidae.Description: Slim body with smooth overlapping scales, symmetrical arrangement of large scales above the head. Greyish brown on the back, bluish with a blackish stripe along the sides. Tail and limbs are covered with whitish spots at the top. Orange bellies are seen in some.

Scincidae.Name: Garden Supple Skink
Scincidae.Description: Slim body wrapped in glossy, smooth and rigged overlapping scales. Arms and legs are tiny, tail is long and chunky. Body bronze-brown on the back enclosed by yellow stripes with bright yellow belly. Sides are black with white spots and a red smudge around the arms.

Scincidae.Name: Singapore Swamp Skink
Scincidae.Description: Upperside ground colour is dark brown, with faint pale markings extending in lines from the head to the base of the tail. Underside surface is beige. Juveniles are paler than adults and somewhat pinkish.

Trionychidae.Name: Asian Softshell Turtle
Trionychidae.Description: Husk is somewhat squarish, leathery, various spines can be spotted externally. Husk is greyish-brown with sporadic blackish bands. Various yellow specks on head and limbs, with some on the husk, belly is white. Nose is elongated, with a long neck and webbed feet with claws.

Typhlopidae.Name: Brahminy Blind Snake
Typhlopidae.Description: The body is totally dark brown to black. The rounded head, with tiny eyes, is not recognisable from the body with a short tail.

Varanidae.Name: Clouded Monitor
Varanidae.Description: Its has a slim and splitted tongue, small snout with nostrils midway between the eye and the tip of the snout. Greyish brown heavily spotted yellow.

Varanidae.Name: Malayan Water Monitor
Varanidae.Description: Adults are greyish brown, nostrils are ajacent to the tip of snout. Young are black with pale fronts, and bands made up of rows of yellow spots down their backs and tails.

Viperidae.Name: Shore Pit-viper
Viperidae.Description: Head is widely angled from the top and is recognisable from bulky body, bounded in kneeled scales. Body purplish-brown, bounded by thin white streaks at the sides. The young are rein with dark brown streaks.

Viperidae.Name: Wagler's Pit-viper
Viperidae.Description: Head widely angular from top view and is recognisable from the bulky body bounded in kneeled scales. Topside of adult females black spotted with green and yellow streaks, underside greenish white with yellow smudges. Young and adult males are green with white blotches or lines, red and white streak also runs down the side and has a red tail.

Xenopeltidae.Name: Iridescent Earth Snake
Xenopeltidae.Description: Compressed head is not recognisable from the body. Topside of body black to brown, belly is white. Tail recedes and short. Infants have a white band binding the nape.
